analysis.name: Andrew Selepak
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Good, well-explained, and engaging lectures. Pay attention and take good notes. Engaging but intimidating at times with attempts at humor. Weekly and tedious (but usually easy) homework assignments, which are graded by the TA. Exams were medium difficulty, and that was because the questions were a mix of easy and oddly specific questions.

Dr. Selepak's class is engaging, interesting, and enjoyable. Well-explained lectures. He likes to be funny, which sometimes works and sometimes doesn't. To do well, come to class and take notes (word for word) on the slides. Also do the readings for every week. Generate practice questions with AI, study with them, and you will get an A.

Professor Selepak was amazing! Hilarious, engaging, and entertaining. The class is graded mostly on exams with little work, with 6 total exams and just some in-class quizzes. Attendance isn't required, but heavily recommended since exams are based on lectures and he doesn't give out presentations.

I had Selepak for Media and Society and thought he was great and funny. Now in Social Media and Society, my view has changed. The smaller class means more interaction, but not in a good way—he shares unnecessary opinions, drags lectures, gives no PowerPoints, only two huge exams, and a long, time-consuming group project.

RTV3405. Dr. Selepak seems like a nice enough guy, but he tries to use humor to be relatable, and it does not always come across this way. It seems like he finds ways to integrate his personal beliefs into his lectures in a passive-aggressive way, causing the message to get lost. The topics are interesting, but his teaching style was not for me.

analysis.name: Ana Longo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 120 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Don't be scared off by the negative reviews following the 2021 spring exam 3. Dr. Longo had detailed lectures, lots of reading (as did the other three profs) and a difficult test but overall not too bad if you studied the learning objectives. Ppl retaliated bc they got a bad grade, doesn't reflect the prof. If u can't handle bio1, hope ur not STEM.

I think many reviews here are unfair to Dr. Longo as people posted them after being upset about the exam. I found the exam to be very fair and lecture-based. I watched lectures on 2x speed the day before, studied 5 days in advance, and did very well. Dr. Longo is available in office hours which I recommend if confused, and is overall a good person.

People are being very harsh to her as a direct result of the Spring 2021 exam. I thought her lectures were really interesting and her teaching style was easy to follow. That being said, the exam was poorly worded and when the TAs predicted a 10 point curve, we got nothing. She does not care about students' success, but hey, welcome to college.

I honestly enjoyed learning from Longo. Her lectures were to the point and I liked the small jokes and memes she included. However; her exam was oddly specific and the wording was confusing; it did not reflect what we had learned that well. If you study you should be fine, but if you don't pay attention to detail you won't do well with her.

There are many other reviews on this page that are not fair to Dr. Longo. Students flooded Rate My Professor after failing the exam, which is more a way for them to express their anger than honestly evaluating the professor. Dr. Longo taught evolution very well, there werent too many assignments or lectures, and it is totally feasible to get an A.

analysis.name: Andres Rubiano Acosta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst experience I've had. The professor is disrespectful in emails and the TAs never reply. Lectures consist of old YouTube videos that only cover the basics, but the exams are incredibly advanced and feel completely disconnected from the teaching material. It feels like being taught addition and then being tested on calculus.

DO NOT take this professor. It takes at least 10 hours of work a week to earn an A, and he requires that you record your screen for all assignments. He cares about his students and is very knowledgeable, but he has no grasp on how difficult the class is for those with no CAD experience. I would only recommend him If you have an easy semester ahead.

YOUR GRADE IS ONLY BASED ON EXAMS. There are pop quizzes that aren't graded, and they never show up on Canvas so you have to check every day. There is so much homework that don't count for anything as well. The exams are SO much harder than everything you do in class. The TAs NEVER respond. If you want an A, take another class. You've been warned.

Lots to say. pop quizzes, not graded, but you have to check daily. Being proficient at assignments will NOT be enough. Many weird or just negligent mishaps, ex. he dropped practices quizzes AFTER the exam alr happened. Could go on forever. TAs were pretty cool. Take this with another prof who cares or come back w/ 10+ years of knowledge :(.

DO NOT TAKE THIS. I had to drop it because I did so bad on the exams despite doing all the HW twice. The class that's built on YT videos (Less Boring Lectures), and the TAs are not it. The 4 exams are the only grades and are way harder than any HW, but you still have to do the HW/pop quizzes for no credit. Idk how this class is real

analysis.name: Soohyoun Ahn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 104 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Remember when learning used to be fun? Dr. Ahn actually makes it fun again. Can't believe I'm saying this, but I actually enjoyed doing the assignments in this class. Super engaging and easy to follow. Definitely recommend it for bio credit, international credit, or just a chill elective.

There is genuinely so much extra credit and opportunities to get an A in this course that you frankly need to be doing nothing to not. It can be a little tedious at times, but it is extremely easy -- and the many assignments can be done in 1-2 hrs.

Professor Ahn was super nice, took this course for credits and gpa boost, and it was super easy. Lectures are on PlayPosit and are super easy. The quizzes are easy, too. No exam, just some discussions and a digital project. I passed with an A, and I'm someone who gets distracted easily.

Super chill class; lectures are split into short videos; weekly quizzes are Honorlocked, but allowed to have a page of notes; 3 major assignments, but none take more than a day; most people end with over an 100 with all the extra credit there is

Man's Food was absolutely amazing online. General class about food- nutrition, food art, flavors, food groups etc. Each week: 10 min lecture, open note quiz, no exams, and one assignment (ex: eat at a restaurant and document the experience, make food art, make a personalized diet plan.) Final exam was a digital scrapbook.

analysis.name: Aditi Mukherjee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Take this class! So long as you show up once a week and do all her assignments that take about an hour a week to complete you're virtually guaranteed an A. The only thing you have to study for is the Excel certification exam which doesn't require a lot of studying. Dr. M herself is very enthusiastic about the course. Take this instead of CGS2531.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. Study early for the Excel Certification exam and attend every class. The in-class projects make up a big part of your grade. She's a good professor, but be on time for class because if you are more than 5 minutes late, she won't let you do the project. No extensions, so don't turn things in late.

Easiest critical tracking class you will ever take. Meets once a week for a project you do with a partner. If you're stuck she'll help you through it. No exams, only play posits and the excel certification/final exam. Definitely chose the excel certification its super easy. Please take this and not CGS trust me.

Most of the class is assignments with unlimited attempts and step by step instructions. Only somewhat difficult thing is the excel certification midterm but that's relatively easy too. Professor mostly just lets you learn through the online textbook and doesn't really teach herself, but its easy to get an A.

Easiest class you will take. Only one exam (on Excel). 90% of the grade is assignments ~2 hours max per week. Meets once per week for max of 1 hour and the Prof is as enthusiatic as you can get about Excel and Access.

analysis.name: Amanda Phalin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 112 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You miss one detail and you are done. She packs on tons of assignments with loads of criteria to follow to a T. As a full-time online student (w/ a full time job), I don't think she understands that just maneuvering around all her loads of crap is hard enough. She treats you like a slacker if you can't keep up with it all and it feels demeaning.

Professor Phalin teaches a completely useless course. The exams are almost entirely (80%) about memorizing obscure facts about a specific country. On top of that, she berates you with 4 assignments per week that are difficult to score well on. Overall, an out of touch professor. No one cares what the GDP growth rate is in 2020 for Canada...

Since the first day of class she's had an unsettling "Not My Problem" attitude towards her students. She's one of those people that's very 'rules-based' and unaccommodating. This class is a perfect example of UF trying to make pointless classes unnecessarily difficult. Her lectures are not worth your time, Smokin' Notes are the way to go.

extremely political. everything is liberal. exams also pull random information. it's not hard but her lectures are just not helpful and biased. just get the smokin notes, make your cheat sheet based on that, and open her class for the exams and no other purpose.

Professor Phalin is a great lecturer and makes class interesting despite content sometimes being boring. Definitely utilize the cheat sheet she allows you to have on the exam. I used smokin notes to help me figure out the most important information to put on it and it was a life saver!

analysis.name: Amanpreet Kapoor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Excellent professor. Lenient grader, very quick grader, the fastest ever. Literally a few times that I submitted a quiz/exam, I got a grade within 5-10 mins. The course is great, there are several learning resources that he offers; not only from the textbook. The exams & quizzes are easy. The programming assignments are tough though.

Best prof in the computer science department. Very clear on theory, great visualizations to help you follow along. Incredibly well prepared, organized class structure. Gamified lecture quizzes for extra credit. Responsive to questions. Open to feedback. Developed an arguably better version of leetcode for students. Actually the GOAT.

Both exams were HARD. ESPECIALLY THE FINAL. I got an A on both Prog 1/2. THIS IS NEXT LEVEL. The average grade on exams is a C/70 (sometimes lower/sometimes a lil higher). The average final course grade is probably around there as well. No wonder they call it the weed-out class. Good professor, though, and very fair.

The best professor I've ever had, and probably ever will have. He was an amazing lecturer, and was great about slowly walking through examples. He always answered questions thoroughly. He moved back deadlines for projects and his policies were so lax. The class was difficult, it's DSA so it SHOULD be. But nothing unmanageable. 10/10 experience!!

This professor is of the kindest professors I have ever had by far. This class is very hard and I was struggling a lot (hence my grade) and he went out of his way to help me pass the class when I reached out to him. He knows how to accommodate students in a way that ensures fairness to everyone but is also gracious to those who are struggling.

analysis.name: Alex Angerhofer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is by far my hardest class this semester primarily because it is SO time-consuming. His slides don't make much sense so you really have to teach yourself and there aren't any resources for it like Study Edge or Smokin Notes. The exam averages on Canvas are C-/D+ 's and you pretty much have no idea what'll be on them. Drop it while you can!

This class is tailor-made specifically for people who were born to pursue chemistry as a lifestyle. Don't let the "general", or "chemistry 1 & 2" fool you, this class is all about advanced topics in chemistry with a lovely mix of physics. I read the bad reviews before taking this class and honestly thought that it couldn't be THAT bad, but it is.

This is the worst class I have ever taken, I ended up having to drop it. Homework is almost impossible, he makes everything so much more complicated than it really is. He focuses on physics more than anything and if you have never had a physics class before you will be lost most of the time. Tests are not multiple choice, long, and really confusing

Don't take this class unless you love chemistry more than you love your family. It is incredible hard and you need a solid background in physics to succeed. If you think you're smart, think again. I had a 4.0 GPA in highschool and graduated in the top 1% of my class and I barely got a C in this class.  Also, the homework is insanely hard.

Dr. A is obviously an expert in his field of chemistry and sometimes overestimates your understanding of chemistry as an entering freshman in CHM2047, but after the stress of doing homework and studying for exams, you'll be in awe of how much you know about chemistry, especially for organic chemistry. Study groups and office hours ensure success.

analysis.name: Ashok Kumar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Kumar is one of the most insufferable people I have ever had the displeasure of knowing, he doesn't care for or about his students, his lectures all feel like he doesn't want to be there, his TA's grade unnecessarily harshly. The material for this class is relatively easy and passable with minimal effort but having to be around Kumar ruins it
Kumar will teach you not only how to construct the shaft but how to lay it the right way as well.

A very, very straightforward professor, follow what he says during lectures or watch the recordings and you'll be fine. He explains everything youll need for the CSWA and a section of that class is a prep period. There is a final that's worth like 5 percent of your grade, but the real final is the final design project which I really enjoyed.

Not a bad option if you can't get Crane. If you go to class you wont have any problems getting a good grade in the class. The assignments are locked by a code but you just need to know someone who went to get it from them and just watch the lecture videos he posts. Passing the CSWA exam isn't hard, and assignments are doable.

Really enjoyed the final design project, especially considering some of the other profs just have a written final (which for a CAD class is lowk silly). Passed the CSWA with ease by following his recommendations. He gives you everything you need to succeed in the class.
Is he the most enthusiastic prof? No, but he's a pretty good one.

analysis.name: Alin Dobra
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Semester is 1 group project that you have to teach yourself through Googling and SO. Dobra does this as a side hustle and prefers lecturing about incoherent nonsense and personal stories over teaching anything related to the required coding. What you learn from him is general industry advice based on common sense but he thinks he's Einstein for it.

He knows nothing about the material and is the laziest "professor" I've ever encountered. The difficulty is balanced out by his extremely vague assignment specifications making it hard to deduct points. Never take a class with this guy. There is no value in his teaching. He just throws around buzzwords and waves his hands during lectures.
Always willing to share his knowledge. Amazing lectures with lots of interesting examples. Projects will help a lot in learning.

Professor Dobra is probably my favorite professor I've ever had. He is clearly far more concerned with students learning than testing and grades. No tests or quizzes, just comprehensive projects and impressively engaging lectures. This goes for both COP5556 and CEN5035.

DOS is a hard class. It's not hard to get an A in because Dobra doesn't care TOO much about if your implementation is correct, rather if you create something worth while. The project specs are fairly ambiguous but that is by design to give you some freedom. Definitely be prepared to spend a lot of time on this class.

analysis.name: Seema Bandyopadhyay
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Homework and quizzes are relatively easy, and the exams are related to the lectures and assignments. However, the exams are significantly more difficult, which makes preparation challenging. The final exam seating was also arranged based on midterm rankings, which felt unnecessary and created extra pressure. Not respecting students' privacy.
Her classes are good, but her respect for students is close to nil. Hope she understands.

If you have a CS background, you'll fly through this course. Easier than AP Comp Sci. Otherwise, seconding the other guy. Good luck! She goes on and on a lot and it's easy to doze off because of it. Not very engaging but if you have questions and don't understand, you need to ask. Do the practice, code your assignments, you'll be fine.

Only graded on the midterm, final, and ZyBooks assignments. She walks through how the compiler runs code on board to help you understand what's going on, so her lectures can feel a bit slow. YMMV with her teaching style but I liked it. Her lectures were clear and helped me understand the basics. Do the practice quizzes. Overall, pretty easy class.

This class was extremely hard. It seems like you are moving backwards from the first mod. Then on the exams there are answer choices a,b,c,d,e,f,g making it nearly impossible to use process of elimination. If you take the class learn it her way even if that is not how you normally could learn, thats the only way you'll be able to pass.

analysis.name: Brian Cahill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 166 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cahill wants you to succeed, but he's not really going to hand out A's like candy. He can come of as callous, but I think that he's just more into tough love than into coddling his students. He's willing to work with you and is very easy to approach, will make an effort to help people who are failing if it's a big problem.

Amazing. I love him. he is so passionate & makes you feel like you matter as a person. He offers help outside of class, and despite all of the extra credit opportunities I still MAY NOT pass the class. Hardest class of my life, no doubt. Incredibly difficult tests. As a person, Dr. Cahill rocks and I look forward to another easier class with him.

Very hard exams and quizzes, which make up almost your whole grade. Gives study guides but they're not any help for exams. Grades harshly and you don't get the opportunity to see what questions you missed on assignments. Class is extremely hard, take it with a different professor if you can. Would not recommend any of his classes.

Genuinely the weirdest prof. I've known. 

Assessments are assigned over holidays, refusal to accept verified medical notes. 

For such an easy class, he is very demeaning. He presents himself as relatable and "cool" at the beginning of the semester, this is a facade.

For the sake of your mental, find an alternative professor.
Great class that opened me up to a new area of psychology. Really knowledgeable, fun lectures, and interesting class. Easy A!

analysis.name: Eben Broadbent
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Eben is a entertaining and fun professor that cares about his students. If you show up to class, you won't have many problems passing. Attendance is what will affect your grade the most. The labs were also interesting and he chooses the right topics to cover while we're in the field. Great prof.

Somewhat spacey; very pleasant. Interested in student enjoyment, and tries his best to learn about everyone. Material can be complicated but assignments are easy. Lots of low stakes group work. Explanatory lab tangents can be confusing. Pack snacks and water for the field!

Great class, lots of field work work, seems to be still getting it organized but would highly recommend if you want an adventure. Lots of group work, not a lecture style but that is fine if you prepare in advance.

This has to be the best professor I've had at UF, if you are slightly interested in forestry, take this class! Eden is a wonderful teacher, and the best part about this class is going out into the forest and learning without worrying about being tested on hard tree biology. I wish he taught all my classes because I would learn so much easier.

Dr. Broadbent is one of the best professors at UF. He is a very kind and down-to-earth professor who is willing to work with you every step of the way, genuinely loves his students, and is excited to teach about these topics. He brings enthusiasm and interest to every class, and attending his classes was something I always looked forward to.

analysis.name: Brian Harfe
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Be prepared to do a lot of reading; there are 2 required books as well as required online articles for each module and while it's not at all unmanageable, be prepared to set aside some time. Every assignment is pretty heavily weighted so don't miss anything. All in all good prof, just keep on top of the readings and you'll be fine.

Not that bad for a quest 2. Most of the time, it takes 20 minutes per week, although the last few weeks take a little bit longer. As long as you get a good TA, you should pretty easily get an A. You can use ChatGPT for all the quizzes and don't actually need to read the books or watch the movies. Also, you don't need to watch the lectures.

Pretty easy course. Make sure you do the assignments ahead of time bc you may need to buy stuff for the small experiments. There's a group project towards the end so just make sure to be on top of that
Professor Harfe was amazing. He aided all his students when they needed help. He was thorough when teaching and answered everyone's questions. 10/10 would recommend

I took this for my Quest 2 class, which is rather easy.  Easy writing assignments, yet the assignments are still fun.  All you have to do is the assignments, and you should be good.  Lectures are about 1.5-2 hours each week, but the professor is engaging and fun to watch, so it flies by.

analysis.name: Colleen Beucher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you need a Quest 1 TAKE artisiric revelation! Dr. B is so sweet and understanding for any problem ypu could have. Her lectures are group discussions. The class is super easy if you just show up. There are around 1-2 short HWs a week based on lectures. There are NO EXAMS and you are graded from a group project and 2 short papers. Dr.B = BEST EVER

I took this class for a Quest 1 credit, and she's nice. But attendance is mandatory and they take off a lot of points. Every class is basically a discussion, on the three 20-page readings we needed to read the night before. I like music so I thought I would enjoy this class more, its just that for 3 times a week it gets annoying. HWs are super easy

I love and highly recommend Professor Beucher. While daily readings was excessive for a quest course, skimming the text was sufficient to partake in discussion, which is most of your grade. She cares for each student and is very passionate. There's two papers and one group presentation, but you are encouraged to pick topics you're interested in.

I took her Quest 1, and the lectures themselves are boring if you are not really interested in music, but her attitude makes up for it. She is very understanding, nice, and the TA is very lenient with grading. The classes are basically just discussions, and the homeworks are short and simple.

Loved Dr. B! There were a lot of readings to do basically every night, but the class was very discussion-based so as long as you knew the general concepts, you'd be fine. She's very sweet, understanding, and very accessible outside of class! You can tell that she really enjoys hearing everyone's thoughts! I'm glad I took this class!

analysis.name: Samantha Banal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Whimsical, and amazing. Would take again, you should too!

She was awesome! I knew NOTHING about literature walking in and she taught it so well. As long as you read what she assigns, do the few assignments she gives, and PARTICIPATE, you will pass! She is great and definitely makes you think. Her lectures are very entertaining and she tries to include all. Very thought evoking. 10/10 would recommend!

Ms Banal was very helpful. The class was engaging because of her passion towards English. She's very enthusiastic and willing to help you if you have problems with any of the papers/ essays that she assigns. I've learned a lot!
Ms. Banal is awesome! She made me want to go to class. She is nice and a fair grader. Her love for literature is inspirational...And she's nice to look at ;)
She really cares about her students and her lectures are really engaging. Getting an A takes some work, the class average is probably around a B.

analysis.name: Jonathan Brooks
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 69 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Brooks is compassionate, personable, and very knowledgeable. He was not once stumped by a question asked in class. He is a solid lecturer and usually had a few "when are we going to actually use this" examples. He makes a notoriously dry subject relevant and as interesting as it can be. Great guy, great teacher. Take him for numerical!

He's a really good teacher who cares a lot about his classes. He gives hard homework but he gives so much time to help his students understand it. His exams aren't bad if you pay attention to his lecture and he gives a lot of hints about it. The topic is kind of dry but its not really his fault. If you put in the effort you'll get an A.

His lectures are very enjoyable if you pay attention and really try to understand the material. The class requires a little more MATLAB than students are taught in COP2271, but the homework is doable, and sometimes enjoyable if you have a good understanding of the concepts being taught. Exams are mostly conceptual.

Dr. Brooks is the best professor I have had at UF! He puts lots of effort into making class as engaging as he can and making himself available to students outside of the classroom with lots of office hours. Go to office hours. He gives plenty of time to complete homework assignments, but they can be overwhelming if you wait too long.

Brooks was probably THE BEST professor I have had at UF so far! His lectures were not only helpful in learning the material but he's an inspirational man who taught us many things about whats to come in life. Numerical methods is hard, the homework takes a lot of time, and the exams are manageable if you study! Take Brooks if you got the chance!

analysis.name: Stephanie Bogart
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I'm currently taking this class and it's being treated more as a writing class than a Quest class. Both the professor and TA are hard graders, every assignment I've submitted has had numerous comments on it, and I've very rarely gotten a 100% on anything. It's taken way too seriously for what it is. Just take a different class.

Dr. Bogart is one of my favorite professors at UF thus far. You can tell that she truly cares! Attendance is not mandatory, but she gives extra credit if you go. The exams are also a little tricky, but if you do your readings and take notes in lectures, there's no reason why you wouldn't get an A/B.

RUN!! I picked this course because I thought the course material was going to be interesting enough to warrant the hard work I was warned about. NO! Class is not interesting, and coursework is very extensive. Don't do what I did and ignore the reviews.

Exams were easy and open note. The lectures weren't really interesting. The writing assignments were quite doable. Just make sure to start on the last 3000-word final paper a week before it's due. The discussions were fun and you didn't have to prepare a lot for them.

I took this without the WR, so I can't speak on that. The lectures were engaging and she knows what she's talking about - I came to respect her a lot. The tests are ridiculously easy, and I barely remember the homework, so insignificant. The TA section was also a lot of fun, but my TA was a hilarious grad student who barely cared, so that helped.

analysis.name: Christina Boucher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst teachers Ive ever had the misfortune of having. Reads slides like an audiobook. Tests cover two or more chapters every two weeks. Lets us assume that everything will be on the test when half isnt. Cant trust what she says is important to know. Furthermore, shes unaccommodating to students and doesnt try to pretend to care.

She doesn't seem prepared for lectures at all and makes up confusing explanations on the spot. She also complained that there were too many people in the class so she made the entire grade based on 4 tests, which were largely unrelated to what we supposedly learned in lectures.

Even though the class is super interesting for math nerds, she just butchered it. She basically reads from the slides and that is it. Honestly, she does not seem to be prepared to give lectures at all. Exams are not the worst. However, you should review her slides.

She just reads off the slides. She had her TA teach the class more than 8 times throughout the semester because she was absent. Tests are very difficult as they are all free response and no specifics are given on what they will be about.

One of the exams covered 4 chapters - a total of 184 slides from the PowerPoints. Two of these chapters discussed matrices and how they apply to sets and graphs. The homework contained many problems about matrices. On the test, not a single problem about matrices. Yet, we were tested on a theorem that was only discussed on 1 slide with no examples.

analysis.name: David Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class thinking I wouldn't gain that much from it, but I was wrong. His lectures are very engaging and will keep you interested, whether you like plants or not. This class is extremely easy, but you need to study for the quizzes They are pretty specific and may include things that he only covered in lecture. Do the extra credit. Easy A.

Who doesn't want a plant every time they go to class?!? Prof Clark is basically a comedian and is passionate about his work with plants. The notes are essential to passing his quizzes and final, but you can take pictures of the powerpoints. Just make sure to know the material for the quizzes and final, or you wont pass.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. The professor himself was very nice, but the quizzes are hard even if you pay attention and study. It's a 1-credit class that I took for fun, but I ended up dropping it after taking two quizzes because I was failing. There is so much information in the lectures, and if you don't write down every word he says...good luck.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Overall, the professor was nice. There are only 4 quizzes, and they are very difficult and do not follow the lecture at all. I took it for fun, but ended up dropping it after 2 quizzes because they were so hard no matter how much I studied. He will put random information on there that he never said in the lectures.

Dave is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, BUT the quizzes (4 x 100 points throughout the semester) are very difficult if you have little prior knowledge. They are on small details from the notes, and lots of what he says (so it's hard to skip lecutres). Lots of EC too (like growing plants)

analysis.name: John Banko
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 362 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Probably the worst class/professor of your college career. You'll be taught how to do the work in Excel, but you can't use Excel on the exams. Why? Well, in his own words, he's "evil." His advice is to run up and down the stadium stairs then take practice exams. Very practical. I felt confident based on lectures and practice problems, failed exams.

This guy is ridiculous. Flat out refuses to discuss exam grading or what questions may have been missed, even though he reserves right to test on those types of questions again. Honestly, doesn't care about you learning or not, just that he went through the motions. If majority of students are failing a test, is that not on the teacher?

If you could have taken this class a year ago with Tapley and didn't, kick yourself, because you just made the biggest mistake of your college career. Lack of a formula sheet for 50-100 formulas, no more charts that used to be given. Unnecessarily horrible for fairly reasonable material. The free response will destroy your will to live.

Banko is the worst instructor ever and his class is just awful. I am a straight-A student, 4.0 GPA, working on honors thesis. I worked VERY HARD in this class, paid for tutoring, and sacrificed a lot of time studying, but my best was not good enough. I still ended up with a C. I am not a finance major, but good luck to those who need an A or B.

What a horrible teacher.  Took it over Summer C and was a total waste of time and money.  He doesn't teach - he talks at you.  Test questions are many times harder than examples in the book, don't even try. My favorite saying was, we have too many finance majors so anyone who would normally get an A will get a C.   FABULOUS

analysis.name: Laura Cruz Castro
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved her class! She cares a lot and it shows. Her tests were not the best, they were hard and there was A LOT for relatively little time. Projects were better. She gives you a lot of time, explains the necessary things, and is flexible with deadlines when a lot of students are struggling. Very understanding and caring, skilled teacher.

This class wasn't the easiest but also wasn't the hardest. If you already know python/coding then itll be a breeze but if you're completely new it's kind of tricky if you're taking it with other hard classes. Assignments arent too bad, Labs are kind of time consuming,+theres usually a 2-q quiz weekly. Projects are DEVIOUS. Exams are ok but get you

She is so chill, if you can take this class with her, do it. Avoid the in person sections of Python with the other profs, heard they are much harder. Everything is open note and there's extra credit on almost anything. Super responsive outside of class and clear on grading. The homeworks can take a little while, but besides that easy A class.

Amazing professor. I was taking the in-person Python coding section and struggling, but her online section is very slow-paced and thorough, so I felt like it was much easier to understand the language. Very helpful and kind, responds fast to emails/discord and always on the side of the student/helping the student. Exams and projects are open note.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about her students then look no further. I have no doubt in my mind that Professor Cruz wants what is best for her students and is patient, kind, and will work things through with you. Having a Professor like her is a rare and incredible experience that I highly recommend you take.

analysis.name: Carol Demas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 118 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There is 5 points of extra credit built into the exams plus 5% extra credit you can get from doing practice exams on canvas for each exam. She is very kind and you can tell she's passionate about math. I like that she includes some history of the math we do/fun facts. As long as you keep up with lectures/homework, it is an easy A.

The homework given will be your main way of solidifying skills needed for the test. Her lectures are good at covering material, but the pace of the course only allows for minimum examples in lectures. Some of her explanations would assume you remember and understand old formulas immediately, making it hard to follow.

The course content could be valuable, but the teaching and support did not meet my expectations. Instructions and grading expectations were not always communicated clearly, and when I reached out for help, my questions often felt dismissed rather than addressed. The classroom and office-hour interactions did not feel consistently welcoming

Dr. Demas is a wonderful professor! She explains the material clearly and makes the math as approachable as it can be. She may come off a bit cold at times, but it's really not hard to get on her good side; just don't skip every exam. I cannot recommend her enough. She's the go-to professor for Elementary Differential Equations and for good reason.

Stay on top of the homework, I know it's alot. It is great preparation for the exams. Makes sure to do the past exams. It's very doable to get an A in this class, especially with the extra credit. The final exam was probably the most difficult but I did well on the first 3 so I didn't have to learn too much of the new stuff. Great professor.

analysis.name: Dave Carlson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do not think this is an easy online class to throw into your schedule. I, and others I know, have ended up spending an insane amount of time working on this class to little avail. The lack of grade diversity makes smaller mistakes have a titanic impact on the overall grade, if you're planning on taking this, please reconsider.

please NEVER take this professor if you care about your GPA or passing classes. this man is so rude and unhelpful toward his students. the exams were based on the most
random details ever. i would spend days studying and highest grade i got was an 87.don't even get me STARTED on the timeline project. he has way too high of standards for an elective

This has been the greatest class I've taken in four years. If you have any interest in rock n roll music, TAKE THIS CLASS. He plays music and videos during class, and even dances along. He knows what he's talking about, and loves the subject. He doesn't post his notes online, so you have to go to class, but I love it so much I don't even mind.

Prof. Rock was amazing. If you like rock 'n' roll you'll love this class! No busy work but lots of lectures on which the exams are based. This was my favorite class I've ever taken because of his lectures and passion for the subject. Grades are only based on 4 exams and 1 project at the end of the semester which could hurt some students.

Do not take this class if you want to lower your GPA. I took this class because I have a genuine love for music... did very poorly on exams. Very detail oriented and he provides a study guide with over 80 terms on it and asks for little details. Not worth taking.

analysis.name: Carolyn Kelley
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 107 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely phenomenal lecturer. You analyze media from books to films to art (The Great Gatsby to Pulp Fiction), and discussed everything from gender to mythological allusions. She's open-minded to other interpretations as long as you can support them. NOT a throwaway class, the writing advice is legitimately helpful. Need Quest? Take this.

Dr K is one of the most caring, authentic, and lovable professors I've ever had. She's really the kind of prof you would take a class for just bc she's teaching it. She inspired me (as a math major) to major in women's studies as well. The topics covered in class are so interesting and really make you think critically about the media around you

loved her. the material is pretty interesting and she clearly loves teaching it. grade is made up of 3 papers and 2 exams, but she is very available and excited to help and give feedback as you go. also very kind & understanding; i have a heart condition that made me miss multiple lectures and i wasn't penalized despite not having doctor's notes.

She's a great person and teacher because she's super knowledgeable, but she does assign a lot of readings and sometimes talks really fast. If you're looking for a class that doesn't require much effort at home or after class, I wouldn't recommend it. I enjoyed my time in this class, but this class was the most work I had in the semester.

Professor Kelley is one of the most personable and kind professors I have had at UF so far. She cares so much about the course, as well as the well being of every student in the class, making it very enjoyable to be present. This class is very interesting and engaging and I seriously think about the stuff she taught us on the daily.

analysis.name: Karina Cadena
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were slow and hard to stay engaged with. The class is very formula-based, so if you understand the equations, exams are easy. I found lecture explanations of formulas extremely confusing and not helpful. I mostly relied on slides and taught myself the material. Be prepared to self-study, since I found it hard to learn in lecture.

My intention here is not to be mean, but honest: Prof. Cadena is a very nice person, but she is not the greatest instructor. Her class was very hard to follow, the quizzes often had nothing to do with the exams, and I basically ended up teaching myself the entire material of the class. Old exams were helpful, but I would not take her class again.

The class is graded on 3 exams worth 75% and 10 quizzes worth 25%. Be prepared to study. I did not do well on my second exam because I skipped lecture and did not study so do not do that. Class is in person but she does zoom lectures. Quizzes and exams are difficult but fair and manageable. She posts old exams to review which are VERY helpful.

Good lecturer, very receptive to questions/comments. She also holds a zoom which is convenient if you can't make it. To study for the exams, just do the old ones (which she gives you so many of). There are online quizzes, which help make you stay up-to-date with the material, and they are multiple attempts so it's chill if you mess up at first.

This professor was rude to me in front of the entire lecture hall. She may have had good intentions, but she didn't have the decency to think through what she was doing. Because the class also had online lectures, I attended those instead. Although I didn't do as well as I hoped, I still ended the semester with a relatively high grade.

analysis.name: Kwai-Lee Chui
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 299 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dont miss classes, study through the now you trys and the exam reviews, and you wont have to use study edge.
I have few words for Dr. Chui's class. It is perfection. Don't even think about taking this class if you don't have Chui. Chui is love, Chui is life.

She is the best teacher I have had in my life!! Her lecture is very clear and straightforward. She care all her students and want to see everyone succeed in the course. She puts so much of her efforts to her students and tries to remember everyone, even though, the class is huge. I love her and want to have her for all my Math classes.

This class is a typical math course at UF but Professor Chui was amazing. She was always very engaged in class and would make sure to answer anyone and everyone's questions to the best of her ability. She also makes it easy to remember concepts in class with funny/goofy references to concepts so that the content is more digestible.

This was a retake for me, and I think Chui was fine compared to other professors. She can be monotone and not very engaging at times, but if you do stay engaged, she's good! But compared to in person, her online section was far tougher. No partial credit, and the exams were much harder. Don't take it with other hard classes. Take her in person!

analysis.name: Daniel O'Neill
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: O'Neill is absolutely fantastic. He is knowledgeable, a great lecturer, and clearly passionate about the subject. That being said, he makes it exceedingly clear that if you do not do the readings, you will not get an A. However, the readings are the only thing expected from you and he breaks them down wonderfully in lecture. Highly recommend!

O'Neill is an amazing lecturer! He's funny, well-articulated, and passionate. His choice of readings was great, and the structure of his lectures was easy to follow. At office hours he's super kind and interesting to speak with. I definitely recommend this course with him. The workload is reasonable and worth it.

The GOAT!!! O'Neill is one of the best professors at UF. You will def need to work for your A (do ALL the readings, take good lecture notes, and use your office hours!), but O'Neill's iconic lectures and clear passion for political theory will also def inspire the same in you. Material is difficult, but not a harsh grader. Remember - details!

Professor O'Neill was an extremely animated and passionate professor who I highly recommend any Poli Sci freshman take Political Theory with. My TA was really informative (although very political) and grading is fair. Sometimes he can go on tangents which are ultimately more confusing than helpful but he was easy to talk to during office hours.

Dr. O'Neill is an amazing lecturer and I highly recommend you take him for an intro level class. His lectures are extremely engaging and although attendance is not mandatory, I recommend going. I don't think its necessary to purchase the textbook to succeed as his lectures pretty much cover all the material you need to know for his exams.

analysis.name: Peter Dobbins
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 253 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This class is poorly structured and extremely hard to access without previous programming experience. Lectures are meandering and taught to the students as if we already understand the material. The textbook isn't referenced so it is incredibly difficult to find resources to learn from, and the grading fell far behind.

Professor Dobbins does not explain things in a clear way. Very minimal access to course materials. For example, were given problems to practice for our quizzes yet were never given the solutions to those problems so you have to try your best and just hope you did it right. The most disorganized class I have ever taken, would not recommend him.

I am so lost in this class right now that I do not even know the right questions to ask! I took this class last semester & that Prof started small & built his way up. I feel as if this Prof is on shuffle skipping around complex topics before he's even explained the basics of Java. Def not a good class for someone with barely any coding experience

I know it's only been two weeks, but this class has been a nightmare. His lectures are extremely confusing and he doesn't teach from the book or provide any notes or resources, making it challenging to teach myself. He goes off on weird analogies about Arctic ecology and convoluted tangents that eventually muddy any point he was trying to make.
This has been the worse class I have taken at UF. The class is so unorganized and unclear that it is hard to learn anything when you do not even know what they are asking you to do.

analysis.name: Joel Davis
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor is such a sweetheart, you can tell he cares about his students. His lectures are amazing, they feel like a podcast. The midterm was mostly common sense (I studied for 4 hours and got a 100), and the final was fair if you study (I studied for 3 days and got an 85).

The class itself isn't bad. The issue was he has very unclear expectations on what you need to know/don't need to know. Sometimes feels l like he thinks he's made points clear...but just hasn't. Beware that you need to prepare for the midterm and the final unless you have a coding background. Sweet but bad at replying to emails with questions.

Best professor I have ever had! He actually cares about his students. Had 2 hurricanes this semester and he was the only one who jumped through hoops to accommodate students without making you feel bad. His lectures are 10/10!! I was scared for this class but you don't really have to memorize any code, you just have to understand concepts.

He is really good. The class is easy, and is a great option for the summer if you are doing an internship. My only small complaint is that he was kind of disorganized over what assignments he was going to cancel or have us do and would sometimes go weeks without communicating with us. I think this was kind of the last thing on his mind in summer.

Dr. Davis is great and as a lot of other students said his lectures are enjoyable and have a podcast feel. I took this for my AI Fundamentals elective and could not recommend it more! First half of the course is coding, second half concepts. The course is very manageable so long as you put in the effort.

analysis.name: Ellen Davis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Fantastic 4-hour field trips - generally weekly - with 2 intermittent key exercises. 3 cumulative field quizzes that demand live botanical ID skills. Exceedingly fun class if you enjoy socializing and the outdoors — countless wonderful memories to be had. Dr. Davis knows a scary amount about plants. Remember to bring snacks and water!

Her plants unit is known to be the hardest out of the 3. However, her slides have everything you need to do well on the exam. She explains the concepts well, but it is a lot of information to digest so you will need to study to score high. While she posts the slides, attendance is technically required and you will learn a lot more by attending them

I thought she was good teacher, I found her easy to follow along and study for but there was a cheating incident in my test room and she had us all retake the exam and I truly belive it was harder and included questions from topics we were not told to study and blamed those of us who did nothing wrong. She also is not clear when asking questions.
there was a cheating situation and she punished the students that didn't do anything.

Didn't read the textbook nor did I pay attention to any of the lectures. Although from what I heard in the background she seemed good. I only used smoking notes and just read it a bunch before the exam and was able to succeed.

analysis.name: Dustin Hall
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It's difficult to get a feel for profs online but prof hall seemed really nice; he even gave us extra credit for making PB&Js lol. This course is heavily dependent on 3 major speeches, if you screw around and don't do any one of them I don't think it's possible to pass the class; that said you're given more than enough time and resources to do well

You will read about six novels in this class, and a couple of the novels are quite explicit/graphic (a lot of sexual lesbian/transgender scenes). There is a lot of reading—around a novel every week or two—so it'll take up a lot of your free time. The professor allows and encourages the use of AI. Only take this class if you really enjoy reading.

IDS2935: This class is extremely easy if you read the novels, but if you do not have time to read 7 novels within the span of a semester (relatively quickly), do not take the class. There are a few grades, a final paper, and a collab assignment. He is a very kind and fun professor, but definitely uses AI to grade things (if you care about that).

Professor Hall was absolutely hilarious and made this class enjoyable. His grading criteria is very clear and I found it extremely useful how he gives extensive feedback on your speeches letting you know where you "glow" and where you could "grow". If you have to take this class, I 100% recommend you take it with Professor Dustin Hall!!

This class was very discussion heavy, so there weren't too many assignments outside of class. Dr. Hall was passionate about the material and helped encourage conversations among students. Lots of reading but most of the books were quick reads so it never seemed overwhelming, Would recommend.

analysis.name: Eva Garcia Ferres
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: worst class I've taken as a psych major. The two-hour coding lectures are unbearable, TAs are overly nitpicky, and points are taken off for minor issues. assignments are harshly graded, and the vague and the rubric always changes which makes even a B feel unattainable. Get a God to get through this class because you will need it. insufferable

this class is so stressful and confusing. nearly impossible to pass and points are taken off for the most petty things. dont take this class if you are aiming for an A. TA and professor will say two completely different things about what to do for an assignment and you will get lots of points off for no reason. beware!!

There is a fine line between teaching and torture. This class walks that line. If you enjoy sleepless nights, flowing tears, and brutal grading, this class is for you. If not, find a different instructor.
Take this with another professor, it will be easier. Most of the class is spent learning how to code on R with little help, which other professors for this course won't do.
each assignment in this class was graded harshly by literally an undergrad, lectures were lackluster, and you can expect a two hour coding session every week

analysis.name: Mahtab Eskandar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This lecturer is available outside of class and trying to help but her lectures are unorganized & she doesn't know what she's talking about. I assume she has no programming background but was assigned to teach this class. She lets you ask questions but most of the time she need to use chatgpt to answer them.

Had her for ISM6251; Lectures were really hard to follow along with and I always felt lost during class. She's very kind and wants her students to do well, but the entire class was anxiety inducing cause I never knew what was happening. If you genuinely want to learn python, I would take the class with another professor. Go to class to get EC.

She tried to make lectures fun yet she seemed to have no knowledge of the materials AT ALL. She spent most of her lecture trying to make sense of her own slides. Questions are unanswered, exams are filled with typos. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!

I took her for CIS 6251. She is friendly, but the course felt disorganized and hard to follow. It's basic Python and curved, but I wouldn't recommend if you prefer clear structure and communication, especially around exams.
Lecture was vague and unorganized, questions unanswered and she seemed unprepared

analysis.name: Emily Hind
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had Dr. Hind for a Spanish Lit course I took while studying abroad in a six week program. She gave way too much work for the lack of time we had and it was very difficult to keep up. Her standards were too high to meet with the quantity of work given. Her quizzes had little to do with the topic of the class and I found her to be unreasonable

Do NOT take History and Politics of Caregiving. Awful class that provides no real world or invaluable information. A lot of readings that are 30-50 pages long and you spend more time doing work for this class than classes that are required for your major. Hind is enthusiastic and likes her course but it is extremely boring and useless.

Loved this class! It was a great class to take during freshman year since there's a lot of group discussion. Prof. Hind is passionate about what she teaches and makes each class interesting.
There's an assigned reading for each lecture/class. No tests but there's 4 major essays. You'll do fine if you go to her office hours and revise with her

Dr. Hind is a quirky lady and this makes class super engaging. Honestly if you just participate and show some interest in the topics brought up in class you are 100% getting an A. There is a lot of reading but realistically you don't have to do most of it if you have a general idea and say something during discussion.
She's a terrible teacher. The worst professor I ever had. Avoid her if you can.

analysis.name: Alice Emery
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Emery's class over the summer, and had a great time with her class. The subject is very interesting as a pre-law student because the disability law course content is really intriguing. Alice herself does not play much of a role in the class itself apart from grading, which she is very lenient on. Really laid back and low stakes.
This has to be one of the easiest classes at UF. The structure is great and the graders are not very harsh as long as you put a little bit of effort in.
My favorite professor I've had at UF so far; she is kind, knowledgeable about the topics, and clear with assignments. Everyone should have a professor like her!

All around great class. 3 two-page papers. This class will require 10 hours of community service. Very fun and very easy! I would suggest this class to anyone thinking about it.

Prof takes a while to grade, but the tradeoff is a super laid back class.
Super easy class, and really interesting! There are quizzes, but they are open note!

analysis.name: Evan Grillon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very nice guy and the class is very easy besides the major unit projects. He leaves kind comments, but he sometimes takes off points without explaining why. I never had issues with him not responding to emails, but I know some have. The only time I tried to come to online office hours, he came late and didn't speak to me. I recommend him though!
Easy assignments and very easy to manage, grades very delayed.

Dr. Grillon was not the toughest grader but often took off points for minor errors. Most importantly, Dr. Grillon took over 3 weeks to grade multiple major assignments and was slow to grade minor assignments along the way.

analysis.name: Faris Kronfli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took both EAB3002 and EAB3764 with Kronfli and both classes were easy. He explains the content in simple terms and wants students to actually learn and understand the class. EAB3002 was online and a bit more structured, but EAB3764 is super lax. Both classes are just assignments and quizzes. Great lectures and professor!

I would highly recommend this class for psych majors needing to fulfill their requirements. Dr. Kronfli is very easy to reach and willing to help answer any questions. There are no exams, just a discussion post, reading guide, quiz, and group project due every 2 weeks. Very manageable :)

I thought this class was a great experience. The guidelines are very clear and the workload is incredibly reasonable. The workload is not excessive and due bi-weekly. I felt like I learned so much and the assignments helped me retain what I learned. I would definitely recommend this class and teacher!

Very easy psychology class. You have to read the textbook to do the assignments and watch the lectures for the quizzes. The material is the same for both, and the quizzes are very straightforward. He's a good professor and makes the class as interesting as possible. The class was easy and enjoyable.

Very accessible through email and willing to explain any concept, question, or concern. I would recommend this class to anyone unless you hate reading a textbook because that is very necessary for this class. Other than that such a good online class and a very helpful professor!

analysis.name: Richard E. Romano
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Romano was an amazing professor and lecturer. Though his lectures tend to be long, he is very thorough and goes through multiple examples. If you go to class, do the assigned practice, and practice exam, you will do just fine in the class. He is very accessible outside of class and is willing to help. I recommend the class, it is interesting.

Prof. Romano is very enthusiastic and funny while teaching, which is helpful in making us entertained. He includes tons of examples and can explain things very well when asked. BUT, Romano mixes up his words and very often says incorrect information. Makes it very difficult to follow a lecture. Holds lecture for longer than he is supposed to.
Teaches a fair class, available for help outside of it, and extremely knowledgeable about economics - can't ask for much more from a college professor

Prof. Romano is the type of professor that holds long, straining lectures that cover the basics of what's to be learned. Then, would go over a practice exam that slightly emulates the notes but gives a good representation of the actual exam. The class is easy to pass, but Romano tends to get lost in his own head. Would not recommend this class.

Awesome class/teacher. Go to class. Tests come directly from the notes. I read the book to understand things better but review the notes for the exams. Don't dwell on the practice prob. b/c they won't come up but they do clarify the concepts. The test pract prob are important! do them b/c they can show up on exams. 3 tests. Good teacher.

analysis.name: Feihong Wang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: SUPER interesting course!!! Great professor. Pretty hard not to get an A on diaries and discussion if you just follow the rubric. Quizzes are pretty simple. Exams can be a little difficult tbh, so I recommend GOOD notes (exams are open notes and textbook). Great professor. Great course. Overall, an interesting course that's pretty easy. I love it!

Professor Wang was really fun to have and genuinely cared about the class she was teaching. My only issues with the class is that all grading is done by TAs and some of them are very strict with the prompts, and also the exams were open book, but all the exam content was indeed from the book with lectures being very minimal content wise.

The textbook used for this course is super information heavy and hard to take good notes on. The exams & quizzes are open note, but exams are not nearly as easy as the quizzes & the lectures don't really help unless they are directly asked about in the exams. Ctrl F is your friend for this class. Discussion posts & diary entries weren't hard either

She is very sweet and caring, you can tell she cares about her students and wants them to know there is always help from her or TAs. The class wasn't much work, just discussion posts and weekly quizzes. The only thing was the online exams, even though they are open textbook and notes, the questions were very niche/specific. Lock in for the project!

Listen, the class wasn't that difficult, but I literally only scraped by with an A which is insane considering it's psych. Her exams are more of a "find extremely niche information mentioned in one sentence in the textbook" rather than applying relevant knowledge. The lectures were barely relevant. It wasn't horrible, but I wouldn't take it again.

analysis.name: Fatma Gunay
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tests were so much harder and more advanced in her class than other Game Theory Classes. Really amazing professor but would often spend a massive amount of time doing the most complicated math equations, just to end it by saying the math doesn't matter, I'm looking for understanding of the intuition, but then make hard exams on correctly doing math

Wasn't sure about her at first bc how quickly she moves, but I can say this woman cares about her students. She has humor and is so generous with her time. Everything is explained through her lectures and worksheets, however I was unsure of my exam material, and she let me sit in her office for HOURS doing problems and answering questions. Amazing!

Exam's are hard, concepts are confusing at the best of times. Really good professor but would proceed to do the most insane math and derivative functions, and then say math doesn't really matter, I care about the intuition, but then proceed to grade the exams on (80%) Math

Prof. Gunay is a smart and kind lady. Tries to be entertaining in what is generally a more boring and no-frills (but useful) class (don't think any negatives about class were her fault). Two exams and a final project, all relatively easy, plus graded (for accuracy) homework, which can be tricky sometimes. Considerate and helpful in office hours.

I loved Game Theory with professor Fatma Gunay, most teachers just go on and on with boring lectures where students want to fall asleep. Professor Gunay is different and adds jokes and stories throughout the lecture to keep students engaged and happy. She also is open to any questions and won't hesitate to stop if a student is confused.

analysis.name: Florin Curta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: VERY easy quest class. Super chill TA's, and lectures (objectively) don't feel and aren't mandatory to succeed. If you show up, note the key definitions and use them in your writings. No tests, quizzes, midterms or finals. only 4 assignments in the course and they are self-explanatory. He knows what he is talking about for fs. He posts his lecture.

I am a first year freshman and this class is definitely a culture shock for me. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but the lectures feel unengaging. I respect the knowledge, but the admin of the course isn't my cup of tea. If you take this class, take notes on the key terms and do not take notes on all of the examples. No tests. Show up.

He teaches history as if it is your major and you are a grad student. Even if there are no prereqs, you NEED extensive background knowledge on his lessons. You will not keep up otherwise, especially because he assumes you know all the context and does not elaborate, talks fast, and all your grades are based on pop quizzes.

Easy grader, but one of the worst Professors you can have in History. Lectures are rambling and incoherent, will frequently demean and belittle students, does not believe in teaching anything that doesn't already gel with his particular, super-Christian worldview (he WILL force it on you), impossible to get in touch with in-person for office hours.

Prof. Curta was clearly very passionate about the field of study but make sure you have at least a background in the time period. I had none, and struggled because of it. His lectures are very quick and if you don't keep up with the information he's giving, you'll be very confused on the quizzes.

analysis.name: Antonio Faciola
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I was intimidated of this class before taking it, but I think it is really doable if you go to his lectures and read through his powerpoints. Office hours run by the TA's were really helpful to go to before an exam, because they would guide you on questions he could ask. Questions were written response, just pay attention to his examples in class.

Your grade is based on only three exams in this class. One exam was dropped, so if you start to fall behind, take the W before the F. He is very nice and SO KNOWLEDGABLE. However, I always studied for this class and never got 100% on the exams. Whatever he says in class WRITE IT DOWN. All the exams are written responses and it is SUPER HARD.

Dr. Faciola is a caring and kind professor however, his class is historically difficult. You need to attend EVERY lecture because not everything is in the slides he gives you, your grade is based off of 4 exam scores (with the lowest one being dropped). He does not allow makeup exams in ANY capacity, regardless of why.

Dr. Faciola is very kind & caring about his students. He personally gets to know everyone. Attendance isn't mandatory & lecture notes are posted online but he's more specific about material in class & notices your attendance. Exam & quiz questions can be too specific but if you really study it's not bad. Quizzes every week & lots of dropped grades.

Dr. Faciola is an amazing teacher.  His exams are tough, but the first exam is the hardest because you don't know what to expect.  Just don't write a lot on the exams and you will be fine, if not you run out of time.

analysis.name: Meagan Frenzer
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and passionate about history, great zoom lectures- that being said I absolutely would NOT recommend taking the online class. There is so much reading/annotating busywork each week, grading takes a long time to come out, and her posted lectures aren't even her and sometimes don't match the quiz/exam content. In person I bet is better!

She makes me want to — myself. There are so many assignments and on each one there are four annotations needed. I can understand this until it's 10-15 assignments each week with four annotations each. And they're graded harshly even when it was clear that effort was made. Would not rec; she's a kind person, but would not want her as a prof again.

2/5. You do learn a lot in this class, but the workload is overwhelming. There are about 7 assignments each week, and each requires 4 annotations. The grading is unclear and inconsistent, with no feedback at all. Some assignments go ungraded for weeks, then many grades are posted at once, making it hard to know how to improve.

Everything about her and her class was lovely. Her lectures were very informative and interesting. She gives extra credit opportunities. She is not a hard grader as long as you follow the prompts, she gives great feedback on assignments and how to improve next time . Would totally take again.

Professor Frenzer's love and excitement for history is reflected in lectures. Her lectures are energized and engaging, but also move at a fast pace. This class is a reading intensive class more than it is a writing intensive class. She grades fairly and justly: the grades she gives are very reasonable. I highly recommend taking Professor Frenzer.

analysis.name: JaKera  Felton
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's a decent professor, she is young and up to date with technology. However, I felt that she graded very harshly during written assignments and the course-long group project. She does offer extra credit opportunities throughout the semester though.

she grades harshly for a stupid class and takes an unnecessary amount of points off for small mistakes. it's not hard to get an A, but she's an annoying and cocky professor who doesn't take accountability for her mistakes. she also sucks at replying to emails, i wouldn't take her again tbh

Professor Felton is young and understand technology, but she gives little grading criteria for assignments and expects you to know what she wants. She gives a lot of opportunities and will help you through assignments if you explicitly ask her, if you don't, she barely provides feedback. She's very nice but I would not take her again.

I enjoyed this class. Very easy A if you do the work, although I didn't receive any feedback on my projects. The materials were interesting and the weekly modules corresponded with the assignment, and these assignments all led into to the final project. Other than not receiving feedback, I didn't have issues or complaints.

analysis.name: Feng Yue
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Incredible professor! He's funny, cares about his students, and very receptive to changes that will improve his course. Exams are difficult, but fair if you study the slides and review guide. Plently of extra credit offered as well.

Feng is an awesome professor! He was obviously knowledgeable about the topic and truly showed that he cared about the students. His exams weren't too tough and he offers a lot of extra credit. I enjoyed my time in his class.

Really great professor! This was his first semester teaching the full class, and he listens to students regarding what he can work on (we asked about EC and got a 25 point assign). Slight language barrier but overall a pretty good professor! Holds exam reviews to condense what's on the exams. Go to office hours and study and you're guaranteed an A!

Mr. Yue is literally the goat. He uses a fill in the blank style of lecture that makes it super easy to follow. One quiz per week and 4 exams are the only assignments and he offers a bunch of extra credit. Super responsive to questions and wants you to do well. Exams aren't bad at all and he offers a review session before each one. Bro is awesome.

Professor Feng is amazing! Exams are straight from the lecture powerpoints and he does hold review sessions for each exams. Quizzes are the only assignments given and they're also on lecture presentation. Attend class to do iclicker for EC. Honestly this is an easy class to pass if you study. He does have an accent, however, its understandable.

analysis.name: Fatemeh Tavassoli
