analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 130 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I feel so bad reading all these bad reviews. She's super lenient compared to other instructors in CISE, gave lots of extra credit that can basically boost you up a whole letter grade. Her lectures aren't the most engaging, and the auto-graded exams can be finicky, but exam questions stick to the materials that you should know. SHE'S NOT THAT BAD.

The quality of the lectures are not good and the class needs to be structured differently.  Also, my TA absolutely did not care to help me out on anything and would also act very unprofessionally and use profane language in class when he didn't want to explain a concept.  The midterms are very difficult and offer little to no partial credit.

Not a hard class in itself, but professor won't help you. Seems like she wouldn't even be able to get an A in her own class and lectures are constantly behind the assignments as if she uses some pre-made curriculum from another professor that she can't keep pace with. Leaves you doing labs using methods you'll learn a week after it's due.

The class itself is extremely easy, almost comically so. As long as you do all the work assigned, you'll pass. I almost never went to lecture in person, and I still learned everything with either the recorded lectures, help materials linked, or the textbook she provided/video supplements online (look at the yt she linked-its great) do not use AI.

While Ms. Tavassoli got a lot of hate during the time I had her, I think she is a wonderful professor. She was responsive to the class's issues and when we had problems during the exam, she gave a curve which bumped our exam grades up a lot. She also adapted her lecture style to fit our needs, something I haven't seen any prof do. Very nice lady.

analysis.name: David Grant
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Content was easy and relevant, and Prof Grant definitely enjoys and is qualified in the course topic.

Graded off 4 assignments, they took some time to get grades back, but nothing difficult in nature.  Had iClicker for lectures, but they were entertaining.

Professor Grant really cares about what he's teaching. Really great lectures, keep you engaged. Fostered more of a conversation while he taught. TAs grade everything, and they seemed to grade relatively tough. Exams are a good mix of MC/essay, which I liked. He made the final optional. Should get an easy A/B if you stay engaged. Would take again.

If you need an easy Quest 1, PHI1680 is a great option. There were a ton of readings but I never did one of them and ended with a 97%. There are 2 exams and Dr. Grant allows you to drop the lower grade of the 2. There were a few group papers and one final presentation. It's honestly hard to do bad in this class.

Honestly the most interesting and engaging class I've taken at UF or ever. Dr. Grant encourages participation during lectures but won't call on you unless you raise your hand, he's very open to people coming up to talk to him after class, he clearly cares a lot and makes the content interesting and relevant to today's world. I loved this class.

This teacher is genuinely so good. I think I've turned in late papers 20 times, and he was understanding each time. Very accessible and cares a bunch. If you do the readings and go to class this is the funnest class. It was really comparable to high school where it was very vibrant and active classroom. if you can take his class, take it.

analysis.name: Thomas Garvey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mr. Garvey is an advisor in the CJC who teaches this intro class. The class is graded on a few extremely easy assignments, as he grades on completion, not content. It is mainly just going to the career fair that is required. He also uses iClicker, the only downside being required attendance and entry/exit quizzes. Useful and Easy A (90 req.)

Claimed his main job is to be an advisor and not a professor and showed it - we had few assignments which weren't graded until the end of the term. Most were just to attend events or write a discussion post. When he did come to class, he was pretty insightful into the journalism school. Easy class to add on whenever if you are required to take it.

He's so easy and understanding. Always willing to help and to listen. We did iClicker every start and end of class so you have to show up, but its just one hour once a week, super chill. A lot of guest speakers and literally no homework. Do it!!!

analysis.name: Laura Greenhaw
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Greenhaw is a great professor, but your success in the class depends on how much you put into it. The entire semester revolves around a group project, and if you get an unreliable team, it SUCKS. If you care about your grade, you'll do great, but if you don't put in any effort, it shows, and the entire team is affected.

Dr. G is an awesome instructor. Just work with your group and pay attention in class to get a good grade. You get assigned to a team and have to work with them all semester to put together a project. Instructions are vague so she gives you freedom but also guides you. 2 exams, midterm asked specific questions so take notes in class during lecture

Dr. G is an amazing professor! The main issue with the class is the group project where it's just luck if you get assigned a good group. The instructions she gives are a little ambiguous, but if you ask her for clarification, she helps a lot. The exams in the class are conceptual but not hard since you get to use a sheet of notes you took.

Dr. Greenhaw is very enthusiastic about what she teaches. My only issue was the group project. I got stuck with a mediocre set of people which made the project frustrating to complete and a drag at times. Make sure you show up to class to take lecture notes, she does not provide the powerpoints and tests you on lecture.

Show up to class and take notes so you can use a notecard on the exam. Everyday is lecture but the topics are interesting. The big group project is actually really fun and you get to meet more people, but stay on top of it! Very little homework and the professor is so sweet!

analysis.name: Grant Jones
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Jones is one of those professors who truly cares about his students. He understands that people have things going on outside of school and works with you to ensure that you get your assignments done. I highly recommend him. His assignments are fun, and discussion posts are always exciting.
Prof. Jones is a caring instructor. He is thoughtful in approach and flexible with deadlines (if needed). This is one of the best and most applicable courses I have taken. period.

Professor Jones was a very kind and lenient professor. He cares for his students and understands when you have time constraints. All he asks is that you communicate with him. Also, the textbook readings weren't bad at all. As long as you read the required textbook (which doesn't take long), you'll do great.

Grant Jones has been the best professor I've had at UF. He is kind and caring, if you fall behind he is understanding and will give you a second chance to make up the work. He does require weekly discussion posts and biweekly R.I Responses, they are about 4 paragraphs each but it's not too hard since he asks for informal writing. Overall great guy!

Great Professor and even better course. Very straight forward with assignments, none of which are too hard. His lectures are very entertaining and he is a good dude. Easy A if you give average levels of effort.

analysis.name: Gunnar Heins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor! I think he teaches in a way that's interesting if your paying attention. If you go to class, do the hw, and focus on the practice exams, you should be more than okay. He also posts a pdf of all the figures he goes over in that module which lets you know exactly what you need to be able to replicate for the exam.

He has an accent which for me never let me concentrate. Boring because of his monotone voice and manner in speaking. His homework is based on accuracy, NOT completion. He gives no extra credit whatsoever. He thinks an average of a high B is sufficient. 
I would recommend Estevez, Gunay, and/or Blair. They are amazing and give extra credit.

Super nice guy, very helpful outside of the class and truly wants everyone to get an A. The class can be boring at times but make an effort to go every lecture, he explains everything. The homeworks are like the practice problems in the class, and the exams are like the homeworks. Highly recommend any class Professor Heins teaches!

Amazing professor! I would take any classes he teaches. He is super organized and very clear about due dates, policies, and lectures. The only thing is that the lectures are a bit long, but that is the nature of the topic. I cannot recommend him enough, please take his class! Super caring guy too, he printed out notes for all the students!

Do the problem sets and you're good to go for the exams! However, he does throw in 1 or 2 questions on exams that you've never seen before. He uses slides and the chalkboard, mostly everything he writes on the board is also in the slides but he goes through it step by step on the board. Really nice and cares about students.

analysis.name: Jill Goslinga
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 360 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Goslinga, aka as Godzilla in the Busines school, will do everything in her powers to weed you out. Good luck.

You have to work for the grade. The majority of the class gets a C. You need a B for Accounting Majors. Everyone else needs a C to pass. Read all chapters, go to live lecture so you are not distracted watching it online. TA's are very helpful and TZ as well! Quizzes straight forward, and tests are tricky.

Goslinga goes out of her way to make the class hard, but it's not impossible to do well. You really need to practice old problems over and over again. The book wasn't helpful. And definitely go to TZ, they know what they're doing.

The tests are ridiculous and the hw is worth almost nothing considering how long it takes. I got StudyEdge after the first test and still struggled in the class. Even if you understand the material, every single test question is a trick question that requires you to know a very niche piece of information. I wish I got StudyEdge sooner.

You will spend an absurd amount of time for absolutely no points on homework. You will study and actively do practice problems/tests and think you understand the material and then get a 49 on exam 3. It will not matter how much you actually know. Every exam is designed to trick you and I will now have to retake the class at another school.

analysis.name: James Hobert
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hobert is the best professor I've had at UF. He teaches quickly, but in a way that makes sense. He is happy to slow down to answer questions from anyone. Tests are nearly impossible, but the curves are fair.

Absolutely the best professor at UF. He is very clear and follows a very logical order in his notes. A lot of non-stat majors take this course and they tend to have more trouble with the class. It's not like the typical engineering classes. You can't memorize your way through and homework is not graded. Put in the work and you will get an A. Simple

Hobert is a good Lecturer. Definitely one of the better professors I've had at UF. People did pretty bad on the exams, but I think that's more to do with the students than him (a lot of UF students are pretty bad at calculus).

This guy is brilliant. He teaches in a very intuitive manner that has a tendency, given the material, to blow minds (in a good way). Prof. Hobert teaches very fast, so I would suggest pre-gaming this class with a redbull. Possibly the hardest class I've taken. Tests are demoralizing. Avg test grade is 40%. Curves FTW.

Tough class even for the smartest stats majors but completely worth it! I learned a ton and am much smarter because of this class. prof is passionate about the subject and wants you to learn - great about answering questions/helping during office hours. It is a full-effort class and probably the hardest I've taken. grading scale was adjusted a lot.

analysis.name: Deepak Haarith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I heard this course was an easy A. This new professor doesn't think it should be. There are so many deadlines to get through. He is very strict and expects you to submit everything on time. He sends many announcements, but gets irritated sometimes and asks you to read the syllabus again.Not sure why he doesnt use his own videos
Tough grader but he once explained answers in detail when I emailed him.
Jus wanna give good rating since few people in class chat groups hate this guy for no reason. He is alright. Slow and tough grading though.

If you expect to do nothing and get an A. This isn't the place for you! If you put in the work, I think Dr. Haarith was fair in grades and had clear expectations. He responded to emails and was available for office hours. This was a great course!

new professor teaching first time with old materials. he was transparent about it and said is making new videos soon. Old videos were kinda all over the place. unfortunately I wont see new videos. tougher to get an A than I thought, but not impossible. Most people get an A still. beware: you must read everything and spend time to get things right

analysis.name: Adela Halo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is very nice and helpful in & outside of class, but only take this course if you enjoy long readings (~20 pages per class/~60 pages per week) on philosophy-heavy material. Also, in-class participation is a significant portion of your grade, so if you are shy/don't do the readings/don't understand the readings, you won't do well in that aspect.

Amazing. Best humanities professor I've ever had. Halo is precise and clear with feedback, exacting in group discussions but always open and approachable. This is a good class if you want to improve your reading, speaking and analytical skills. All the readings are valuable and carefully selected. No time is wasted. Challenging but rewarding.

Halo actively encourages excellence in her students. She makes expectations clear, gives valuable feedback, and grades fairly. Her attitude is professional yet approachable. Think Professor McGonagall. Her class might seem intimidating at first, but if you put in honest effort, you will do well in the course and feel proud of your work.

Literally my goat. Reading is worth it because if you participate she loves you. What you say in discussion will be judged heavily. She's weirdly hilarious and very inspiration if you are interested in just about any branch of academia. Always available for a discussion or advice.

Adela Halo is an absolute expert on political theory, and she enhanced what otherwise would have been a boring intro class. If you have any background in the subject, the class will be mind-numbingly easy, but Halo at least kept my attention through most of the semester. There is a *ton* of extra credit so you should have no trouble getting an A.

analysis.name: Heather Young
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was very paper heavy. Some assignments are confusing, but just email her. She responds with clear instruction if asked. Be prepared to write about the same topic throughout the semester. Papers got a little tedious but it's very easy to do well. She offers several extra credit opportunities. Everything graded by TAs.

All around the best professor I have had at the University of Florida. She is very fair with grading amd every assignment has a rubric to follow so there is never any confusion on what you need for class or when it is due. If you are looking to take a speech class for requirment or not this is the one to take.

This class is a lot of work, very tedious, time-consuming, and annoying. Your TA grades everything. That being said, there's so many extra credit opportunities that have brought up my overall grade like 3%. Put in the effort and you'll be fine, still an annoying class tho. I took this during the summer with 3 other stem classes and still got an A

The class consisted of weekly writing assignments (~300-500 words) and discussion posts. The assignments were very repetitive and oftentimes asked for the same information as the previous week's assignment. The grading guidelines were sometimes unclear, though the assignments themselves were very easy. Highly dependent on your TA.

Her class was one of the most enjoyable that I have taken so far at UF. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Only complaints are that you can't trust the canvas due dates (but she gives you a due date sheet) and the tendency to push AI to science students.

analysis.name: Hannah Alarian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: POS3204: Dr. Alarian is the most entertaining, knowledgeable, and passionate professor I've had at UF. She is determined to teach you well and explain material you don't understand. There is a lot to read for this class and she gives out pop quizzes, but she makes sure you are prepared. Overall, the exams are easy if you are attentive to the class.

POS3204 -  you will read A LOT. readings can be confusing, with many of them being published studies. semester long group research project can be tricky, but she's very accessible and helpful during office hours. participation is MANDATORY. read before class and be ready to talk. if u dont talk for a class or two, you will get marked down.

Dr. Alarian was below average. Get ready to work hard, a little too hard for a mere polisci course for my taste. Brings one too many elements from other subjects into the course which genuinely just make it harder if your a liberal arts student

Dr. Alarian was one of my favorite professors of my entire college experience. I think I learned the most out of her class than I did any other single class. She was very direct with what was necessary to succeed, and if you really wanted to do well, you could.
This professor cannot teach or profess anything. Expect to learn and teach yourself everything outside of class.

analysis.name: Iser DeLeon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Save yourselves honestly. He doesn't care about this class & genuinely zero work was put into it. No updated syllabus, kinda just making things up as he goes (both the midterm exam and final project were surprises). Nothing is clear about what he wants. No learning is happening. Only like four assignments in the entire semester

He can be very disorganized. We have weekly projects and it is the last week of school and he has not entered grades for any of them. He will usually say "they will be graded later today" but they end up not being graded.  Makes the class more stressful because you don't really know your grade. Also very slow to grade exams and uploads thing late.

He's a great teacher. Actually addressed the misconceptions behind ABA. He uses real research to supplement his findings and you can find the book online for free if your clever. You have to go to class because he has weekly quizzes. He makes you read and answer questions for optional homework but it pays off in the end cause it's for the quizzes.

He doesn't grade anything! Each week we were supposed to have a project to work on, but most of the time he didn't post the description of the project. It's the final two weeks of class and he hasn't graded a single project and doesn't respond to questions about grades. Exams were easy/the only grades entered because they were graded by Canvas.

His class is structured to the benefit of the student. Expect daily attendance quizzes, but it keeps you on top of the material. Study guides for every exam, extremely helpful. Go to office hours before the exam for extra help. His lectures are amazing. He cares about his students. Best psychology professor at UF.

analysis.name: Shu-Jen Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 337 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Took Mac2311 my freshman fall and got an A. I went to class, did my homework, went to discussion (weekly quizzes), but MOST IMPORTANTLY took every practice exam i could find. Also, study edge was a big help. I put the time in and got an A. Took AP CALC AB in high school and got a 1. You got this! Class has required attendance due to clicker points

She's an amazing lecturer. She wasn't my assigned professor but I watched all of her lectures online. In my opinion she's the best to teach you Calc 1. I had already taken  Calc in highschool, so I knew what I was doing and I can tell you that Huang explains everything in the easiest way possible. She's energetic and loves teaching.

She seems nice. I just don't like the way her tests r designed. It's testing ur memorization ability rather than whether u actually understand & know how to solve certain problems. I wouldn't mind her testing on terminology & thm stuff if she allowed a cheat sheet on tests. MATLAB is cool to learn, but it can also be a pain. Ec is nice though.

The lecture material critically lacks detail and context, making comprehension nearly impossible, reducing it to rote memorization. Prof. Huang's dismissive or sarcastic response to student questions creates a toxic atmosphere. This behavior discourages students from seeking necessary clarification, creating a climate of fear and anxiety.

I feel like they were more concerned with catching students cheating than actually teaching. The lectures were hard to follow, and the exams had only 10 questions with no partial credit, making it tough to score above 70 even if you understand most of the material. The class also has a terrible TA.

analysis.name: Keiji Iwamoto
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very caring professor who is also very good at breaking down complex topics in Japanese. There is a lot of homework, but he is understanding if you submit things a little bit late due to having a big exam in another class, family issues, etc. Super kind and one of the best professors I've had.

Professor Iwamoto was great! Of course, Japanese language courses have a lot of coursework, but that's the nature of the course. So if you don't mind that and you have the opportunity to take a class with Professor Iwamoto, you should!
He has high energy and ensures every student in his class understands the grammar. His office hours are useful too

Professor Iwamoto is one of the best professors I've ever had! He made learning Japanese (which by itself is a very difficult topic) digestible and created a fun and interactive learning environment. I think he does a lot to make sure students don't feel to nervous to speak and encourages everyone to try their best.
The best professor I've ever had, and you can tell he enjoys what he's doing. Average level of difficulty for a language class, but he genuinely wants to help you succeed.

analysis.name: Joseph Larkin III
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Larkin is by far the least productive professor I have had throughout my undergraduate and graduate education. He is a poor lecturer and tests students on very specific details from the text that were barely, if at all, mentioned in class. He is also disrespectful to students. I beg anyone considering this class to reconsider. Very stressful.

Class is way harder than it needs to be. The exams focus on trivial details that he barely stressed in class. Since there is no way to practice with old exams, it is VERY difficult to know what material should be focused on. He is a nice man but I regretted taking the class.

The material is interesting but test questions range from satisfyingly challenging, to confusing, to un-needed trivium. You also dont get to review any test/quiz questions. It's difficult to figure what's important. He's a good guy, but if his class were clearer and more to the point, I would have learned more easily and taught myself less.

If you are looking at this and wondering if it's worth it to take the class, please reconsider. The topic is interesting and the book explains everything just fine, but the professor makes it incredibly hard. Testing on small details, confusing lectures, just not worth it. Buy the book and teach yourself if you are curious about immunology.

If you are a graduate level student, do NOT take this class. It's frustrating, pure memorization and not educative at all. Doesn't make you think and understand, it makes you memorize useless stuff. Really frustrating.

analysis.name: Flora Iff-Noel
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Iff-Noel was one of the best Latin teachers I've had! She's very strict on attendance, so don't even think about skipping or leaving early, but she goes a lot into the meaning of what you're reading, which is really nice. She sometimes seems slightly scary, but she's so nice and helpful. She also gives you very good feedback.

She was very nice and sweet, but I hated this class, she just read off the screen. From someone who isn't majoring in classics, this class was useless, and I hated coming to it. There's a minimum of 3 discussions, a group presentation, 12 quizzes ever Friday, a midterm, and a final. I passed, but this area isn't my strong suit it was just so boring

I loved her class. She meets students where they're at, and she's very knowledgable about her specialties. If she's teaching anything about Augustan age elegy, I'd highly recommend it. She's also very strict on attendance, but if you're someone who participates and clearly isn't just skipping for fun, she's very understanding about it.

She was a great teacher! Her Latin classes are definitely a bit harder than some of the other ones in the department, but they're not bad at all. She seems a little scary sometimes, but she's not, she's super nice!

It was more of a Latin literature class than i was expecting, and WAY more of an augustan-age class than i was expecting, but it was a great class overall! She was knowledgable, and very helpful with answering questions after class.

analysis.name: Amie Imler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: This class is genuinely an easy 100%, but it is A LOT of work. The only reason why I didn't give her a five-star rating is because I do not like her flipped-classroom way of teaching, as there are way too many pre-lecture videos to watch over the weekend,. Other than that, she is super nice and knowledgeable.

Mrs. Amie is the sweetest! She was the lab instructor for Intro to Animal Sci and extremely qualified and knowledgeable about the animal agriculture sector. She brings much experience teaching high school agriculture and running her own livestock operations to the classroom, which enriches the student experience. I recommend getting to know her!

The class itself is fairly easy. However, be aware that attendance is mandatory. Class is normally given at 7:25 or 8:30 (in the ANS building which is FAR from main campus). Every week, you must watch around 2-3 hours of pre-recorded lectures because she DOES NOT lecture in class. The assignments are easy, but it is a lot of busy work.
Pretty good. Her Career's class is a lot of busy work. You do get a full drop for a speaker if you can't show. A couple of the large assignments feel random but it's an easy A.

This class was very fun. A lot of the assignments were VMCAS sections to complete to prepare for the vet school application so I would not recommend it to freshmen with little college experience, but it is doable. Grading is done fully by the TAs. Class time consists of presentations from different veterinary professionals, so it is very helpful.

analysis.name: Jill Ingram

obviously very very smart and super sweet (gave us cookies at the end of the year 😭)

analysis.name: Ingrid Kleespies

Could not recommend RUT3443: War and Peace enough as an elective. This course changed literally everything for me.

Extraordinary professor. Incredibly passionate about russian language/literature and so knowledgeable. Very fair grader as well. Lets students learn at their own pace. Very accessible outside of class and through email. Lots of room for extra credit improvement. Would take again.

Dr. Kleespies is genuinely a good person. She was very attentive to all or class (which was less than 30 people), and made sure EVERYONE participated. As mentioned prior, there is a lot of reading if you don't want to sound like a doofus in class discussions. Stay on top of the papers by writing them in advance. Just be proactive and participate.

Dr. Kleespies is a great professor! She really care about her students learning. She makes sure you get to practice pronunciation a lot. Iman is a brilliant professor and Industry Professional. She only wants the best for every student so there might be some tough love shown occasionally, but I promise it's just because she knows your true potential. Highly recommended all of her courses!

analysis.name: Sarah Jayasekaran

Don't take this class over the summer! I'm sure it is a fine class to take during a full semester but they squish all of the coursework into an undoable 4 weeks. Such a nice lady, but she just reads from slides and once you ask her a question, she is pretty stumped. The exams and quizzes are definitely harder than they should be for a gen ed class.

analysis.name: John Mendoza-Garcia

A true waste of credits and time. Assignments are unbelievably nit-picky and ridiculously annoying to find material for. What could have actually been a meaningful class turned into a flat out annoying ordeal. Sad that a required class is taught so poorly.

Absolute JOKE of a class, he is impossible to reach and even if he does see your message, there's a 96% chance he'll say something along the lines of "its in the rubric" which is utterly unhelpful. analysis.name: John Streese

review_highlights.comment: Have nothing bad to say about this class or the professor. Dr. Streese is honestly great. He's one of the best instructors I've ever had in all of my educational career (elementary school to college). I wish he taught more classes. He is just one of those legendary guys that you'll never forget. Please, please, please take him. You won't regret it.

For Calc 1, he is the absolute BEST professor ever & not hard!!! Granted, I already had credit for Calc 1 from AP Calc, but I just retook it to brush up on some things, & I'm HAPPY I did. Streese is truly a great human being & professor. Please try to take Calc 1 with him SPECIFICALLY if you can. You can't get anyone better!! He is truly a gem.

Please, please, please take Calc 1 w/ him. He's super chill, kind, and funny. Lowkey, not a bad class at all if you just grind past exams (which he provides a surplus of) and just pay attention in class. Can't lie I already had credit for Calc 1 from AP Calc BC but retook to brush up on some stuff and Prof Streese is just so good. Highly recommend!

analysis.name: Jan Robitzsch

analysis.name: Kevin Knudson

Required to buy 5 textbooks (2 written by her), 2 papers with content that will never be discussed in class, and exams with very ambiguous questions. Do not take CPO2001 if you see Leslie Anderson next to the course.

Literally the class was 2 essays and 10% participation. Lot's of reading, but I didn't do a lot of it. Lecture heavy, but useful for writing her papers. She's very opinionated, but write your essays based on that. I personally enjoy her, but I know people don't because she's lecture heavy.

Not really sure why ratings are so poor, I know everyone has different learning styles but legitimately if you just show up, pay attention, and participate in discussions you will be more than fine. I personally really enjoyed the integrated discussions/seminar style format.

Worst Teacher at UF. She needs to be fired. She is not only rude but if you get questions wrong she deducts points of your grade! I'm going to the Dean and I'm going to complain about this poor excuse of a teacher. Avoid like the plague!

analysis.name: Lauren Hodges
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: VERRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRYYYYY surprised by the low ratings for Hodges. This class can't get easier. Yes, you need to understand musical stuff, but if you actually study a bit (wow, such a shocker in college), you can get A's on the longer music essays/listening assignments. She should have a 5/5 rating with 100% take again & a 1/5 difficulty.

Easy online class for a gen-ed or humanities requirement. Weekly work is just a textbook chapter/video lecture and a short quiz + discussion post. You can just control-F words from the quiz questions in the textbook for the answer instead of actually reading. There are 4 easy longer written assignments every few weeks that take 2-3 hours each.

Online class that is not very rigorous at all - would recommend to fulfill some GenEd requirement. I never watched a lecture, and you absolutely do not need to do so in order to get an A. Accordingly, I can't comment on how good of a lecturer she is. If you like music analysis at all, then the content will be interesting - Unit 2 was my favorite!

Class is pretty boring in structure, just 1 discussion and quiz each week, and a listening assignment every month, but the lectures weren't too dull. Thankfully, every quiz is open notes which makes this class significantly easier and more bearable. This is the type of online class where you can easily cram a weeks worth of it on the last day.

This class was really interesting to me as it covers music ranging from Indian music to Jazz. There are weekly readings, but the textbook is quite interesting as you'll have music to listen along to and analyze. Fun class overall, but make sure to not make simple mistakes in the listening assignment and to double check.

analysis.name: Evan Lauteria
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely great professor. Gave online games to play and write reports about that was engaging with sociology topics. No real homework other than that and the surveys related to it. Only 2 tests and both were very easy if you reviewed the PowerPoints he posts. Skipped basically the last 2 months of lecture and still got an A. Highly recommend.

Gave us online "games" to play and write essays about, very straightforward. A couple of easy worksheets. Two exams that weren't bad. You don't really need to read. Skipped the last half of semester and just reviewed the slides he posted. I would recommend attending lecture at least once a week if you plan to skip though.

amazing. attendance is not mandatory, 90 is an A, 2 exams (worth only 30% of your grade), 4 short papers with lenient graders, one of which gets dropped including zeroes for no submission, and he's funny. first professor i willingly loved going to class for, please take him. not a single bad thing i have to say i hope he wins the lottery

dr. lauteria is goated. he's so enthusiastic about the course and makes going to class enjoyable. just make sure you get a good group for group projects, but even if your group sucks you'll be fine. exams r based off of his lectures/slides. despite the class being relatively easy, i definitely learned a lot!! take him if u can

Great lecturer; kept me extremely engaged. There's 2 exams that are super easy as long as you know the vocab he gives you. Four homework assignments are playing a video game, talking about them in groups, and writing short papers about them (easy and fun). Attendance is extra credit. Take this professor.

analysis.name: Larissa Williamson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 389 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Between much too wordy definitions with far too few examples to illustrate what they are telling me, multiple choice questions designed to trip me up in the semantics, and the mousiest personality I have ever seen in an adult, this class is easy, but supremely grating on my nerves. Easy because what I don't get I can Google.

Her lectures are verbatim printouts of what is covered in the text. She does not elaborate on the points she discusses; rather, she merely sits in front of the printouts, annotates them, and reads them aloud. You can easily just read the text yourself; her lectures don't add anything new. Very disappointed with the quality of this course.

GET STUDY EDGE it is the only reason I learned anything. Attendance is mandatory but you can log on and do it from anywhere. Lectures are her filling in blanks on the lessons. There's a lot of homework which helped me learn but it's a no calculator class and there are questions that make you use one. Also a CODING group project….. good luck!!

Absolutely terrible professor. You cant understand her at all which means you will have to teach everything yourself. Homework and quizzes are straight bs and her notes dont explain anything at all. She is no help at all and graded one of my exams wrong and was adamant on not rounding up my grade less than 0.1% so I could get an A.

Take it online. Attendance mandatory but could do LC at home. Random coding project. And lock in for midterms or u might get cooked. Final has no overall practice but question are similar from year to year. Not difficult class as long as u know how to manage without a teacher.

analysis.name: Timothy Murray
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was the best class I have ever taken at UF. I loved it so much and it was so easy. It felt like the whole class was one big family and it was the best environment ever. There was a decent amount of readings but if you don't read all of them you'll be fine too. Trust me, take this class, you won't regret it. You might be bored at times tho lol

The readings can be long and kind of boring, but there's usually only one per class that is actually required. Dr. Murray is super engaging and enthusiastic about the course. Due dates were pretty lenient, and grading was relaxed. Would highly recommend taking this class with him as the discussions are actually worthwhile.

This class is very straightforward; you listen to a panel of researchers once per week and meet with your TA and group to work on your semester project. Very low stress, and all the interaction with the class will be through your TA. You get a good introduction to research, although it can be boring at times.

Took him for MUS1610, and he is a very good professor. If you're taking a quest and need a class, take MUS1610. There are weekly readings, but you can skim through them, and they aren't difficult. Attendance is mandatory and graded, and the assignments are very easy and spread throughout the course. The professor was done wrong on ratemyproffessor.

This class was extremely disorganised and I can count on one hand the number of times Professor Murray actually provided any type of clear instruction. If you're in URSP, you just have to sit through it, but don't expect any actual educational value. In class, you watch almost entirely STEM panels and you work in your small group outside of class.

analysis.name: Melissa Mellon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor who is very accessible during office hours. She listens carefully to students' questions and makes a genuine effort to help them understand the material. Expectations are clear, and the course involves longer writing assignments, including a 6,000-word requirement. Overall, a very supportive and effective instructor.

I actually had this professor for ENC2305, but the option disappeared. Dr. Mellon is such a fun and helpful professor. She gave good feedback for essays and she was friendly and welcoming. She teaches other English classes and quest courses, so I recommend having her if she pops up as an option.

Super easy A along with knocking out the 6000 word requirement. Assignments are graded pretty easily and most people in the class get an A. Her lectures can sometimes be annoying as she yaps a lot, but as long as you show up to class, you're good. I would often push assignments to the last minute and would always get high A's. Highly recommend!

Great teacher. Definitely take her. Relates very well to students. Allows you to rewrite one of your major assignments per semester. Will do anything to help you learn and become a better writer. Very helpful during office hours. Genuinely tries to see situations from the students perspective. Very animated in class. Keeps everything loose and fun.

Took Mellon for spc2608 Summer B as a Freshman and I got an A. Grading is based on 4 speeches, and 2 written exams. Exams are a piece of cake, i got a 100% on the midterm. The class can be very subjective in grading. Speeches are graded from a rubric, but many times I didn't agree with the grading. Overall, not too hard to get an A with Mellon.

analysis.name: Mark Power Smith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: When I say run in the other direction, I mean it. His grading criteria is extremely unclear, and he takes off points for things when asked about, will say maybe he shouldn't have. He never guides the class in the direction of what he wants us to get out of readings, leaving us unprepared for the answers he wants on exams.

Professor Power Smith is an amazingly entertainer lecturer, and makes what could easily be a very boring course and repetitive class routine into a phenomenal student-based discussion class. He's also very caring and gives good feedback on assignments. Definitely take him for a Quest course if you get the chance.

Professor Power Smith is great! He sparks playful debate between classmates which helps us get to know each other, and encourages us to openly discuss our opinions without fear of judgment. Office hours were very helpful to get feedback on how to improve my writing, and he is overall a great person to talk to. I hope to take another class with him!

Amazing lecturer, and I really felt like he prepared me for most of the quizzes, which, admittedly, were quite difficult. Make sure to do the readings and participate in the class discussions if you want to do well.

analysis.name: Mike Moorhouse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Moorhouse isn't a bad person, but i didn't learn anything valuable that would be useful in my future career. Super old-fashioned and close-minded. i wish the class was more applied-learning and less academia-centric.

I rarely leave reviews for professors anymore, however Dr. Moorhouse is the most amazing professor I have ever had, that I feel the need to share. I normally have a hard time sitting through lectures, but not in his class. He is such a good lecturer and genuinely cares about your wellbeing, which is hard to find. I am so grateful to have met him.

Dr. Moorhouse was great. As long as you go to class, it's an easy A. 3 credits, but only meets once a week, lots of extra credit, and the material was presented in a way that is easy to understand. He genuinely wants to see students succeed and provides all the resources to do so. Office hours are also super helpful if you're struggling at all.

I usually skip classes, but I never wanted to miss this one. The material was genuinely interesting, and attending made the exams very manageable. The required reading was engaging, and the professor made lectures clear and enjoyable. Highly recommend this course.

Amazing teacher. Lectures are interesting and he is a good speaker. You have to buy a book for a required reading, but it was like $20 and a good read. Very straightforward exams and very little class work. Attendence checks are random and count for a grade. Participation will give you extra credit + has extra credit assignments.

analysis.name: Carissa Nicholson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You don't actually interact with Professor Nicholson too much in this class, as the TAs do all the grading and the lectures are done by somebody else. However the work is pretty easy, online assignments on a weekly basis. Depending on your TA, they may grade harsher than others, but overall should still be an easy A if you put in the work.

She's almost not involved in this course its mostly you and your TA. The work was pretty simple throughout the semester besides the final project but that was also ok. What really bothered me was how long it took to release the grades for the museum essay. I turned it in oct 5 and the grades were released dec 2 which is an insane wait time.

This class is not necessarily hard, it's just annoying. A lot of random assignments but they aren't difficult, just a waste of time if you don't care about the subject. The only time I communicated with the professor was in a Q&A discussion post. She's fine, nothing bad/good. Everything seemed to be graded by the TA's, who take forever to grade.

The work is usually pretty clear and pretty managable especially if taken online, but she (or the TAs) take FOREVER to grade things. As of writing this, I submitted an essay a month and a half ago and it is not graded yet. My TA answered emails quickly but graded too harsh. They are sticklers over the dumbest things, but give good feedback.

The assignments for this class are nonsense and are graded so slowly. We did a paper over a month ago with no feedback whatsoever and now we have to start our final project and cram our proposal into a 2 minute video presentation that has many requirements. Online lectures are super boring and slow. Only redeeming quality is the light workload.

analysis.name: Nigel Newbutt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't think I could say enough good things about Dr Nigel, he is an amazing professor. Very reasonable, caring, and engaging with every single student. You can tell how passionate he is about the subject and his work as it shows in every class, announcement, and conversation. If you have the chance to take his course, DO IT! I'm sad it's over.

Dr. N is the best!! You can tell he truly cares about his students, and he is passionate about his material. He does do a lot of in class group work but it's nothing difficult, just be engaged with your group. There are also not many assignments to submit throughout the semester. I would take his class again if I can.
All of the assignments are super easy and very manageable. Dr. N grades pretty quickly and always gives helpful and positive feedback. Definitely a very easy class.
Dr. N always provides amazing feedback and grades very timely! His grading criteria is clear and followed, and I really enjoyed this class.

Professor Newbutt is amazing! I wish more professors were like him! He shows a general and authentic interest in his students. He wants to help if you need it, offers meet-up times that are convenient, gives extra time when needed, and is hilarious! The class is laid back and you move at a comfortable pace.He makes every week interesting and fun!

analysis.name: Linda Nguyen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 137 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The best way I could describe: You are learning Spanish, but the tests are in Italian and you are supposed to understand Italian because Italian and Spanish are both derived from the Latin language. I have never received lower than a B+ in my entire undergrad and am struggling to pass this class. Averages on tests are so low she wont publish them.

The lab part of her class was so unorganized we had to sign up for an exam time , with half of the class scheduled to take the lecture exam Thursday, students obviously freaked out and lined up for hours to get a spot on Friday, this created a fire hazard and had to be shut down and she was mad at us, but this is no way to sign up for an exam.

Dr. Nguyen is the worst professor I have had at UF. Her lectures are very basic, but she expects you to have a grand understanding of the material. She blamed our low test averages on attendance and not her incredibly poor ability to educate us on the points she considers important. She does not care about her students.

I genuinely enjoy anatomy and was excited to take this class. Unfortunately, Linda Nguyen was an awful disappointment. Her exams are incredibly inconsistent so you never know how you should be preparing for an exam. She writes questions in a way that are meant to trick you and are very hard to answer correctly. I would NOT take her class again

Dr Nguyen is the worst professor at UF. Her lectures are over simplified and useless going to class, but her exams are extremely difficult. Need to read the book thoroughly inside out to do avg on exams. Blames the bad grade on attendance not on her lack of teaching us properly. DO NOT TAKE HER. Doesn't curve even if the class average failed.

analysis.name: Jason Nowell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 152 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Coming from someone who struggles with math, these reviews are so inaccurate. Professor Nowell is very accessible and would drop everything to tutor you. Xronos gives practice problems and review that mirrors the exams. He drops 4 quizzes and deadlines are flexible. If you're taking this class, PLEASE go to office hours - you'll see improvement!

Made Pre-calc way harder than it should be. Tries to explain topics so that you understand more than just the formula but ends up confusing students. Exams ALWAYS have something on them that was never taught in class.

The way he teaches in lecture makes everything hard. The steps that you thought you knew from middle and high school has to be thrown away to understand his style of teaching. The problems he does in lectures are way easier than what he puts on the test. Every test we took, there were mistakes he made on the exam. You really have to try hard .

Jason, who although seems like a very kind and smart individual, does not know how to effectively teach a large body of students. His lectures and lecture notes are extremely confusing , even when they are on simple concepts. All of the work throughout the semester (homework, exams,lecture notes) contained multiple typos and mistakes.

Sets and Logic is an inherently difficult class but Professor Nowell did a good job explaining these difficult, conceptual topics. He gave the class a say in what kind of exams we wanted and provided extra credit throughout the course. He was very helpful when you went to him for help.

analysis.name: Neha Rani
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are useless when it comes to learning anything useful for software engineering. Every week there is an in-class assignment that is a complete waste of time.

I took her for summer. The class is essentially just a group project/participation award. Her lectures don't matter for the class and have no real substance. The difficulty depends on how ambitious your group is, you could get an A with very few workhours if your group wants to do the bare minimum. Attendance was once per week and could be virtual.

This class felt very fake. The prof pretended to lecture, the TAs pretended to grade, and the students pretended to learn. You have to make a website without learning how or being assigned prereqs. It was an easy A if you do the work, but the weekly assignments are repetative & unnecessary. Wastes potential to simulate a real work enviroment.

Her lectures were completely a waste of time and she looked like she didn't want to be teaching. We were not prepared by her lectures or the TA's discussion to create the main group project. All the documentation assignments took away from our time teaching ourselves full-stack dev and it seemed like busy work. This class was so frustrating.

Essentially a semester-long group project with hours and hours of useless busywork sprinkled in. During lectures, all she does is read off slides with near-zero emotion in her voice. The only reason to attend class is the required, completely unrelated in-class assignment every week. Easy A, but the biggest waste of time I've ever been put through.

analysis.name: Marinas Naibi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures and work given often felt unorganized and we had few assignments to be graded on. The lectures would often focus too much on concepts, but then the exams would be more math heavy in comparison. I would recommend utilizing your textbook and outside sources. Otherwise it was still an interesting class to take.
Her exams are poorly managed. She has no prep material for exams, which makes exam prep an overly difficult process.

Ive seen a lot of people here say this professor is a lot of work. I took AST1002 during the Summer, so it may be different for me. Prof. Naibi is fair and understanding. Shes passionate about the subject. While theres a little bit of work, its really not all that much. Just do your quizzes (easy for the most part) and go to class, youre fine.

My TA graded discussion posts like she took joy in ruining our grades. First college class I've gotten multiple D's on discussions. The projects take forever if you don't pay for a website like CourseHero. A ton of online assignments due every week and if you miss a few theres no shot you're getting an A. TOOOO much work for an 1000 level gen-ed.

The class itself is A LOT of information but its kind of interesting. The quizzes are super easy and the exams are mostly questions from the quizzes or practice exams. The projects arent too bad and the homework can sometimes take a while but its not hard at all. The lectures are sometimes hard to understand and usually contain a lot of info.

analysis.name: Desika Narayanan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is awesome and he has a way to make every lecture interesting and enjoyable. The exams are weighted less than your typical math/science courses and the homework is 45% of your grade. I was able to understand a majority of the material with light studying.

Dr. Narayanan was awesome! Outright said he wanted us all to get As, and made that a reality for anyone who tried. Encouraged collaboration on homework and made it a major portion of the grade so exams were less stressful. His lectures were entertaining and I enjoyed this class much more than I expected. If you have a choice, choose his section!

Absolutely love this man he really knows the material he teaches, and does it extremely well. This is my second semester taking a class with him, and his expectations were the same. He wants all of his students to not only succeed, but understand the material and take it with them. Very awesome guy.
Dr. Narayanan is amazing just take him as a professor

I learned so many really applicable programming skills from this class. He's very generous with grading and really wants you to succeed. The project was challenging but really fun to try to figure out (I think only one person got it right but we all scored really well for effort lol). Would recommend this class to every physics/astrophysics major.

analysis.name: Natalia Dambe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: First of all, she is a good teacher, however, there are no textbooks or recorded lectures. She pulls test questions from articles and videos she posts each week. Many articles would not work. Midterm exam had questions that were covered last week of class. Not enough time on quizzes, but two attempts. It is a good class, not the easiest.

This teacher was amazing! Very kind, responded to emails in a timely manner. The information in the class can be a little difficult to understand sometimes, but that is expected. Overall, would be more than happy to take another class with this professor.
While the content itself can be boring, she is very kind and caring and responds very quickly to emails. Obviously very knowledgable in her field already, despite only being a graduate student.

analysis.name: Augusto Oyulea-Caycedo (oc)
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's retiring, but: great guy, lots of knowledge, sucks as a professor however. Lectures are barely there and he goes off on twenty-minute tangents every five minutes, making it impossible to take useful notes or even pretend to feel engaged. Little to no instructions on final poster project made it a difficult thing to get done.

The lectures are 90% photos with no captions. It's often hard to understand him because of his accent and quiet voice. Tests are based more on the book than his own lectures and usually include minute details no one focuses on. You have to teach yourself everything if you want to pass. Didn't communicate with TA and hard to reach outside of class.

Very passionate about what he does and incredibly knowledgeable. Lectures were good and I enjoyed listening to them. I had a great experience in the class. Professor has clear grading criteria and is willing to explain things to you, and work with you, to succeed in the class

The first few weeks I didn't know he was speaking english. The tests are based on the book not lectures but  attendance is taken randomly. The class isn't that hard if you do all the reading but you have to teach yourself because you cant understand anything he says. The lectures are painful and dont help with learning. I suggest another professor!

The class is pretty boring, but he is the sweetest man ever. He is very intelligent in what he does even if he goes on little tangents sometimes. You really won't be able to get through the papers without going to a few lectures & skimming the textbook. He lets you pick your topic for the term paper & asks everyone to share their work at the end.

analysis.name: Esther Obonyo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 2 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good professor with lots of resources but probably a better manager than educator
She cares a lot about students and makes her best to help us succeed, but we have a lot of homework and projects and some of the stuff we do doesn't always make sense. Some lessons are boring.

analysis.name: Odile Guinot
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice teacher lectures are just unnecessarily long. Textbook with Smoking Notes is helpful if you don't wanna watch them. Honestly the only thing that sucks is that the tests are weighted super heavy so if your test average is a B but you have 100's on everything else you will have a B which is a bit disheartening. Extra credit is easy to get.

class is really easy just vocab heavy. never watched a lecture and study only day of exam (on me) so if you put in a little effort you can get a good grade. LOT OF HOMEWORK (still easy nonsense) but its like 100 questions per chapter. id take it again bc its easy and doesn't take too much time out a week.

People complain about the lectures but they enrich your learning by providing real-world examples. It's way more interesting than someone droning on without pizazz. Dr. Guinot is so cool and a great professor. Prepare to lock in, its a 4-credit for a reason. You don't need to pay for extra teaching

Ollie Guinot is a great professor. I had her for undergrad marketing and she was great for that class. For this class, she expects a lot for an elective most students are taking because it says marketing. Overall, this class is interesting and pretty easy, but she nitpicks about details often because she values the material probably more than you.

Honestly, theres just so much lecturing. And if she gets behind she just releases extra lectures so it takes longer to watch through. Its A LOT of reading and its very easy to quickly get behind in the class. Also, its all McGraw Hill.

analysis.name: Monikaa Oli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lab is one credit but its more of a part time job. Get ready for quizzes once a week based on two modules with material that won't be useful to study from because the TA makes the quizzes up. Multiple projects throughout the semester and a final project each worth 100 points. Most unorganized class I have ever taken and I'm a senior.

Take in the fall with Lee instead. Oli's Canvas sheet is messy, and disorganized with various rubrics for the same assignment often found. Lab itself is easy and an easy A, but it's tons of busy work and annoying. The weekly lab reports are lowk a completion grade. Class would be better if it was online….

Dr. Oli tends to be very disorganised. Course content was a mess; the Canvas pages were very hard to navigate. Emails would occasionally get lost for days or weeks, and communication with Dr. Oli and the TAs was nigh impossible. Requirements and expectations were constantly shifting, making it very difficult to keep track of what needed to be done.

Passivea ggressive to students and her faculty don't like her. Interactions may feel more critical than constructive, which makes it hard for students who value supportive, solution-oriented mentorship... would not get on her bad side.

IDS2935 MICROBES WITHOUT BORDERS (no course option for that). Interesting and fairly fun for a quest class but a lot of assignments. 1 discussion, 1-2 activities, 1 quiz, and 1 assessment every week. Plus 3-4 big PowerPoint presentations. Prof was somewhat responsive but the syllabus is confusing and due dates change often. No required lectures!

analysis.name: Abby Owens
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: GOAT Calc 3 TA. She has a website with past exams for all the tests that are great study resources. She goes over the exact kind of question that will be on the quiz right before you take it. Also very knowledgeable and can explain basically all questions.

Abby is really nice and genuinely cares for her students. I struggled pretty heavily in Calc 3 near the end, but her lectures were always great and extremely helpful. She is very passionate about what she is teaching and always go over tips and tricks to simply things that our professor didn't do the greatest job explaining. Only positives to say.

If you have the option to choose your TA, take Calc 3 with Abby.  I have nothing but amazing things to say about her.  She clearly explained all content and was very accessible for her office hours.  If I ever had any concerns prior to exam day, she would clearly detail any practice problems I needed.

Abby is genuinely one of the best TA's I have ever had for a class, she explained topics so thoroughly and made concepts so much clearer while also being the sweetest person ever. I truly looked forward to going to her office hours every week, sometimes just to chat and give myself a short break from studying. Highly recommend her!!

Abby was an amazing TA - always welcoming and patient. She explained tough topics clearly and made sure everyone understood. Her relaxed, supportive environment made it easy to engage or just take a brain break by listening or chatting. One of the best TA's I've ever had - I wish I could have her for more classes!

analysis.name: Asli Odabasi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: AVOID FOS2001. It had a reputation as an easy elective, but was reformulated into something else entirely . Frustratingly complicated assignments with confusing instructions. Weekly quizzes with a very short time limit, and the exams are administered with ProctorU, an invasive proctoring program. Do NOT take as an elective, you have been warned!

This class was incredibly easy. 4 open-note multiple choice exams, a weekly open-note quiz, 3 assignments throughout the semester, and short weekly readings on Perusall that were very interesting. Nearly all of the answers to exam questions are in the notes. You will probably spend an hour or less per week on this class. Would highly recommend.

This class is extremely easy, probably one of the easiest UF offers. If you are not a science student this class is also mundanely boring, but for how easy it is its worth the free 3 credits. Odabasi is not the best lecturer at all but you honestly don't need her that much for the course.

This is the easiest biological science credit class. All the exams are open note. There are 3 big assignments that are graded somewhat toughly, but still very easy. There is some reading, but they are short through Perusall, but content from them do end up on exams. Some weeks have a lot of assignments, but they don't take more than 5 minutes.

The class is all lectures with quizzes and exams, plus one 300 word assignment, like 11 assignments in all. Plus it's an easy A as long as you watch the videos. Seriously,  Dr. Odabasi is wonderful! The class content wasn't enthralling  but it's also not my major.

analysis.name: Conor O'Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The weekly quizzes are tough even if you do the readings because the questions are pretty specific. There were three exams and they were kind of difficult so it was essential to do the readings and review the lecture notes. There are three books for the class and we read a chapter in all three of them each week. Attending lecture is not mandatory.

He is a great professor. Takes the time to explain topics thoroughly and is very knowledgeable in his field. He is really respectful, and his class was overall easy. Two exams that were based on lecture slides that were posted, and two in-class writing assignments that were not difficult. He is not a tough grader at all.

First half is based on textbook (basic social movement theory), second half is interesting cases. Lectures are based on the readings, not super inventive. Very nice and helpful if you go to office hours. TA grades everything so that's a toss-up.

Professor O'Dwyer was amazing. He is incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and passionate. His lectures were organized and nuanced, sparking engaging discussion. There is a lot of reading, but I took notes on only the lectures and earned 100% on every exam. I learned much more than anticipated and left the class with a solid political science foundation.

He is a very knowledgeable professor but not a good lecturer. The tests were on material that we had not learned (like maps of eastern europe) and they were not simple. Attendance is MANDATORY meaning that if you miss more than 1 day you're grade will suffer (excused or not). Wouldn't take him again, but I learned a lot - mainly from the readings.

analysis.name: Eamon O'Connor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great guy! Had my quest 1 with him, and he was chill. Weekly reading assignments and 1(pretty easy) group project, and 3 essays. One of the best professors I've ever had, very understanding, is easy to understand and has interesting assignments. Would forever take this class again

He's an awesome professor who makes lectures fun. I have a hard time paying attention in general, but he knows how to keep it interesting. Assignments are fun, and interpretation is quite open. It's a really good way for students to really understand and explore their interpretation of an answer, and sharing. Expect to actually enjoy class.

Loved this class! I'd take it again in a heartbeat. It really opened my eyes to the way we tell stories through digital means and even positively influenced my own work. Very caring professor that likes to have fun with his students while teaching, which makes the learning much more enjoyable. Learned about lots of new media as well!

He's great, always fun to go to his class and engages well with the students. He gives some great readings to learn from and the presentations are really funny. I enjoyed a lot of the assignments we did and had fun looking at my classmate's work in critique, was always hilarious and a fun learning environment. Love this guy

analysis.name: Karim Oweiss

The heart and muscles are not talked about once, even though this is a bioelectrical systems class. He's tough and can't teach anything to save his life
Lack of details about assignments

Professor Oweiss knows the course material with high technical competence. He can answer any question the student asks regarding the topic in a clear and concise manner. I regularly found myself encountering ideas I had heard about previously but they were said in a new and more concise way that allowed me to more deeply understand basic principles

analysis.name: Mark Rush
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 833 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: AWFUL. Refuses to give extra credit and wont shutup about it. Sent a whole yap sesh about how UF is getting more competitive so hes making the class harder- hello??  Proceeds to not curve bc online students cheat while others study their asses off.
Tests were not at all like the practice exams, Lectures are so boring, no extra credit and does not drop anything. Very difficult class with no economics background.

Very inaccessible and unresponsive to students. He discourages emails and provides little to no academic support. Three exams determine 90% of the final grade, with no extra credit. He even sent an email advising students to drop the course if they were not confident in earning a passing grade, since he would not offer assistance to improve grades
He is funny but for some reason he made the tests so hard this year. I barely passed and I am smart.

Prof himself has a good personality and cares about the course. However, he recently changed the grading scale to be 90% exams, comprised of 3, 30-question exams. Additionally, a 93 or higher is required to even get an A. The grading was way too hard for what the course was. Just take it fully online because that's the only way you're getting an A.

analysis.name: Puminan Punthasee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Maybe he was better for other semesters but way overhyped as a professor. Class is paced terribly and hes very inaccessible and seems to be clueless about the goings of his own class. The resources he provides are good but him as a professor is not good. Class is graded only on exams with no buffer grades so you have to dedicate your whole life

Not accessible outside of class whatsoever. Did not teach well at all, and even went as far as to tell students to stop asking him questions because that is what his TAs were for. Truly not a good professor and I would not recommend him to anyone. Run the other way if you can. Stopped teaching us a week and a half before the semester ended.

Pete explains concepts really well, but his exams are trash. Must do office hours and ALL study guides questions or you struggle. You're basically NOT tested on material, instead you're tested on memorizing the study guide questions. The class is doable if you can commit 15–25 hours a week to studying. He can also be sassy and unorganized.

worst professor ever & ta's would always cancel hours the week/day of exam. what's the point of u TAing then? makes the class & exams harder than need be. tries to purposefully trick you on exam q's. told my friend he's going to "get us" on the next exams. refused to curve in fear of "too many ppl passing"??? title ix king @ multiple uni's. avoid!!

Pete tries to appear energetic and good, but he takes it too far and makes the class intensely harder than it has to be. Orgo is hard already Pete :(

analysis.name: Alicia Petersen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Petersen made this course entirely more difficult than it should have been. Most of the course was her very dryly going through example problems straight from the textbook without engaging with the students at all. We have had a total of 6 assignments and our first exam from almost 2 months ago is still ungraded.

Wildly inconsistent and full of empty promises, but you can probably put in minimal to no effort and still fair okay in the class. She will not grade anything until the last minute. I am convinced she didn't realize this class was not astronomy at any point in the semester. Just look at her gator evals compared to your least favourite professor.

If there's one thing Alicia Petersen excels at, it's turning the joy of learning into a harrowing experience. The moment she enters the room, you can feel the excitement drain from the room like air escaping a punctured tire. Her lectures are akin to a fentanyl overdose, with each droning word serving as a lullaby to induce academic narcolepsy.

(1)  Assignments and the midterm exam still have not been graded, nor have answer keys been provided. Despite repeatedly promising in emails and during class to release them, nothing has been done. (2) Lectures consist copying from the textbook. When students ask questions, the professor often responds with, "I don't know; that's what the book says

Just reading through the slides and the book. Does not explain anything clearly. Homeworks are not graded at the end of semester, and we received grades based on some initial homeworks. Gives absolutely no feedback on your homework/assignments. It's better to have anyone else as the teacher for this course.

analysis.name: Sara Pollock
