Good lecturer. Made the material very simple to digest.
She didn't teach me anything. It was better to read the book alone.

Class is challenging but very doable, she gives you everything you need to do well. her teaching style makes it so that you really understand the material, which I appreciate a lot. two exams, both take-home, harder than she described but not anything crazy. weekly homework (graded easy) to help you learn the material. loved her and this class!!

He understands that not everyone is into what he likes (nematodes) and thus he is a pretty lenient grader. Should be an easy A for additional life science course for CLAS biology major. There is a group project, but due to corona there was a group paper instead

Easiest class I've ever taken and honestly not as boring as it sounds. He's a good lecturer & his discussion periods go by fast. I ended with a perfect 100. I also thought he was a dilf so there was that.
Awesome Professor, really relaxed. Doesnt really respond to email so its better to go to office hours for any questions. Gives extra credit and exams are open note. Do the work, get an A.

New to teaching, it really shows. Going to lecture is pointless. The meat of the class is lab reports, which take 8+ hours per week to complete. She made the 1st exam too long, had to trash it. does not present her material in a way that students can understand. She is inconsistent on her tests. You must attend class and do all assignments if you want to even pass her class. A genius, down to earth & genuinely cares. Mess up a submission? He'll email u to let u send it to him, no penalty. Had a life crisis? He'll check up on you on a personal level & give extensions. Yes there's a lot of readings and some essays but mostly watch the lectures & use the slides as notes. Skim readings for quotes to use. Communicate w him.

TA grades everything, one was definetily chiller than the other one. Overall, actually watch the lecture videos and take good notes and put time in on your own and the class is not too hard.

I can't understand anything he is saying because of his accent. This isn't meant to be racist at all; I am very against that. IK it's not his fault, but it did interfere w learning

Good intentions as a person but not a great professor. He gave extra credit and was sometimes understanding, but sometimes wasn't. The course was intro level and he made it much harder/ complicated that it needed to be.

analysis.name: Denise Quinlan

She is a great TA and would make an amazing professor! She is understanding and cares about her students. She doesn't grade harshly and wants you to be able to earn an A and succeed in the course. Her lectures are engaging and she makes discussions fun. I highly recommend!
Class was easy and the prof was more than fair on grading.

Amazing professor! His slides are very useful. He knows his subject very well.

analysis.name: Sindia Rivera-Jiménez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: There is not much positive I can say about her, besides the fact that she is super nice and tries to help when in person. I don't know how to put nicely into words that she is the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with. She is unorganized, always behind in lecture, inconsistent grader, doesn't know the material, and just simply doesn't uphold the standard of other ChemE professors. She is a nice person, and I had high hopes for her.
Dr.Rivera made guidelines very clear and helped out with everyone's team project since that is what the class is on. She was very nice at office hours, but I wish she was more prompt with emails.

Dra. Rivera has been one of the best professors I've had at UF. She is passionate about chemical engineering, so that made me understand the class better. I think her class was pretty difficult, but her office hours were very helpful. Would take again, but prepare to work!

I love Dr. Rivera! She is so sweet and is so welcoming to all questions and doesn't treat you like an idiot if you don't understand something. She is very passionate about chemical engineering which makes the class more enjoyable. There is alot of very difficult homework but she helps in office hours. The exams are usually easier than the homework!

analysis.name: Quinn Mccoy Hansen

LOVEDDD THIS CLASS!!! if you can get it for you quest 1: do it. it's super engaging and fun, even if you aren't a sports fan! the grading isn't tough at all (shout out to cristina fr) and the assignments are very easy to complete. overall, he's a super caring person and you can tell he's truly passionate about what he teaches. 100/10

Easy class obviously as it sounds, and if you're lucky enough to get it as your Quest 1, enjoy it. Every class was awesome and it was super enjoyable and laid back. Cool projects and some in class essays but never hard or difficultly graded. Very debate based and its cool to hear everyone's takes on things. He lives up to the 4.9.

Professor Quinn is one of the best professors that I have ever had. You can tell that he is super passionate about what he is teaching, and that he cares about the input of every student in his class. The class itself is a quest 1, and is full of super interesting content connecting soccer to micro and macro issues in the world. 10/10 class

Amazing class and amazing professor. The assignments are super easy and the workload is so light and he's genuinely so passionate about what he teaches. Easiest possible quest class to take at UF and I highly recommend. He's also an amazing person and super chill. Best possible quest class imo.

analysis.name: Ralena McDevitt

She's also super funny and has some really great stories to share! I recommend her to anyone! Take ASL!

Professor McDevitt is a helpful and engaging professor. This was my first time taking ASL, and I learned so much. She is very kind and enthusiastic. There is no note-taking, and you learn everything from just being present. The assignments are easy and her tests are as well, as long as you attend. I really enjoyed this class and would definitely recommend taking ASL with Professor McDevitt!

This class was awesome! I highly recommend you take ASL with Professor McDevitt; she's great and clearly explains everything. I was very skeptical going in since I had 0 previous ASL knowledge, but was pleasantly surprised by how digestible she makes the material. I look forward to taking ASL 2 with her in the spring

She is able to convey the material very clearly and all the learning is done in class. Participating in class is what helped me succeed the most and remember signs. I knew the alphabet and a few signs before this class, and it was pretty easy to pick up.

very sweet professor but SO unorganized. Never knew my grade in the class and he does not know how to use canvas correctly. only take him if you are a super type B person and you're ok with deadlines being constantly up in the air ...

Professor Tisby was one of the best teachers I had at UF. She is nothing but caring and wants all of her students to succeed. upbeat guy, pretty hot professor, interesting dude, but most of the stuff done in this class feels pointless; the entire subject of paratexts is seemingly useless. very tough grader, and you dont get anything back until november, so u don't really know where u stand. and grade on midterm WILL be lower than you xpectd, but u can improve on final

analysis.name: Suzanne Utley

Awesome and extremely professional teacher. Professor Ulanowicz is awesome. She put a lot of background information about the text into the lectures and really encouraged conversations, especially with different perspectives. Professor Ulanowicz is AMAZING! Take her class if you're genuinely passionate about the subject, and I promise it will be one of the most rewarding educational experiences you can have. This was a super super easy Latin class (I took it back in 2023, forgot to rate her) but she was amazing and so funny. She's also super understanding.

As a graduate student you already have so much work to do and this class expects you to have a pop-quiz at 8.30am every week (open book luckily), you have to submit discussion questions on sunday night and it takes the whole week to work through a homework set due on friday.

analysis.name: Adam Veige
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Chem 2 with Dr. Veige can be described simply as a "train wreck". He is cocky, and his arrogance is clear with his exams that are designed to be near impossible. The class average for one exam was a 60% and he blamed that average on students not studying hard. Believe me when I tell you if you want an A in chem 2, stay far away from him.

This class was very difficult, I left every exam feeling defeated even using study edge and studying a week a lot. His exams are tricky and nothing like the questions you see in class. Get study edge and it will help but he is a difficult professor.

If you want your GPA to suffer, this is the BEST CLASS TO TAKE! Dr. Veige's chem 2 is such a nightmare, it's hard to describe. Dr. Veige is cocky, arrogant, and it is clear that he doesn't give a hoot about your performance. He provides little to no guidance when it comes to preparing for exams, which are impossible. SAVE YOURSELF AND YOUR DIGNITY!

Veige is helpful with the content during office hours. However, the exams in this course felt like they were written to trick students so his help did not improve my grade. The material was presented differently in lecture than it was presented on the exams which was extremely frustrating. I felt like I couldn't do anything right in his class.

BEST CHEM 2 PROF!!!!! He's so nice and has a greater demeanor. That said, you should definitely read the textbook/watch yt videos or else lectures didn't make sense and a lot of classmates struggled on exams. At very least write down the practice problems before lecture since he goes through those fast. Everyone wanted to take more classes with him

analysis.name: Chunmei Wang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Made a simple linear algebra class much harder than it needs to be. Weekly quizzes are unreasonably hard with questions far beyond what was covered in class. Lectures are poorly organized and a mess to watch. Lots of extra credit and lenient grading but be prepared to spend a lot of time learning the advanced stuff yourself.

Professor wants students to succeed in class. Lectures are not the best and you will likely have to teach yourself most of the material from the textbook but it is doable. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Weekly quizzes and exams based on homework questions.

The professor didn't use a textbook, instead copying content from another university's lecture notes without sharing the PDF. Homework was uploaded as screenshots, not LaTeX. Typos and unclear notations, like (A^{-1})^{T} = A^{-T}, caused confusion. Clarification requests on vague homework were refused, saying it'd be unfair.

Tough class, she just reads from the book without providing a clear explanation of the material. Weekly quizzes and mandatory attendance. Get ready to learn from the book if you actually want to understand the material. On the plus side, lots of extra credit and two quizzes dropped.

analysis.name: Melissa White
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Now that I'm graduating, I'm reflecting on my time in college and remembering how much of a uniquely bad experience this class was. I felt uncomfortable in this class. She would constantly talk about herself rather than the course material and would brag about things like putting in bad words about students so they don't get into grad programs

I would never take her class again! She grades so bad, she needs everything in the assignments. You work hard yo deliver a perfect assignment but she gives you just 60 percent of the marks. She is never satisfied. I agree that the course was interactive. I would never take her class again. She doesn't even support in emergency situations.

If you take a class with Dr. White, be prepared for lots of pointless assignments and an incredibly agravating group project. As long as you do the assignments, put in effort, and contribute to your group project, you should get an A. However, it comes at the cost of having to deal with the condescending and unprofessional Dr. White.

Dr. White seems to care a lot about her students and she is always open to helping students with their assignments. Her approach to the class does seem too casual though, with most of the lectures being over a year old and recorded in pajamas. Overall the class is okay but filled with busy work and felt like the prof did not care about the content.

The professor is condescending, self-aggrandizing, and rude to students. Highly opinionated and obstinate. Please do not construe her attitude as appropriate or common in the workplace, she'd have an HR list looking like a CVS receipt and be fired immediately. My recommendation is to consider other avenues for learning entrepreneurship.

analysis.name: Whittaker Schroder
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Whit is everyone's favorite for a reason. GIS is so tough, but he tries to teach us how to use the software, and is always accessible through email and office hours. He will give you everything you need to be successful, and is very understanding of incomplete labs, and will go over it with you. He really cares for his students, take GIS with him.

He was a very chill professor with not very many assignments. Attendance was taken at random but he is pretty lenient on if you have to miss for sickness or other reasons. We only met two out of the three days a week too. Overall a great professor

I took his seminar Collapse and Resilience and loved it. I was one of the few undergrads in the class, when I felt behind he reassured me it would get easier with time, which encouraged me to work even harder than before. He is so brilliant but so humble, so kind and so fun to talk to. I hope everyone gets to take a class with him, he's astounding.

Couldn't rate him any higher, you're very lucky if he's your teacher. Dr. Schroder is a super chill professor who gives out easy work at reasonable times and online. The work itself is light and as long as you look over the study guide and the slides you're guaranteed to pass. He's a goofy teacher as well and overall really kind!
made me switch my focus to archaeology and super handsome

analysis.name: Yuanxin Wang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The sweetest professor you will ever find at UF! He is a lenient grader and does not ask for documentation for missed attendance. He truly cares and workload is light unless you fully read the readings every week (not necessary to do well). TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!!!

I cannot recommend this professor more! He is super flexible about absences and is very forward about what he expects and is leniant on grading. The class has a short weekly discussion post, two exams, one paper, and a presentation which sound way worse than they are! If I could take him again I would in a heartbeat!!

OH MY LORD THIS PROFESSOR IS AMAZING. PERIODT. One discussion post per week, about 100-150 words. Then you're also graded on a presentation, a paper, and a essay-based midterm and a final. This professor is the GOAT, ngl, and he also gives us the prompts a week before the exam date. TAKE HIS CLASSES RIGHT NOW

Lots of reading but never did any of it. Prof is chill, just make sure to raise hand at least every other day to ask a question for participation grade. Took over summer B. 2 papers, weekly mini-paper, participation grade (attendance graded), and group project you do on one of the 6 weeks. Paper prompts given week ahead of time. Easy A

What a king. He's new and clearly wants you to like him, which isn't hard because he's very likeable. Really encourages discussion and makes you feel smart. Lots of readings but he lectures on them, so you can skim. Tests are easy if you review the readings. Learned a lot, thought a lot, and I would gladly take another class of his.

analysis.name: Siyao Xu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Reviews hating on Super Cool Siayo (not Siyao) are misinformation. Girlboss has such a cool cherry sweater and generally just great fashion. She teaches 2061 and we love her for it. She posts a review video before each exam where each question she goes over happens to be the exact same as the exam. 5% extra credit for total grade took me ten mins.
These people who are complaining are the same people who would be crying in 2048. Girlboss is a win!

Dr. Xu was very new to lecturing when I took the class, but she was super receptive to anything to make her class better, even changing her entire quiz format to help us learn better. She loves having people in her office hours and is very easy to ask questions to. One of the sweetest professors in the department for sure, would take again!!!!

Her lectures tend to feel slow, but she gets through all the content fine. Her exams and quizzes are based off the homework but contain some fundamental differences so you will need to understand the content. She brings up relevant research in class sometimes which is cool and she listened to our feedback very well. Her extra credit is generous.

Professor Xu is very clearly new to teaching and is still figuring things out. She is extremely caring, easy to approach, and lenient with grading (exam questions were VERY similar to her reviews). Her lectures were ok. She was very receptive to criticism so I think her courses will only get better from here

analysis.name: William Kenney
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 100% recommend. Attendance isn't mandatory but your grade consists of in class assignments and a few exams. In class assignments are done with your table group and graded on participation as we go over the answers in class. Everything you need to know for exams will be gone over the class before the exam (just study!) and there's no surprises.

Professor Kenney is a great prof!!! He has very clear lectures and outlines for the exams, so its hard to get anything below an A. There's usually an easy group assignment every week based on a short reading he will give, but its overall a very chill class and would recommend.

Easy A. He goes over the entire exam on review day, so even if you don't pay attention the entire unit, you can still score very high. He's a great professor and person; genuinely wants you to do well and is passionate about the class. The assignments are easy; you work with your group for all of them and require little effort from each member.

Professor Kenney clearly cares very much about his students and the material. As an environmental engineering major this class was not mandatory for me, but i found it very interesting and informative. He loves when people participate, and is very kind. He prepares you very well for exams(of which there are 4), and expectations are always clear.
If you need a science credit, take this class. It is great.

analysis.name: Han XU
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Without exaggeration, possibly the best Chinese professor in the country. Hard to imagine such a demanding and rigorous course taught in a better way by a better instructor. Waking up at 7am every day for the class was challenging and the persistent quizzes keep you working, but she is so nice and removes so much anxiety that you don't even notice.

Xu Han is an amazing and very understanding professor.She is a great teacher and I learned so much from her. You can tell she really loves her job and she makes me excited to go to class in the mornings. Hopefully I am able to get into her intermediate chinese class next semester. There are a lot of quizzes.

I've had 5 different Chinese language teachers and Xu laoshi was EASILY the best. She's very caring and wants you to pass, but she will also challenge you to get better. You will be challenged, but class is very structured and she is very clear about her expectations. She's super personable and just an overall lovely person. I miss her class.

Professor Han Xu or Xu Lao Shi in class was the best Chinese professor I've had and I am taking her again this semester with an earlier time because I wanted her specifically. She is incredibly caring and truly values what is best for the student more than anything. Expect weekly homework and vocab quizzes that aren't overly difficult.
Really kind and sweet professor! Lots of quizzes though so make sure you study

analysis.name: BingKan Xue
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good class, but lecture and homework is math-based, while exams are physics problems. It makes the homework not very useful to study from. Use previous years' exams to prepare. Take mech 1 if you want an easy A, take theoretical if you want to learn more physics (...or math, really).

We had two professors for this course. I enjoyed Prof Xue's lecture style much more and his exam questions reflected the lecture content very well. His organization of the class was understandable and he did not over-assign reading sections (unlike the other prof). Attend class, the iClicker gives a lot of extra credit.

Very difficult course, as expected... Introduction to theoretical physics is the first course in the undergrad physics curriculum really introducing you to the formalism. I don't think prof. Xue did a good job explaining the content well. A lot of the math, although meeting the prerequisites for the course, was glanced over with no explanation.

Tests ranged from difficult to straight-forward, but Prof. Xue gives tests from previous years to study. Homework made up 40% of the grade, but extra credit is given throughout the semester. Class sometimes diverged from the lecture notes, but he overall adhered to the structure of the notes.

analysis.name: Xiaochen Duan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is genuinely passionate about math and it's very easy to see that as a a student. He offers additional help if you're struggling personally too. I also personally found his sense of humor very entertaining and it made it easier to keep focused on the class. 10/10 would take again.

Xiaochen is genuinely one of the best TAs at UF. He wants you to succeed in the class and gives you every opportunity to do so. He explains things really well and is always available in office hours to help you!

Best calc TA you can have. His discussions are so fun and he really dives deep into the material and connects it with calc 1 basics. He also prepares you very well for the quizzes and cares about his students.
Absolute goat, no doubt the best TA you can choose for Calc 3. Helpful, passionate, he's got everything.

Mr. Duan was one of the best Teaching Assistants I have ever had the privilege to learn under during my time here at UF. Mr. Duan was always positive and enthusiastic to teach, and would consistently check up on every student to make sure that every one of us actually understood the material that was being taught. Very kind guy would def take again

analysis.name: Long Xiao
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You are set in this class if you study the slideshows - he will never ask you a question that you can't find in the slides. You are supposed to read the textbook, but you don't really have to in order to be successful in this class. He is very kind, reasonable, amusing, and respectable. I really enjoyed his class, and I cannot recommend him enough.

The absolute GOAT. Constantly cracking jokes during his lectures while still going in depth. Posts everything in a timely manner to Canvas. Very flexible to meet with outside of class and responds fast to emails. Some class content can be a little confusing, but it's 100% doable as long as you stay on top of the reading. 100% recommend for anyone.

the best prof hands down. u get a double sided cheat sheet on exams that u can type and print out, lowest quiz is dropped, both he and his lectures are super funny. sometimes his questions can be confusing, but still super easy. he randomly takes attendance 10 times during the semester but youll want to go to his class anyways. extra credit too!!

Honestly such an amazing professor, if you have the chance to take a class with him do it. It is a lecture-based class, attendance is taken randomly on 10 days. There are 8 quizzes which are 4 questions each and based on lecture notes, and 3 exams throughout the semester that he gives you a study guide for and lets you bring in a cheat sheet.

I loved his class. He is super kind, helpful, and approachable. He was always available for extra help and resources to succeed. He also teaches very well. You have to study and understand the material to do well on quizzes and tests, but he sets you up for success. I wish I could take more classes with him because he is the best!

analysis.name: Ye Xia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: WORST professor I have EVER experienced at UF. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The whole class is 2 exams and 1 project. He gives ZERO direction on the group project so you're completely on your own. Assigned homework ON THANKSGIVING. Also the lectures are completely useless. You will want to commit SIGKILL if you take this class

Honestly, I found this class quite interesting, but mostly because of watching the textbook author's lectures on YouTube and reading the textbook. Professor Xia's lectures are dry and drawn out which make them hard to get through. The test questions are easier than the complex homework, but many felt like “trick questions” based on unclear wording.

CSE senior here, Xia was easily the worst. The final exam and project (65% of the final grade) were never released, only the final grade after the semester was over. The prof reads off slides and exams are needlessly difficult. Tip for survival: Jim Kurose (textbook author) videos on youtube. Kurose lectures better in half the time and he smiles.

Might be the worst professor at UF. This guy still being allowed to teach is the worst thing to happen to UF since the shoe throw. In all my life, I've never seen a teacher just not grade the course. Both the final exam (40% of the grade) and semester-long project (another 20%) that we all spent time studying for and working on were just ignored.

Professor Xia is very knowledgeable about computer networks. This class is a lot of reading and homework, but his lectures essentially go over the textbook with slides created by the authors. There are 6 homeworks, two exams, and one semester-long project. Start homeworks early and study several days out from exam and you will be fine.

analysis.name: Xumin Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Professor Xumin is funny, enthusiastic, and very knowledgeable. I took his Quest 2 class on Poverty and it was interesting, but a lot of group project work and many reading assignments. In my opinion, the material from this class could be condensed into only a few lectures because it's very repetitive. He is the most responsive professor I've had!

Dr. Zhang's attention to detail, knowledge of agribusiness concepts, and responsiveness are what sets him apart. He genuinely cares about all of his students and his work ethic and dedication to his classes is admirable. The lectures, quizzes, and discussions are straightforward and interesting. The Landscape project is tough be he helps a lot!

Dr. Zhang is the definition of a good Professor. He is very enthusiastic and informative during each one of his lectures, his assignments are very fair, his exams go good as long as you study well. I had him for two classes, one of which was online, and he was great in both. Dr. Zhang, not only wants students to learn but also excel.
Xumin my goat, take this class its so easy

analysis.name: Xiaoguang Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A professor whose class is almost entirely determined by 3 exam grades. Lectures are really rudimentary and don't do much to prepare you for the exams which are much harder than the reviews. You'll most likely end up teaching yourself the topics or learn from and do review with the TA's. You can definitely do well in this class but Zhang won't help

He was a very nice guy, but his lectures just weren't great and hard to follow. He'd ramble about unimportant stuff for 75% of class and then rush through what actually mattered and most of the time miss important slides completely. Nothing he said ever really stuck for me, but you're going to have to do a lot of work on your own regardless of prof

Dr. Zhang was pretty good. I enjoyed his class and he was a good lecturer. The grading scale is very lenient as it is an 85. Exams were mostly easy and he provided practice exams and practice problems. There are weekly quizzes and assignments. Neither are too difficult.

Dr. Zhang is a professor who clearly cares a lot about physics and puts a good effort into his lectures and course overall. At times, lectures don't always focus on relevant info to exams and class can be difficult to follow, so be prepared to rely on his provided review problems and homework to fill in some of the gaps in learning.

He seems like a very caring, nice, and knowledgeable guy... but he sucks as a lecturer. He mumbles and wears his mic way too far from his mouth. It's extremely hard to hear anything he has to say, especially when the concepts are this difficult.

The class itself was very hard; exam 1 average was ~75% and exam 2 average was ~55%.

analysis.name: Xiaofei  Bai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bai deserves all the good things. He is by far the best Professor at UF. I know everyone says “this Professor truly cares about their students” but Dr. Bai blows every other professor out of the water. He is there not to hinder students but to see everyone succeed. Pay attention, do the work, do the extra credit. Effort will be rewarded.

Dr. Bai has been the best professor I've had. I don't typically rate professors on this platform, but Dr. Bai deserves it. He cares more about his students understanding and interest in the material more than anything else. His lectures are fantastic, the exams are material based and you won't be surprised by anything and take adv. of xtra credit.

Professor is super enthusiastic and will help you if you have any questions regarding the lecture. Lectures are presentation that are very easy to read and understand. Tons of extra credit. Tests are not that hard if you go over the lecture slides and practice questions he posts.
If you have to take genetics, take it with him. He wants you to succeed and makes it so attainable to do very well in his class. Exams are straightforward and there's extra credit.

Ive never rated a professor before but I feel like Bai deserves the shoutout he truly cares about his students doing well and you should take him if you want to do well in genetics his test are very straight forward most of the exam question come from in class Iclickers which he goes over and the other comes from homework.He also ofers extra credit

analysis.name: Myunghee You
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her class was easy but her organization needs serious work, a majority of her lectures consisted of scribbles on a white board and she barely covered the useful slides that she has posted on canvas. The exams are open note, but short on time. Its an easy class but not an easy elective to get an A in because of the two heavily weighted exams.

She provides a lot of information, but does not communicate exactly what will be tested. We had 4 exams, two multiple choice and two essay format. Her grading criteria is unclear and subjective. If you're thinking of taking this as an elective, I'd suggest taking something else.

Dr. You is very nice and obviously cares about our success in the class. Over the semester, there were 5 discussions posts and one essay, with two open note/online exams that were taken in class. The graphs that she made for lectures were hard to understand, but the slides themself had all the information. Easy A and really nice person in general!

2 open note exams in class heavily weighted. 5 discussion posts, EASY & a final essay. Grades discussions and essays very easily. Exams are pretty hard as you dont have much time to look for the answers in the slides so use other sources. All theories we talk about I learned in crim theory so u dont need to listen to lectures but go for attendance.
Best class I've taken at UF! Would 100% recommend

analysis.name: Youngmin Park
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 1 month into class and bros a wreck. cant teach the class well, couldnt write a multiple choice quiz correctly, assigned straightforward homework -- and then lost it bc students couldnt answer random abstract math questions on the spot for an 'audit' that was rlly an in person oral exam. now hes cancelling the syllabus?? steer clear.

I have never written a review before but Dr. Park is MORE than deserving. He provided so much encouragement to us as we improved, gave lots of extra credit and multiple drops, and made himself available by meeting and online frequently. He even cancelled the final because his students made such an impact on him. Best professor ever. Take his class.

Caring professor from day one, dedicated to student success. Seven exams may seem like a lot, but each covers manageable material. Always available on Discord and never declined in-person meetings. Extra credit offers low-pressure coding practice. The best professor I have had at UF, highly recommend you take the class if you have the chance.

This guy is an absolute sweetheart. He really wants each and every one of his students to succeed. Yes, the course is test heavy but because tests are frequently there's not much material between each test so it's not as rigorous as you think. He's always available to ask for help through Discord. 10 out of 10 professor.

I'd highly recommend taking any course with this professor. The exams were very representative of the content covered in class. He also provided ample extra credit opportunities and exam drops. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.

analysis.name: Alexander York

review_highlights.comment: Save ur sanity and don't take this professor. His lectures are confusing and they are not even his he takes them from an online program and does absolutely nothing for the class. His exams are so difficult compared to the study guide and nothing prepares you for it. This class ruined my mental health

Dr. York is a great professor. He is confident, gentle, and easy to understand. You can tell that he's very passionate about math when he's lecturing. He encourages participation and is supportive of students. One thing I didn't like as much was the fact that he writes extremely quickly during lectures; it's hard to keep up sometimes.

Dr. York was okay. I'd say the biggest disadvantage to his teaching is that he writes the notes instead of following the guided ones. At first, I attended his lectures but in the 4th exam, I started going to Demas like everyone else. Dr. York is very familiar with the material, so there is nothing you can't ask him. Overall its easy but boring.

He was horrible. I never went to his class but instead I went to Shabazz. She isnt better either because every time I went to her office hours she was so stand offish and weird. York will take forever to email you back and then want to have an attitude because he doesn't want to teach. Also, the tests are impossible to study for and are very hard.

Overall solid prof. Good lecturer and really helpful explaining concepts, calc 3 itself I found harder than the other two but he made it a lot easier. York and Shabazz gave 3% of extra credit this semester which really helped out. The exams are worth a lot though, I had an A for the whole semester until exam 3 so make sure not to fall behind.

analysis.name: Youping Chen
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hard to understand, atendance is mandatory. She'll be no help in learning the material but she gives helpful tips for what will be on the exam. Know how to do the homework problems and the practice exam. She gives 10 point extra credit for every exam so that's helpful. She is a blight on the engineering department

She was very hard to understand during lectures. In addition to her accent, she started wearing a mask about halfway through the semester which made understanding her twice as hard. Otherwise, she is a decent teacher. Exams are graded lightly with an additional 10% added on to each exam if you do the extra credit. Cares a lot about students

Lectures were basically pointless other than getting attendance credit. She was very hard to understand, spoke fast, and had pretty bad handwriting, so you would actually gain nothing trying to listen during lectures. Only hope is to read the book and learn yourself. She does give exam redos for extra points which does help out a lot.

Quite possibly the most useless professor at UF. Not only does she speed through lectures to the point where it's impossible to keep up, she doesn't prepare well enough for lectures to adequately answer questions when students ask them. Her exams and final project are also ridiculous, as she's just as unclear about how to approach them.

Understanding her in lectures was extremely difficult. Her exams would often have the same questions she did as examples in class, so it's great to have paid attention during lectures. She allows a formula sheet during exams that you can write anything on. Write class examples. Homework was tough for sure. She allows exam corrections for points tho

analysis.name: John Yelton
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Yelton has by far been the best teacher I've had. It's really easy to tell he puts a lot of work into his class because of all the demonstrations he does. He's a bona fide genius, and wants to see you do well and keep you engaged. However, he does move very fast, so I would recommend not skipping his class.

When I took Physics 1, I was faced with a major life event that distracted me from school. Professor Yelton was beyond caring. I was scared to approach him because, to me, he was just a face that delivered lectures to 600+ students. But he really listened and was willing to work with me while still grading fairly.

he's pretty funny during lecture; he has a dry sense of humor. he explains concepts well and does relevant sample problems during class. there is also iclicker 5% extra credit. do practice exams and understand the concepts discussed in class. if you just know how to do the math and don't understand the conceptual aspect, you will not do well.

YELTON IS AMAZING!!  If you have to take physics at UF, try your hardest to get him.  If you have to wait a semester to make sure you get him, do it.  He makes jokes (and they're actually funny), very clear in his explanations and just makes you want to come to class when he's the one teaching.

1/3 professors I had for phy2 w/calc, he was easily the funniest. He taught the fundamentals so the difficulty of his lectures vs the other two is not fair to compare. The 3 exams in this class are extremely difficult and worth 25% of your grade each. Hours studying left me with slightly above avg results, despite my pretty strong understanding.

analysis.name: Zhifeng (James) Chen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tests consisted of key terms from lecture/textbook (he gives you a list of them in advance) and analysis of primary/secondary sources that we went over in class. The lectures can be fast and dense, if you get the big picture it's alright. Lot of readings, but they were really interesting! Slow grader, but a good lecturer that wants you to succeed.

Professor was condescending and impatient with student questions/concerns. Pulls very vague impossible details from books on quizzes and tests every/every other week. Office hours did not help, email gets you no where. Accused students of cheating with no basis. Multiple students withdrew mid-semester from distress. It's not worth it - AVOID!

Worst class i have ever taken. Does not give clear instructions. NO TECHNOLOGY ALLOWED. Good luck on the quizzes, they are the most obscure terms and questions you'll ever see. Lectures are almost obsolete and does not matter to any of the essays or quizzes. Everything graded is on the textbook or the two books you read for the class.

He is a friendly professor, but he takes forever to grade and frequently does not provide feedback for why he is grading you as harshly as he is. Unless you are physically in his office for office hours, he will not respond. Ignores emails, grades harshly, and does not teach the material that you are expected to master.

professor will not answer questions, accuses multiple students of cheating to be proven wrong, gives 0 guidance and will tell you to figure it mout when asked for help. rather than helkping you he will tell you to drop the course. should not be teaching at the University of Florida

analysis.name: Gaia Zori
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Zori was one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. Her class was fairly easy with weekly group assignments, one individual paper, and one group presentation. She had two exams, both with extra credit and open-note quizzes.
She is extremely kind and one of those few teachers who enjoys her job. Her class was low stress and fair exams and assignments. I wish she was my teacher for every class.
Great professor. She is very knowledgable on the topics she teaches. She cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. It is an engaging, debate-structured class.

Dr. Zori is one of the best professors I have ever had!! She loves to teach, and it really shows, she is very knowledgeable, understanding, and helpful. She wants you to succeed. I cannot say enough good things, take any and every class of hers you can!
Dr. Zori's expectations for assignments were very clear and she is a very fair grader. The class is structured as a debate with 500 word reflections afterwords.

analysis.name: Andrew Zimmerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class. I needed something for my Science credit and expected a class called Oceanography to be manageable at the least, but it's unexecpectedly (and unecessarily) hard. Professor Zimmerman does not seem to understand that most students are only taking the class to fulfill a credit, and the class seems to be overly hard. Don't take.

Exams are 72% of your grade. Very hard to get full credit on exams. Extra credit of 2% offered for going on field trip. I studied for hours for the first 2 exams and it will be hard for me to get an A with only one exam left. Discussions and exercises are easy and quick to do. I would not take him again because of the grading scale, but nice guy.

The exams are just sm harder than you would think for a class titled, "oceanography." I went to almost every lecture and just still did not do well. He offers extra credit but like idk. Take something easier, it is not worth it.

I took this class for my gen ed for science, and it turned out to be way harder than expected. His lectures are very important to pay attention, and only some of the information you need to memorize is given on the study guide. You should really memorize the practice questions given in lectures and the study guide questions.

Took this class for my gen ed science course, and it turned out to be much harder than expected. Tests were basically your entire grade, and they were hard. Make sure you look over provided practice test, and rely heavily on in class practice questions. Extra credit was given to raise grade 2%.

analysis.name: Alex York
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 103 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was a great class! The lectures are kind of boring and the homework takes a long time, but I think this class works really well being online. Spend maybe 2 or 3 hours a day (including the 1hr lecture) and you should be fine. Exams are very fair and straightforward, but be weary for tricks!

Busywork, busywork, busywork!! Next to zero extra credit, exams are weighted heavily. Homework is incredibly time-consuming. His Summer C lectures were disorganized and sometimes quite long. Expect a fairly straightforward but time-consuming class. Exam content is straightforward, but this class feels more like applied precalculus than calculus.

Bang average professor, long boring lectures he zips through without much explanation half the time. Homework takes a ludicrous amount of time to do for what the content is. That being said, the class concepts are not hard. Just be ready to spend 3 hours on one unit between the lecture/lecture quiz/hws.

The lecture videos were good means of learning, but they were monotone and boring especially with the long lectures at the end of the course. The exams are weighted heavily, but the exams are easy if you take the time to study and do practice exams that are provided.

There are about 2-3 lectures per week, and each lecture has a 10-20 question homework as well as a quiz with 3-5 questions. The tests are exactly like the quiz questions and are pretty easy. I never had to interact with the prof during the course because it was online and I had no technical difficulties. The beginning of course is easy, end is meh.

analysis.name: Aaron Zubia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very intellectual professor, not a super interesting dude though and lectures are slow and fairly boring. Super fair grader, fun reading topics and very helpful in terms of feedback. Understanding, forgiving and nice guy, class was very straight forward you'll get a good grade with any amount of effort.

He is smart, but as smart as he is, he is twice as boring. Also, if you're a conservative, he will like you more. It is not super noticeable, but he tries to have some gotcha moments if you lean more liberal on the topics we're discussing. But he does foster good discussion, and I never felt super uncomfy giving my opinion.

Wouldn't recommend this class. Very reading-heavy and you will find yourself getting more work from this class than any other (quizzes, reflections, etc). While Dr. Zubia is funny and knowledgeable, he doesn't provide any kind of clear grading rubric & the material is unorganized, so students often have to remind him to upload the assignments.

The readings are a lot. Though they weren't too bad in and of themselves, I often found the quizzes to be more based on memorization of the texts rather than comprehension. That said, Dr. Zubia is an amazing professor and very intelligent. He works to make himself available outside of class, and there is extra credit later on that really helps.

This class had the highest amount of readings and the most difficult ones of any class I've taken. There are also quizzes every week. That being said, he cares about his students. If you go to office hours and engage respectfully in class, you can get a good grade. It will also GREATLY prepare you for any high-level poli-sci course.

analysis.name: Zulma Zayas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Makes you buy a $90 dollar course subscription to get all your homework, quizzes, and tests on top of the tuition you're already paying and converted some assignments to harder, in-person versions to make "grading easier", even though all the homework, quizzes, and exams are automatically graded. Just making things harder for students ultimately.

Yary is truly the best professor I've had at UF. Her enthusiasm and energy created an environment I genuinely looked forward to every day. Even when attendance wasn't required, I still chose to go because I enjoyed the class so much. ASL 1 isn't a difficult course when you put in the time and effort. So grateful I took ASL with her!!!!

Professor Santiago's lectures are very fun and engaging. Classes are canceled fairly often and attendance is not mandatory. Everything is accessible online if you miss class and she's really easy to reach through email or office hours if you struggle with anything or have any questions. I had a great experience and plan to take ASL 2 with her too!

Professor Yary is by far one of the best professors I've had at UF. I had her for both ASL 1 and 2, and her care for the language is evident through her teaching. She is great at explaining signs and will always take the time to answer any question you may have. You can tell she loves what she teaches.

Don't take this course with this professor if you suffer from ANY anxiety. The professor was rudely snapping and groaning at me because I had struggled to sign my name during the first week of class and that behavior continued throughout the semester. So many days I left embarrassed and on edge due to her teaching style.

analysis.name: Jindrich Zapletal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have never heard the word "ah" more times in my short existence on this earth before entering into this man's lectures. I would strongly recommend against taking any class of his, as you will be on your own as far as the material goes.

Dr. Zapletal seemed as if he absolutely hated having to teach students. I recently discovered that he is tenured and that helped to explain his attitude. I'm not sure if he had an accident of some sort or if he genuinely has terrible public speaking skills but he stutters like it is his job. It is very difficult to understand him in lectures.

Makes lectures and content pretty digestible and generally easy to understand. Follow along with the textbook and make sure you can do lecture and homework problems on your own. He provides one sample exam for each of the midterms and the final, pretty realistic in difficulty level to the actual exams. Witty guy + keeps it interesting. Fair grading

The class isnt too bad, for what it is, considering the other lecturer provided all other resources and information. Zapletals lectures were, however, awful. I couldnt focus on anything through his speech impediment, and often left feeling more confused about the subject matter.

Prof Zapletal is alright... your grade is based off three exams and six homeworks, so its very easy to quickly drop to a low grade. His lectures arent very clear, and some complicated proofs that dont show how to complete basic proofs using the theorem. Personally, the textbook didnt help me much either, so I had to rely on outside sources.

analysis.name: Yong Zeng
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are meaningless; I went to class. I believe one would've done better self-studying the entire class than listening to him. Originally had 6 homework assignments, but reduced it to 5, leading to less buffer for grade. Talks more about research than the actual class itself. Had extra material to go over, so he had class during reading days.

Dr. Zeng is a very kind professor and was very responsive via email. Grades are based off 2 midterms + 1 Final, which is primary based on chapters 20-26. His lectures were informative but really had no benefits to me doing well on the exams. If you're passionate about chemistry take him. The final exam at the end is challenging but fair. Good luck!

Professor Zeng's lectures are just screenshots and snippets of the book read out, which are not at all helpful.  His grading is very inconsistent, with points being deducted on homeworks for no discernable reason.  There was a large amount of extra credit at the end of the course.

Half of the material overlapped with statistics and gen chem, but I often left class feeling confused. He's kind but doesn't explain content well--definitely read the textbook. Grade is only based on four exams, each with 20 MCQ and sometimes a short response, and you get to drop your lowest exam grade. Few useful practice questions are given.

Dr. Zeng didn't explain material clearly. It felt like it was a better use of time to skip lectures and read the textbook instead. His material was mostly about statistics and a deeper dive into chem 2 topics with a small section on chemistry instruments. Your grade is based on  3 exams and the final, but 1 of them can get dropped.

analysis.name: Lisha Zhou
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this class in Fall semester 2024. Overall, the class was relatively easy. It definitely helps to have prior coding experience coming in as the first few weeks were essentially teaching you how to use an IDE and how to code in python. Labs are easy, exams are kinda hard, and don't procrastinate on projects. They are really long.

Her lectures are hard to understand, her grading is so strict, definitely not beginner friendly. However she is available a lot after class but beware of the queue. Take this class if you started coding in the womb. If not, do yourself a favor and skip

This review is for CDA 3101--wasn't an option in the RMP drop-down menu.   Prof. Zhou is easily one of the most caring and responsive professors that I've had.  She goes far out of her way to make learning comfortable and enjoyable for everyone.   I will absolutely take a course with her again if I have the opportunity.  Inspirational!

I didn't rely much upon her teaching abilities, but the class structure is excellent. The projects and labs blend together the material quite well. As long as you are able to keep up it is manageable and even easy. Plenty of extra credit.

workload is insane for a intro class. she doesn't curve bc the average on the tests is around a 70%, but she doesn't consider that most people already have prior experience, and the people who don't get screwed. projects take forever, there's a lab every week, and you don't get a moment to rest and catch your breath.

analysis.name: Ashish Aggarwal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He did a great job teaching MATLAB and showing students how to problem solve and think outside of the box. Office hours are always available and the TA's will be a tremendous help with any trouble you're having. The exams are fair and the final project is fun and rewarding. I loved the class.

Having him as one of my first professors was lwk a bad first impression of what college professors would be like. Ashish was one of the best instructors I have ever had. Teaching a programming language is not easy, but he makes it easy. If you attend all lectures and actually do the assignments, you will be perfectly fine in this class.
This guy is genuinely top 5 all time. He made my first semester at UF sunshine and rainbows. I had no idea how good I had it until second semester rolled in (Prog 2). I'll miss you Ashish.

Oh, where do I start? Ashish Aggarwal, you are a beacon of sunshine in the otherwise dull atmosphere of CISE. Ashish's lectures are simply beautiful: thorough, engaging, and to the point. His exams are as fair as they get. If I could have Ashish teach all of my classes, I would. If you think there is a better professor than Ashish, think again.

Amazing Professor! He genuinely cares about his students and goes out of his way to make sure that you are understanding the material and doing well in the class. He explains things thoroughly and makes sure you grasp the concepts and are prepared for the exams. He will stay after class to help you and he has a lot of office hours!

analysis.name: Agnes Leslie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Leslie's Lectures are fun and extremely engaging; however, her grading criteria is not clear, which ended up costing me my grade in the long run. She would mark points off for criteria explicitly listed in the rubric, but often the expectations were too vague. Even after completing extra credit, I ended the class with a B+.

Cannot recommend Dr. Leslie enough, seriously the most interesting class and her lectures are wonderful. She is an absolute wonder to have as a professor, and super accessible if you have questions. If you are thinking about taking her, please do!

If you respect your time do not take this class because Dr. Leslie will not. Readings can exceed 150 pages a week and then won't even be referenced during the long droning lectures but will feature on exams. The guidelines are inconsistent and unclear and Dr. Leslie is more then content to hold you accountable for her mistakes and risk your GPA.

I absolutely loved Dr. Leslie. She is so passionate about her class, always smiling, and has a positive attitude. She does a lot of class discussions and assigns readings, but they are really interesting if you pay attention. You get out what you put into this class. Easy A, but I learned a ton.

analysis.name: Pasha Agoes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He truly cares. Passionate. He extended deadlines, the work was really not difficult. In-class Canvas quizzes every 1-2 weeks, discussion post, some writing assignments, in class paper midterm exam, and a group final project. The midterm is mainly from the textbook. He gives study guides. Small discussion style class. So understanding and funny.

Dr. Agoes was very disrespectful and I felt talked down to when asking for help. He was extremely unresponsive to emails. I was very frustrated all semester taking his course. I normally see the best in everyone, and maybe he was going through something, but I have never felt more disrespected by a professor before. My classmates felt the same way.

He is kind and takes time to get to know his students. There is minimal work, and instructions are clear. The midterm was kinda random and took a bit of studying, but it wasn't too bad overall. Attendance is mandatory, and the class is discussion based. Discussions got oddly political a few times, which was weird, but overall I would take it again.

I would 10/10 take a course with Dr. Agoes again. He is such an easy grader and really makes it difficult to fail his class. He is very strict on deadlines though, so just make sure you have your work in on time and don't ask for any extensions and you should be good to go.

Dr. Agoes is one of the best profs I have had at UF. He cares about the success of his students and is extremely accessible for help. Extremely understanding! Clear syllabus and grading structure. Grades fair and quick. 10/10 would take another class with Dr. Agoes. Really remarkable as a professor.

analysis.name: Aghane Antunes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's a writing intensive class so lots of papers, but love her! She's super chill and a very fair grader. Highly recommend taking her class. Easy A if you do all your work.

Took this as my 6,000 word class and it was easy! Probably 1 or 2 hours of work per week depending on that week's assignment. If you took APHG in high school, it will be a breeze. There's discussion posts weekly, a few bigger papers (~1,000), other random assignments, and a group project. Didn't feel like a burden at all and prof was very nice!

Great professor that kept the class very easy. Only four essays, all under 1000 words, and the weekly discussion of 250 words, which was pretty easy. One group project that doesn't take long. Very easy to work with and has a 24-hour grace period for submitting assignments late but has accepted later assignments and still gave me 100%.

Great Professor, don't have one negative thing to say about her. Very accessible outside of class and very understanding when I missed an assignment (still got full points). Very simple ppt group project. Discussion post and quiz once a week. Short papers about once a month. Whole class was organized well and assignments were well outlined.

I took this class since I needed 6,000 word credit class. However, I found that the # of words we had to write was WAY more than 6,000. We had large projects (1,000+ word essays, presentations, etc) and discussions due each Monday. They were relatively easy/she is not a tough grader, but I would not recommend to anyone just looking for word credit.

analysis.name: Agata Kowalewska
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Summer B was the first time this course changed.  It is no longer an easy class.  I took this class because I wanted to take a break from my other classes, but I am ending up doing more work for this class than my other two classes combined.

Lots of homework that have nothing to do with the material that students are tested on. Study guides are rather broad whereas the tests themselves are very detailed/specific, so don't rely on on the guides either. Beware of ProctorU. If you're just looking to satisfy a gen ed credit, I strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

Lots of readings 200+ pgs. 15 modules with at most an hour of videos and an hour and a half of reading. Skipping videos are not suggested because some are not covered in the book. Gives extra credit that's already provided to you. Exam is multiple choice and T/F with detailed questions. You have to work for a B unless you pick things up quickly.

Easy class? Not anymore. You have to read a lot of pages and watch a lot of videos. Just took my first exam and it was really nit picky. I watched and read everything but ended up getting a D on my first exam. Memorize details and scientific terms.

As I am getting close to completing her course, I came to the conclusion:  1. Lecture videos are painful to watch. 2. Quizzes cover modules from the textbook almost every time 3. Exams are tricky, and sometimes seem that were written by someone who wants the student to fail. Mostly, they are not based on her textbook, rather on a mix of books.

analysis.name: Tolulope Agunbiade
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: To the person that said "they're not ready for a UF education if they complain about Dr. A", I have a 3.8 GPA. But pop off I guess? Dr. A isn't TERRIBLE. She's just disorganized and sometimes goes back on what the syllabus says in terms of exams and quizzes. It's an annoyingly tedious class.

This class is very unorganized. You have a quiz each week that you only get 5 minutes to answer 5 questions and these quizzes dont follow the syllabus. The term paper is graded on two different rubrics we got little guidance on. There have been many times where the modules werent uploaded in time. This class is stressful.

HORRIBLE, AVOID. She litreally does not have an idea of how to respond to emails for feedback. She first said I will respond to emails asking for feedback, then later sends an even vaguer email to the entire class which confused more than it helped. Her TAs are useless, take off points for no good reason, INCOMPETENT!!!

Dr. Agunbiade is very friendly and the TA, Nicholas Martin, is awesome. There are academic review papers that need to be read and write a reflection every week. You also need to work as a group to study one chosen disease over the semester as in many projects. It was an interesting class and not as hard as I thought. It's a good Quest 2 class.

There are exams and weekly quizzes. The class is a decent amount of work so be prepared to put in a few hours. Dr. A is a nice person, but her class is unorganized. However, she is willing to work with students and hear you out.

analysis.name: Pauline Aguinalde
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Loved the professor and class. There is a lot of material, but the exams are straightforward, and she gives extra credit opportunities. Super interesting topics, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. I would 100% take this class again

Such a nice professor who genuinely cares about her students. The class is content-heavy but so manageable. Minimal homework besides studying for exams which are straightforward. Would definitely recommend this class and professor

Great professor. Extra credit opportunities for tests, in class test review, no final exam (final project that is broken down throughout the semester). You can tell she is passionate about teaching and loves the subject. Easy A class.
I would highly recommend this professor. The class itself is content heavy so it is fast-paced but absolutely manageable. Interesting topics and exams are very straightforward.

analysis.name: Shubhi Agarwal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I attended every lecture in the beginning and could barely understand her.  Additionally, she treated us like high schoolers and would call us out for being on our phones/talking.  Mid semester, I stopped attending class because I quite honestly found it pointless.  I got the same score on my second exam as I did on the first, proving my point.

Professor Agarwal genuinely care about the success of her students, and want them to learn as much as possible in her class. However, her lectures are very confusing and it is periodically difficult to understand her. I feel like she over-complicates an already complicated subject. She is very accommodating in grading as she curves the grades.

Professor Agarwal is a very nice lady and is super passionate about economics, but she is a terrible teacher. I attended every single lecture in fear of getting behind and 90% of the time I had no idea what she was talking about ever. She goes way too fast so it's incredibly difficult to take organized notes or understand anything.

There's nothing necessarily wrong with Professor Agarwal, but I won't take her classes ever again. Her lectures were boring and hard to understand, so I stopped attending at some point and just read the textbooks. Now don't get me wrong, she is a nice person. If you go to her office hours, she will try to be as helpful as she can.

She knows what she is talking about and delivers the material in a concise and targeted way that makes it extremely digestible. Never read the textbook, just participated in class. Her problem sets are not difficult at all and she is also a very lenient grader and wants her students to succeed. I would take her class again!

analysis.name: Dror Abend-David
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I've taken three classes with Dror throughout my college career. The first as a first semester freshman and the last as a spring semester junior. He has taught me in and out of the classroom very important lessons about life. I enjoyed going to his class and participating. I have the utmost respect for him as a professor and as a person.

Very cool teacher, doesn't stick to the syllabus really but you end up learning something. Grading is a bit weird but if you listen in class it shouldn't be hard at all to get an A. Would definitely recommend.

disorganized, no lesson plan,class time is wasted with games that has no pedagogical reflection,deducts large grades for innocent mistakes, never accept grades negotiation even if all class agreed he is wrong. ask us to prepare no. of pages and the next day he teaches other pages,a very easy course was converted into a hard and stressful.

I took Yiddish Language & Culture. The class was easy, especially if you already know the Hebrew alephbeth (or alefbeys), or any German. The lessons are taken directly from the textbook (can be found as a PDF). There were only 4 other people in the class (!!!) when I took it, so you could choose to accelerate your studies almost one-on-one, or not.

Dror has mandatory attendance, which is necessary as the only way students would attend his dry lectures. He likes to stand up front and talk the entire class, with the occasional calling on students or pairing us into groups. Despite the heavy lectures, you won't feel particularly knowledgeable when you leave. The essays are vague but graded easy.

analysis.name: Abdoulaye Kane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Becoming Black is absolutely one of the easier Quest 1 classes, considering the horror stories I've heard from others. The readings aren't anything crazy, but you are expected to submit thoughtful questions for discussions. Lectures are nothing super special, but you can tell Dr. Kane loves what he does.

Love Kane! He was always understanding and easy to reach outside of class, and also passionate and well-versed in what he taught. The class is reading heavy. I skimmed most of them. Weekly is question actually a lot of ur grade. Grading is subjective, and based on TA. The TA was Ryan Cousins was cool and funny, but don't expect a free 100 on them!

No final exam, just an essay and a presentation. Few other essays but grading was free. Every week was a reading you could skim and you had to come up with a question for the discussion on Fridays. Reading was dense but you didn't need to know much. Lectures were kind of boring so I did work for other classes. He is passionate and talks a lot.

Great class. Workload is super light. Prof is so willing to help his students and his passion for his work really shows. Wonderful readings. If you happen to not be able to do them then the lectures summarize them. There's only one exam and he's a super lenient grader. Otherwise, it's pretty much a paper, presentation, and small quizzes.

The lectures didn't have much to do with the assignments we had to do, but attendance was mandatory. There are some short response papers and at the end of the semester there was a very open essay and group project. It seemed like if you did it, you would get a good grade. It is evident he cared though and was thoughtful during lectures.

analysis.name: Amr Abd-Elrahman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher! Very helpful.  He is a long distance teacher, at least for my course, and he was always available to take calls, emails, etc for GIS questions!  Slight accent, but better than almost all other professors at UF.
Is extremely thorough when teaching, takes an unnecessarily long time to explain things. Classes have alot of work but you can get help easily.

Review for SUR3641 - survey computation class. Very fair grading and curves class. If you show up, show your work, and have understanding of the problem the grades will reflect that. Gives credit for coherent attempts. Fast grader and will provide extra time and feedback if needed. Homework is heavy and lots of spreadsheets. Good exp. overall.

Grading scale is so biased toward not getting an A from this course, as if, the aim is not to learn, but to get any grade less than A. Assignment rubrics are not in detail and you get your points deducted for something that was not asked in the assignment.
Overall, I do not recommend this course.

The professor is very knowledgeable and helpful. The course can be demanding at first, but once you advance in the course you just follow the system smoothly. The professor answers students' questions efficiently and quickly. I also learned GIS! I recommend taking this course with Dr. Amr.

analysis.name: Rock Aboujaoude Jr
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
The one thing you gotta understand about Professor Rock, is he's very descriptive on each energy development module of the class. He teaches in a way that made us feel like he was guiding rather than lecturing, unlike many other professors in this department. 

He also uses a lot of Lord of the Rings memes and references 

10/10
I loved Rock!  He was clear about instructions and always took time from his day to help when we had questions.
Rock was the best TA I have ever had! During office hours he would always be available to help with readings and even met with me outside of class many times.

analysis.name: Abdolkarim Asghari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: MCB3020 with Asghari was the best class I could've chosen to take alongside Orgo 1 in terms of manageability. I used Smokin Notes to study and I think it was CRUCIAL to my success. Dr. Asghari was a great professor! All the lectures are online, and he posts slides to accompany the videos. I used Smokin Notes to study for the exams, and it helped me do well and understand the content.

Super nice professor overall, and you could tell that he definitely cared about what he was teaching. His lecture videos were a bit confusing, but the study guides helped a lot. The exams were pretty straight forward, and I barely used SmokinNotes.

analysis.name: Zhanar Abil
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
