review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR FOR GENETICS. She made this class 10x more difficult than it needed to be. First, she gives a final which not all professors do. The exams, except the final, were multiple choice AND short answer. The short answer was extremely difficult (ie. one question asked to draw transcription, like tf???). Very nice women though.

Read straight from the slides.  When I asked her to explain test questions she essentially restated what the answers were without adding any other information.
After publicly stating on canvas that the test scores were far worse than she wanted or expected, she just said "oh well" and submitted grades.  No curve, no extra credit, nothing.

Class wasn't difficult material wise, but it's a lot, and receiving an A is nearly impossible. Prepare to STUDY. LONG textbook. You need a 94 to obtain an A, which meant small wiggle room in this exam heavy class. Hated the group project; graded harshly by TAs, which I felt was unfair. This class caused me a lot of stress. But very nice professor.

Here's the strat:

1. 10/20 lectures for 1% of the grade, up to you to allocate your time.
2. Have the self-discipline to make sure you understand the material
3. iClicker and past test questions make up the exams
4. Textbook and slides are more than enough to gauge what you need to know
5. 94% is an A but it's manageable
6. Do homework, it's light

Extremely bad lecturer, she does not even seem interested in the topic she is teaching, and lectures for two hours in a monotone voice. I was not even going to bother writing a review but even after being a horrible professor and claiming that grade curving was up to her discretion, she would not give me .5% to bring my grade to an 80.

analysis.name: Abigail Held

review_highlights.comment: You can tell Professor Held is passionate about chemistry but she lacks organizational skills. Take another prof

She was just okay. I dont think I got too much homework, but learning from lectures were hard. Sometimes it was just the TA and it was hard to hear at times. The homework (ALEKS) was a waste of time. She didnt give out any practice exams to study from so for the 4 exams it was hard to study.

I thought this class was pretty challenging considering it is only an intro level chem class. Professor Held was very caring but often times I got confused during her lectures. Truthfully study edge is what got me to fully understand the material.

analysis.name: Laura Acosta

The SWEETEST most caring professor I've had. Her exams are very fair, and the material is interesting. Take her if you can!!

Such an amazing human aside from teaching. Very caring and makes material so interesting and helps students without making us feel bad. I think if I paid attention more during class instead of cramming I could've gotten an A. Exam averages were literally 95%, she's amazing

Dr. Acosta was such a wonderful teacher. This was an Honors Uncommon Read course, and I honestly didn't know what to expect, but Dr. Acosta was warm and genuine from the start. Dr. Abrams is amazing. Everyone complains about how hard her class is, but come on it college what did you expect? She is the first professor that has truly challenged me, and I love her for it. Great lecturer & loves to call people out when their arguments don't make sense.

For a Quest 1 course that is mainly for freshmen to take, she expects more than just introductory college level writing, more like philosophy major level writing. She can be pretty vague in terms of expectations and criteria for papers. Very nice person and was very understanding for COVID. Also great lecturer. Just wished she graded better.

I LOVE PROFESSOR JANOWICH! Hes honestly the nicest teacher ever. He always compliments students no matter their experience level and makes sure to point out the things you did right while also giving valid critiques. I hated waking up early but this class made it worth it. My favorite class ive taken BY FAR. He really helped boost my confidence��

Most chill, helpful, and supportive guy ever. We love King Ronald. If I catch you talking bad on him I'm swinging. He finds the good in everything you turn in and never berates you if you mess up, can't find time to finish an assignment, accidentally sleep past class (oops), etc. Also super knowledgeable on artists and techniques. Light of my life.

Ron is so laid-back that he is almost horizontal. Put forth some good effort and you'll be happy with your grade, but it is up to you whether you will just go through the motions or actually try to learn something and create decent portfolio work.
Ron is a great professor. He gives you great feedback and many helpful tips. He wants to see you do well in the class. I feel like I have actually learned a lot in this class.

analysis.name: Ron Chandler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Chadler is an absolute gem! He is knowledgeable, cares for his students, and is always available for a chat. The class is super easy; there is no homework (everything is done in class), no quizzes, tests, or a final exam (instead, one really meaningful gratitude assignment at the end). Attendance is 50%, though, so don't miss class. Take it!!

Easiest psych class I have taken. The material was very inspirational and easy to understand. Very easy A, and almost everyone ends up with over a 100% in the class due to extra credit at the end. Weekly work is very easy, and you barely have to think about the class outside of lecture. Group work and one scary presentation, but very easy. Take it!

One of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever met. Takes time to get to know every student beyond the classroom and class is very interesting and fun. The TA I had was also fantastic and so sweet. Ending with a 104%, everyone should take this class if they can. The fact Chandler doesn't have a 5/5 is shocking.

Positive psych: don't get the textbook.  This is the easiest class you'll ever take.  I found the whole thing depressing, which I know is ironic.  The whole premise of the class is how to find the meaning of life in a worldview that rejects meaning.  Take the class, it's easy, but be prepared to do no critical thinking at all otherwise you'll hurt.

I enjoyed Professor Chandler. The class was an easy A and he cared about the success of his students. However, the lectures were short and often taught by his TAs. Everything was graded by the TAs too. Its a good class; nothing hard at all, but you hear more from undergrads than from the professor. No exams, just simple individual and group papers.

analysis.name: Aaron Karlson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor will not grade anything until the very very last day of the semester. Be mindful of this when taking one of his classes.

The work is steady until the last 5 weeks, then it leaps in difficulty. He will take the time to do office hours but he constantly says go back and watch the lecture even when you explain you didn't understand the lecture.

Mr. Karlson's first concern is the success of his students; he responds to questions promptly and with detail, no matter how trivial the question may seem at times. He also encourages students to review material on their own to improve their skill with Maya, which is incredibly helpful. He cares deeply about his students and is an amazing professor

Professor Karlson is amazing! The level of difficulty of this class is high, but its not about him, its just the learning curve of Maya is pretty steep... make sure you attend the lectures and start your assignments ahead; animation takes time. He will answer questions super fast and gives great feedback... Again, start your homework on TIME

Professor Karlson's class was a joy to attend every time! 3D Animation was super fun, and he made the lectures hilarious and a great time to be in. The class itself was hard, but that comes with learning Maya and animation, if you've never done it before. He was super caring and was good at feedback, so don't be afraid to reach out to him!

analysis.name: Sean Adams
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is not the easiest class, but it's one of those where you look back and are glad you took it. Adams was very helpful and passionate about history. He really pushes you on the writing component, but this helps prepare you tremendously for other classes you take down the road. A lot of reading (up to 100 pages/week) but I'd take this class again

I had Dr. Adams three years in a row and took four classes with him. I can't recommend him enough. The lectures are engaging, his grading is clear and helpful, and overall a super understanding guy. He gives feedback on all papers, of which there are usually 3 major ones and several mini ones. The class grade is mostly those, and attendance.

Adams has good knowledge about the subject and uses it to make the lectures interesting. He gave quizzes that were easy if you just paid attention in class. I know he and someone else were grading assignments, and most of the time, there was good feedback.

Dr. Adams is awesome. Extremely interesting class with amazing lectures. 5 ~500-750 word short responses with 2 drops and 3 ~2000 word essays. There isn't enough room to say everything but Dr. Adams is extremely understanding and always fair. He even stayed 10-15 minutes extra after every class to talk to students and answer questions.

LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! Super informative and engaging lectures (don't skip the class!!) and gives great feedback on essays. Not a super harsh grader, but pushes you to do your best and expects you to use the feedback he's given on your next essay. Is incredibly fair and holds himself to same standard of deadlines and professionalism. 100% recommend!

analysis.name: Aaron Hill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would not recommend Professor Hill. While the material itself is not hard, we are graded on things such as "professionalism". I had a situation where I couldn't get in touch with any members of my Capsim team. He claimed that teammates not participating was part of the real world and deducted a full point off of my grade for reaching out to him.

This class is way harder than it should be. Lots of exam questions come from the minutiae of the expensive and very boring textbook. Very much a cookie cutter McGraw Hill class with lecture videos that are delivered robotically. Capsim group assignment was pretty good, however, I still would not recommend this class. Overall not worth the effort.

Disclaimer: I had technical issues for the first month of the semester, and it was hard for me to catch up on all my classes. That is why I gave it an average difficulty. The professor sends very thorough, helpful, and detailed weekly emails with reminders. You can tell he really cares about his students, and is a fair grader.

I found his class very straightforward, and he teaches many of the essential business concepts you may already know. There is a weekly lecture, smartbook, quiz, and group Capsim assignment (which is much harder than intl. business Capsim). There are many drops and grading procedures in your favor. I wish he had more practice material for exams.
Great and easy professor! Simple 3 online exams of 20 questions, 3 case studies, and a simulation. Can get away with dedicating only 40min a week to this class and get an A

analysis.name: Aaron Molstad
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Homework was fairly challenging, but about expected time consumption for a math class. Molstad cares and will help in OH and his lectures are alright. The practice exams are easier than the real exams, but the real exams were not god awful (still hard), but he curves and provides some extra credit. From this you can intuit that he is a solid choice

Teaches material well and is very helpful in OH. Some HWs are lengthy and midterm/final were 5-7 day take-home exams (it will take most of that time to do) but everything is fair. STA3032 was my only prereq which made some topics harder but its definitely doable with enough effort and I learned way more in this class than in eng stats.

Homework load not huge. Lectures very full of mediocre-ly explained material. Homework problems are difficult but manageable. Gives a practice exam that is similar, if not easier. Then exams are extremely difficult and different from homeworks and practice exam. I pay attention, do homework, take notes, study, and do awful on exams.

I struggled a lot with this class but Prof. Molstad was very helpful for clarifying material. Exams make up 70% of your grade but he does curve. Exams were difficult and were somewhat proof heavy which differed from the computational practice exams. Make sure you do all the homeworks and get the highest grades possible.

Dr. Molstad does his best to teach you the concepts and make sure you understand everything as you progress through his classes. I thoroughly enjoyed STA4504 and I would absolutely recommend taking it with him if you get the chance.

analysis.name: Jessica Aaron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The semester isn't even over and I have a lot of words to say about this. The class itself is poorly organized and most people complain that they don't ever know whats going on. Her slides are often incorrect and you end up teaching yourself from the textbook. It feels like you set yourself up for failure by taking this class.

She is a very nice teacher, and does try to help. However, if you ask something in class that she doesnt know, it becomes irrelevant. She couldnt teach certain concepts and you needed to rely on the book as your teacher. I was disappointed because I expected to learn more, she used anothers materials that she didnt always agree with, very confusing

I'm minoring in Spanish and have never made below an A in a Spanish class, but I'm all but confirmed to make a B in this class. Super frustrating professor for what should've been an interesting class.

Jessica Aaron is one of my all time favorite teachers! She is extremely knowledgable and is always looking for ways to make her class fun, interesting, and informative. However, she gives ALOT of reading, so DO NOT take her classes if you know you will NOT TAKE THE TIME TO READ.

had her for both SPN3700 &4930. she does a WAY better job at 4930, because in spn3700 she would contradict herself or ask the TAs to clarify, but was all over the place information-wise. book helps with 3700, and for 4930 it's a lot of reading, but as long as you get jist, you'll do fine on the essays. homeworks were on canvas & open notes.

analysis.name: Ron Gromoll
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gromoll has a lot of experience in the hospitality industry and was able to share these stories in each module in a way that related to the material at hand. Professor Gromoll was a great professor! The grading criteria was very clear and he graded assignments in a timely manner with constructive feedback. The class mainly consists of 500 word papers on the lectures given throughout the semester and assignments pertaining to career prep such as resume building and interview practice through Quinncia.

I was very anxious going into this semester and I'm ending the semester more confident, better prepared, and very excited for my future. While I didn't end up going the internship route, Prof. Ron's class was so worthwhile. The lecturers he brought in were amazing and it's not often you get a professor with so much job experience.

Professor Ron Gromoll- HANDS DOWN- the best hospitality professor at UF. I took him for LEI3360, LEI3992, and LEI4940. He gave amazing lectures and was so inspiring. He wants to see his students succeed. I recommend following him on LinkedIn, as he kept in touch with me right before his retirement and my upcoming graduation.
Ron is great and super helpful as you work to launch a career in hospitality. Make sure you will be able to make it to the designated class time as attendance heavily contributes to your grade.

analysis.name: Theodosios Aivalis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Dude the semester ends in one week and she has not graded a single thing. Our entire grade is pretty much one project that we add onto every week yet she has not graded a single submission. How do I know how I am doing if I get no instructor feedback?

analysis.name: Katerina Aifantis

very nice professor! she used examples to make things clearer and prepared us well for exams. was accommodating to unforseen difficulties of students. definitely recommend to take classes with her!

She prepares you very well for exams and gives a fairly light amount of homework (7 assignments for the semester, 2-5 hours each). She radiates kindness and is always willing to help, plus she rewards participation

The best professor I have had at UF. She is unbelievably caring and accessible outside of class time. She will even check your homework before you submit it so you can get a 100% every time. Her exams are fair and her lectures are great. I had a great experience in this class, and I hope to have her again. Highly recommend.

Prof Aifantis is great. Her class is interesting because she briefly focuses on the most relevant topics and then goes through a lot of examples. Exams are similar to homework and shes always available to answer questions by email. Would definitely take again!

analysis.name: Aicha Ouzia

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She deducts points without explaining why or what was wrong. She's awful at explaining the material. I'm taking the class online and even though she answers e-mails, she never actually helps you with the question you have. She makes it seem like explaining things is a hassle to her and she's busy to read attachments. She never provides written feedback or comments explaining why you got the grade you got.

There is little attempt to describe how the language operates and she will simply speak it as if you're already supposed to know. She'll get angry and stomp her feet if you phrase your sentences incorrectly or are hesitant to speak in class. There are many assignments due every day online and she won't care if you have technical difficulties.

analysis.name: Aida Hozic
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Waste of time. The readings and lectures are awful she rambles and treats everything as profound. She's an inconsistent grader taking points off for not being emotional enough or not saying exactly what she wants, even when it's not in the prompt. She claims not to care about AI but gives 0 based on suspicion alone and won't let you explain.

Professor Hozic is a nice lady. She seems to care about her students and really wants them to be satisfied as well as better off after the class. My biggest issue with her is that she can be quite snarky with feedback. She doesn't use rubrics and can be rather mean if you don't write with complexity or don't do the readings "justice" on quizzes.

-Harsh grader no rubric.
- Quizzes on content to be discussed in coming week make lectures feel unnecessary or unimportant to pay attention to.
- In lectures tends to ramble.
- attending office hours is basically mandatory if you want to succeed in this course- she will hate you if you don't and grade even harsher.

Overall a very caring and knowledgeable prof. Is a nuanced grader but always gave good feedback. Assignment explanations can feel vague at start but expectations are consistent. Readings were assessed before lecture started for the week, sometimes made lecture feel redundant even though attendance was required. Warm and accessible.

Professor Hozic is one of the best professors in the Poli Sci Department and made my time as a Poli Sci major much more enjoyable. She knows a ton about pretty much any subject and has a great wit, both making her classes very interesting, no matter the subject at hand. I had her for Divided Cities and Politics of the World Economy. Take a class.

analysis.name: AJ Jung
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!! Throughout my time in grad school this is the hardest grader i've had for no reason. Its frustrating because her grading is based off of opinions, so you have to guess what she will like. When I went to office hours she had little feedback and then ended up taking off many points for "potential changes."

Wow where do I begin, maybe avoid at all costs, maybe she shouldn't be teching this class when she isn't the best speaker.  She gives no guidance on grading and then tears you apart in the rubric.  This should be an easy class that helps you grow but I actually got nothing out of this BS.  She just tells you to make your slides more Mickey Mouse.

DONT take with AJ JUNG if you have any concern about public speaking. The way it is structured is like hazing/exposure therapy. Grades are extremely harsh and I've put more work into this than any other in my education only to maybe get a B. She does warn people with saying that she never gives out As and it is RARE to get an A on any assignment.

The "nobody is perfect" mindset to toxic extremes. Rubrics have no details but she has specific expectations. She'll arbitrarily mark off points because only a "perfect" speaker gets above a B. And perfect speakers don't exist. Appeals & office hours are a scam. I have lots of experience presenting professionally but now completely dread it.

Avoid this class if you can!! Professor Jung is a very strict grader and will contradict herself when grading assignments. Your grade is very subjective; she has very few office hour timeslots and takes 3-4 weeks to grade assignments. Don't bother disputing your grade because it can go down if she finds more errors.

analysis.name: Seun Ajoseh

Easy class. Light grader. Very accommodating and cares for his students' success.

The class is Tough, but the information is interesting.  It takes a little while to get use to his accent, but come to class because he notices.  Work through homework multiple times, read chapters.  Have questions in class and know general concepts.  Passing is easy, getting an A will be a LOT of work.
Horrible class format.  TA doesn't help whatsoever
can not understand a word he says!

analysis.name: Ajay Shanker
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shanker is a great professor. He assumes you know certain things that you should know prior to taking his class. He is a little difficult to understand but you can teach yourself if you cannot understand him. His test are open book, open notes, you can bring anything to them but they are still difficult. He really loves steel and concrete.

Doesn't teach any of the material for Homework or quizzes. Spends class time showing pictures of beams, trusses, etc. rather than teaching material. Supposedly has great powerpoints for lectures that he never uses. Very unclear regarding grading policy and what will be on the quizzes. Promised to drop 4 lowest quiz grades and is now refusing.

Dr. Shanker is a great human being and he cares about what he is teaching. However, it's time to call it a day for him. The lectures were often overshadowed by YouTube video noise that he could not hear. He also does not seem very efficient while using google chrome and canvas. I like him as a human being, but he's not a good professor.

While he may be monotone (w/ some accent) and hard to focus on for two straight hours, this class is not hard by any means. This semester, we had no exams; just open note/book/hw quizzes once per week. Quiz day depends on how many people are there, if we feel prepared, etc. (he's very lenient and will push things back if you ask). MANY DROPS TOO :D

For a real challenge on understanding and paying attention to a prof giving a lecture, this is your class. Dude's a good guy but he's the most horrendous professor I have ever taken. Class is completely unorganized. Word of advice, write as much as you can for notes and try to understand hws. Grade is all open notes quizzes. Textbook may help. Gl!

analysis.name: Apollo Amoko
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Amoko isn't universally popular among students. He's criticized as being condescending, too dense + boring of a lecturer, and too pedantic of a grader. This understandably turns off many students. But you may find, as I did, that you quite enjoy his insight and teaching style. If his class content appeals to you, I say give him a shot.

The instructions for assignments are vague and unclear. Feedback on essays isn't particularly helpful either. He's passionate, the content is interesting, but the class is unorganized, and he isn't very timely. If you need structure, he may not be the professor for you.

Do not take him! Please! I was warned, but I ignored it thinking it was just complainers who want easy A's and will complain about any professor who challenges them, but that is not the case. His lectures are disorganized, instructions unclear, and even though participation is a large part of your grade makes you want to sit in the back & be quiet.

Although unorganized, I have to say I did enjoy his classes. They focus more one the discussion and history behind the novels, which always took interesting turns. Many people on RMP think he's harsh and/or pretentious, but he honestly just has a dry sense of humor about him. He's a very smart guy and honestly very nice.

Very rude professor. His instructions for essays were very vague and his feedback was harsh and pretentious. He was very rude in class, cuts students off and tells them that their comments and opinions are essentially wrong. analysis.name: Amber Ross
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

It also means she doesn't talk about relevant material very much. 2 1/2 months since submitting my first paper and still don't have the grade back.

Professor Ross was unorganized and took almost a month to provide feedback on the paper. The essays are graded willy-nilly and are unnecessarily scrutinised way too hard. Not a single person got a 100% in participation.

Grading is fine but don't expect to learn anything of value. He's a super nice guy though.

lowkey one of the best professors i've had at uf. i was going through a rough term and missed a bunch of deadlines and talked to all my profs but he was the only one who actualy cared and worked with me and took extra time to help. super easy to talk to and very approachable. exams feel really fair too if you study

He so awesome. Super caring and exams are really fairly written. Lectures can be not the most engaging all the time but his care for teaching and students shines through. As long as you are willing to study a bit outside of class, I would highly recommend him as a professor.

Nice guy overall and you can tell he actually cares and listens. The class is hard and the subject is kinda boring, and you need a lot of practice, like a LOT. Still, everyone I know got an A. There are a lot of bonus point opportunities. Go to office hours and do the practice problems if you want to do well.

analysis.name: Ramon Aleman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 10/10 recommend this class to. this will sound dramatic but i couldn't have made it through this semester without the positive impact this course had on my mental health. I learned so much valuable information, finished with literally a 100% so everything is very easy, and Ramon is an incredible lecturer, teacher, and person.

Ramon was not only a great teacher, he was also there to support his students in any way necessary. I'm really glad I chose Stigma and Mental Health as my quest 2. The class was interesting and relevant to today's society. If you need an easy and fun quest 2, definitely take this one with Ramon.

Very easy, just need to show up and participate a few times in class. Mostly lecture and discussion based. Lectures can be boring but not difficult, and he plays video clips and documentaries throughout the course.

Probably the easiest A ever. Though this class was as gentle as possible talking about mental health, it does come with a trigger warning in my opinion. Sometimes the discussions felt a little aimless, but great discussions nonetheless

analysis.name: Jessica Allen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Allen has a very poor understanding of the content in the Dynamics course and consistently makes mistakes in class. When these mistakes are made she has been very unwilling to admit wrongdoing while being combative to many questions asked. A proffesor who so adamantly hates trig should not be teaching a course where it is so important.

She is so knowledgeable and wise Oh great teacher the wise was instrumental to my learning in this class and every day I had to enter the room was a great day the exams were fair and she made the material very fun to learn attendance is optional but she does not post recorded lectures and the notes are not the best if you do not have the context.

This great and wise professor was an integral part of the learning experience; lectures aren't recorded so show up and you'll benefit as she is a great teacher who makes the class very learnable; no textbook and exams reflect the content well so make sure you actually understand it before; would recommend Oh great teacher the wise to anyone

She is very passionate about dynamics and makes it pretty easy to understand, similar to physics 1. Exams, quizzes, and hws are all very reasonable. Attendance not mandatory and she posts the notes but there is a QR code for extra credit if you go to class

I took Dr Allen for Dynamics, and she made the class very simple and built the curriculum very well. She did QR codes in class that you could scan as your attendance to earn extra credit. Her homeworks were somewhat difficult at times, but never over the top.

analysis.name: Amie Baisley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You gonna learn nothing, trust! She knows what she is teaching, for sure, but she doesn't know how to teach nor give a clear and constructive feedback. She is accessible, but yet, her explanation is just her repeating herself from the 30 min lectures that she makes us watch. If you wanna learn something, not just copying stuff, don't take her class

Organized. Good, but full Office Hours. Unreasonable expectations. Expects you to know Matlab+No grades until the end of the year. You aren't going to be able to spend the 25 hours a week to finish the HW (not hard, but statics must be done on PowerPoint) + 10-70 hrs for each coding project (once a month) with 8+ page report (with proofs + words).

All the comments with Quality 1.0 and Difficulty 5.0 are accurate. So let me persuade you to not take this class. With this class, you will contemplate dropping out of college and you will get burnt out. The lectures you watch will be filled with jargon and the homeworks and projects will make you cry. Please don't take this class lol

Nice lady but don't take her. You don't get any useful instruction and are required to learn the topics by reading through 3 worked out problems per module. Unfortunately the worked out problems aren't well annotated + some calculation steps are skipped. Also, her method is very odd so you cant use outside resources to cross-reference the content.

Flipped classroom, except the material you're expected to review before helps little with the problems that you're expected to solve in class. Attendance is mandatory for homework sessions that you don't really get anything out of, and the grading system requires you to do everything her way or you'll lose credit despite a right answer.

analysis.name: Berkay Akyapi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not worry about buying book for QMB 4701. Go to class and take good notes will very easy if you do. Test are open excels which is super helpful. The Professor cares and dude is super chill. Go to office hours if you have questions. but he knows his stuff and this class is easy if you take good notes.

I really enjoyed having him as a professor for this class. He made everything as simple as he could and if you emailed any time even 9pm at night he responds within minutes with full explanations of a question you have. He was very helpful in office hours.

Berkay is a very fair professor that cares about students having a well rounded understanding of concepts. I have seen the same topics being taught by other professors seem more complex, but Berkay structures the content in a great way to learn. The exams can be challenging for some, but I believe they are very fair with the content in lectures.
My second time having a course with Professor Akyapi and he is a great professor! Make sure you go to class or you will be a little lost.

Berkay is a kind and caring professor. His lectures are extremely helpful with quizzes and exams. The first exam was super easy, but the second exam is really hard. He made most of the questions into trick questions with barely sufficient time. If you are confused, ask him because its easy to fall behind.

analysis.name: Fatima Akinola
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had her for Survey of Calc 2 which is an online course. The lectures were not that great and were not given by her. I needed study edge to get through the course. However, her grading criteria is clear with 3 lowest lecture quizzes being dropped and lowest exam grade being dropped. It was not that hard of a class and is very doable.

She was my professor/TA for Survey of Calc 2. The lectures were all Kevin Knudson, but her grading criteria was incredibly lenient. Lowest 3 quizzes and homework dropped, and lowest exam was dropped. I basically didn't do the last week's work and still ended the course with 100%.

This class was super manageable. The grading is very lenient, you have multiple attempts on pretty much every assignment, and the practice exams are very similar to the exam. I put very little time into this class and ended with an A because of the exam reviews she gave.

I am being completely sincere and not malicious when I say that she should resign as a TA.  She cannot, in good faith, continue. She consistently made errors during the explanation of problems. Every day she couldn't explain questions. She is very kind and passionate about math, but I cannot say she is an effective teacher.

She gave amazing lectures, and clear notes. She was super nice, and gave really good feedback. I'm terrible with trig, but I managed to pass the class with her notes. Attendance doesn't matter grade wise, but you gain a much better understanding going to class than just reading from the class notes.

analysis.name: Salah Algabli
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style is great! He makes sure that everyone understands fully, and when you can't answer a question, he helps you through it so nicely and understanding. He is great when it comes to teaching, and the activities in class are never too challenging. He understands that it may be everyone's first time learning Arabic. He is a great guy!

Really awesome professor for a homework heavy class. Definitely have to stay on top of coursework, but he makes things engaging with one zoom and one TA session a week. He is super understanding and you can tell he loves what he does

Dr. Algabli is an amazing professor. I've learned so much about writing research papers and about Arab culture. His lectures are engaging and fun, and he is very supportive, respectful, encouraging, and always willing to help and guide students.

Today is my graduation day, and I feel lucky to have him as my professor throughout my time at UF. From the very first course I took with him, I was inspired to keep enrolling in his classes every semester. He was a constant source of support, especially when it came to my PhD applications. When someone says "UF," it will always mean Dr. Salah.

Professor Salah is one of the most supportive and engaging professors I've had. He creates a respectful, welcoming space where students feel encouraged to grow. His classes are well-organized and thoughtful, and I learned a lot especially in terms of technology, creativity, and thinking in new ways.

analysis.name: Farah Akiely
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: idk why the rating is so low. urp3001 was so easy. all the quizzes and exams are on quizlet. the discussion were kind of long (theres 3) but as long as u follow the criteria and write about 800 words, its an easy A for those. and there is a group project but its pretty simple and short (2 slides). easy 3000 lvl class. just follow instructions well

This professor really isn't terrible. I was surprised at the amount of work for the course but it forces you to learn a lot. The course is just on urban planning issues since that's what Professor Akiely studies. The feedback on assignments was poor and vague, also graded harshly. The discussions were all high-level essays. Assignments are creative

Took a class that had two professors, and she was one of them. My experience with them was horrible. They are rude, condesending, and unnaccomodating. Some assignment critera they provide isn't always clear and they wont clarify, telling you to do as the rubric says. Even if you follow the rubric exactly, they will find ways to lower your grade.

Very tough grader, some expectations not listed in the rubric. Online class so there is basically no interaction with the professor. There is extra credit at the end of the semester but as long as you do the work and put in effort you shouldn't need to do it.
It was an online class so not much interaction with the professor. Very strict on grading and there was a lot of writing assignments in the class.

analysis.name: Elif Akcali
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Akcali is definitely one of the best professors I have had. She holds great lectures and knows how to keep a steady pace throughout. There are six quizzes, six homeworks, six in-class assignments and three exams.

Probably one of the best professors I've had at the University.  She is really helpful and all of her homework and tests are fair.  Very clear and gives you notes in class so you can follow along.  As long as you go to class and pay attention you should be able to get a A.

Mediocre teacher. She knows her material well. Every time I emailed her asking questions, she has ignored them. Sometimes in class can be condescending and/or arrogant to students at times, but like I said she knows her subject.
Fair grader. Always answers questions. Keep an eye out for her mistakes in class, point them out and she will fix them.
Excellent Teacher!  Very organized.  Her tests and homework are fair and she updates her website frequently.

analysis.name: Farah Akiely
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Akiely is great!
I had a health issue which made me fall behind in class work. She was very accommodating and reassuring. We met during office hours and she was very understanding.
Quizzes open for one day, I wish they open for longer. Grades are fair and based on rubric. It is an easy A, but has lots of work.

Decent elective. It is not difficult to get an A as long as you put work in. Quizzes and exams are not difficult if you use your resources. Discussion posts are lengthy and require citations but are graded fairly as long as you follow the rubric. Group project is tedious but fine if you have good group members. Overall interesting class material

Professor Akiely was a very tough grader. Discussion and group project instructions seemed clear, but she would take off points for not doing things that were not included in the instructions. I took this class as an elective, but I would not recommend someone to take it as an elective unless you had a true interest in these topics.

I enjoyed this elective. This course requires readings for quizzes and some work on the discussions, plus a group project. Getting an A is not very difficult. Discussions were the assignments that need some time and effort, and Farah was a very fair grader.

analysis.name: Akhil Kshirsagar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Do no read the textbook, it is the largest waste of your time. Go into each chapter and use quotes from their intros as evidence in your papers. Easy grading as long as you answer the prompts (which can be answered without any reading). The only test is only worth 10% of your grade and I just used quizlets I found to study for it. Overall EZ class.

You have 13 assignments, 6 quizzes w/2 attempts each 17%, 6 assignments 40%,+ 1 final exam (proctored) 43%. The quizzes are hard, question bank is from book chapters but the book is long winded and very hard to comprehend as well as the lectures. The 2 written assignments he is a picky grader and the final exam had questions not reviewed in course.

Getting 100 on every assignment without any study and effort. Just 5 min pre-recorded lecture per week, then write short essay and discussion. Final exam is somewhat unreasonable, bc he did not teach, but he curved it. All people I know in this course getting an A.

Terrible professor! He ignores students emails when asked about grading! Even when he is clearly wrong! For example, he gave me 0 marks for a criteria that states "Include reference section in APA format", which I did! Overall, terrible professor, and I would absolutely not recommend!

I don't know why this professor has a low rating... I got a ~100% on every assignment he manually graded. Only problem with the class were the quizzes, they're pretty much impossible to do good on, but they are only worth 10% of your grade, so it isn't the biggest deal.

analysis.name: Francis Akanbi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The nicest professor to exist, period. He is so compassionate and genuinely cares about each person in the class. Research is done in a group with minimal assignments. Very easy class (even with the worst group members). It's very easy to reach him via email and he's very open to comments from students regarding class structure and such. The best!

One of the greatest professors i've had at UF by far! Professor Akanbi takes students opinions and feelings into consideration and always does his best to make sure we are doing okay with the material being learned. He is great at teaching and made it seem like a 3 hr class went by quick! Very engaging conversations as well. 10/10 would take  again

Professor Akanbi is an angel. He is by far the nicest and most caring teacher at the CJC. I would recommend that you take this professor if you ever get the chance. He cares about the welfare of his students. Professor Akanbi understands that being a student with other course loads is difficult and he works with you to make sure you succeed.

Definitely one of my favorite professors at UF. If you are taking this class, definitely take it with Francis, you will not regret it. He is so kind and does everything in his power to make sure each of his students succeed.
Prof. Akanbi is an amazing professor. He cares greatly about his students and wants you to learn and grow while taking his course. He is caring, kind and compassionate and is always in a good mood!

analysis.name: Akintunde Akinyemi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: easy class, he likes people who pay attention and contribute in class. If you show interest and read some of the materials he gives and talk about them in class you are on your way to an A!!!!

He is a great teacher. Go to class, participate, read the books, do your best on tests. He is extremely understanding. If you mess up a couple times, just tell him the truth and he'll work with you. Awesome Teacher!!
Very easy class. He likes respectful people and people who show interest in his materials. Participate a lot in class and you will be on your way to an A

He's just a really nice guy! His African Oral Literatures class was straightforward and interesting. I've had a continued relationship with him as he's written me recommendation letters and I took a Yoruba course with him. He's really patient and I can only say positive things about him.

African Oral Literature sounds boring but he makes it pretty fun. It's a lot of story time and learning about Nigerian culture. Show some effort or interest and you'll get a good grade. Super nice guy. He's also got a really cool African accent which makes listening more interesting.

analysis.name: Nilufer Akalin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class is interesting and very easy to get an A. There are only 2 in-class exams that have open-ended short answer questions about concepts we learn and you're expected to tie in some information from the readings she assigns. You can definitely do really well on exams without reading every single article. Just skim them and you'll get the gist.

Professor Akalin was so passionate and knowledgable about the course material. Many skipped class due to attendance not being mandatory, but those who went formed a great relationship with her. The coursework consisted of minimal assignments that were graded very easy. Don't stress about the exams, there was no final, and extra credit is offered.

I enjoyed Dr. Akalin's class a lot. I found the subject material really interesting. The reading reflections were difficult at times and the class was really lecture heavy/ based on outside readings. I didn't enjoy that participation was mandatory, but she made the class really accessible which I appreciated.

Professor nilufer was so approachable and very kind- you could tell she was passionate about the material. For WST2322, you're graded by few things but the assignments and even tests are very easy. Just show up to class and you should be able to make an easy A
This was a great class with a great professor!

analysis.name: Anwesha Chattopadhyay
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. is very nice and lenient with deadlines and issues, also brings snacks for students. Her lectures are boring and almost never have anything to do with the assignments you actually have to do. The rubric is a little confusing, but she allows revisions on assignments, so no need to stress if you get a low grade. Class is pretty easy/boring.

Anwesha is one of the nicest teachers I've had at UF so far. She's very understanding and will extend deadlines if you need. Just participate and you'll be fine. The essays are fairly easy and the readings are interesting, if a bit long. Highly recommend for a lit credit if you need it.

The professor is never organized throughout the course. Also, her instructions are really bad which lead me to email her multiple times and she also takes two or three days to reply back to your email which I found frustrating.

The class was manageable with only one assignment per week. Professor Chattopadhyay is very flexible with deadlines and is understanding. Also, she allows students to redo assignments for a better grade so it is easy to do well.

Prof. Chattopadhyay had us read a text, write a short discussion post (as long as you write something that shows you read the text, you get credit), and then discuss the text in class. She's lenient with deadlines and gave extra credit. There are two papers during the semester, and she lets you make revisions to earn back points.

analysis.name: Anna Gardner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take her for APK3110c! She's very nice, caring, and approachable. Her exams were very fair (just memorize the ppt slides) and she offers extra credit (worth up to 10 points). Make sure to review your past exams at office hours as some past question will show up on the final. All exams has B+/A- averages so it is easy to do well in this class.

Dr. Gardner is everything you want in a professor and more. The class totalled around 9 assignments, which you can easily get 100% in if you fulfill the minimum requirements. Best quest 2 ever (EAM), and a professor who reads every paper, gives great feedback and motivation, and deeply cares about what she is teaching. Take this professor/class

she is literally so nice and made my semester sm less stressful. A quest 2 class should not be as demanding as my core classes and she recognizes that. There are 6, one-page reflections throughout the whole semester and one group presentation. Rlly chill. take her

Dr. Gardner is the best! I've had her for 3 classes now. Workload is always quite manageable, and her lectures/slides really prepare you well for exams. Exams are very fair. Homework assignments are very relevant & easy. Hardest part was a term paper, but instructions were clear and all did well. Definitely take Gardner for exphys and/or clinical!

Dr. Gardner is one of my favorite APK professors and I would recommend her to anyone. She makes what could be an extremely boring class very fun. Her exams are not hard but they can be tricky so read carefully! Dr. Gardner is always available for questions and extra help if needed. I would recommend her to anyone.

analysis.name: Sio-Iong Ziggy Ao-Ieong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He was terrible! I took this class online because obviously the pandemic & although all teacher understood the difficulty of the different circumstances and tried to accommodate he did not. He ignored student emails about difficulty of test, sent out a rubric on participation the last day after saying it wasnt required. DO NOT TAKE WASTE OF TIME.

I took this class over the fall with the pandemic and it was terrible. It would have been nice to have a TA . He would get frustrated with us if he asked a question and we did not give an answer that he liked. The exam content was not clearly specified in the syllabus & exams often heavily focused on certain topics that again weren't specified.

Ziggy was really chill and understanding. He answers emails pretty quickly and he makes sure that the class makes us think but that we also get a good grade. He curves tests if the whole class does badly. Just make sure you pay attention to lecture and you read the material he assigns. Also turn your camera on during Zoom projects.

Ziggy was very unsympathetic and the least understanding of all the professors Ive ever had at UF. His exams were extremely difficult and didnt make any sense, they were primarily scenario based and in class he never gave us any examples. He refused to give a study guide or let us review exams. I regret ever taking this class!!!!!

Honestly, do not recommend. Exams were ridiculously difficult and specific, and worth a huge percentage of your grade. Difficult to participate in class and participation is a big part of your grade as well. No rubrics for presentations so you don't know what you did wrong. Seemed way too difficult to be a 3000 level class.

analysis.name: Kristen Apraiz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Apraiz is super caring about all her students and provides feedback on all of your lesson plans and debriefs. Even if you're not in education, this course is fun and valuable.

Dr. Apraiz is amazing! She genuinely cares about your progress in the class and gives feedback on every lesson plan. By actually teaching a small group of students throughout the semester, this class will show you if you want to pursue teaching or not!

Loved my experience with Dr. Apraiz. She really cares for her students and the small size of the class allows for her to get to know you personally and thats awesome. 10/10 would recommend trying this class with her.

Dr. Apraiz is truly an amazing professor who cares for all her students. Even if you are not an education major, I found her course to be very useful in seeing if I would like to work with children in the future.
Wonderful person and great class to take if you are interested in working with kids.

analysis.name: Altan Apar

review_highlights.comment: Super helpful and easy to reach. He always made time for me after the class to answer my questions and responded to my emails quickly. He expects you to do readings and discuss in class. If you go to class and do the readings, you will be fine. I did learn a lot.

He is clear, caring, and very personable. Really wants you to succeed. Readings are sometimes dense but he does a good job to make them understandable. He gives tons of examples from his job experiences. Overall a good teacher.

350 characters is not enough to express all my problems with this man. He's nice, but that's pretty much it. When you do decent on an assignment (which is pretty hard to achieve), he heavily critiques it. He is hard to understand. Class was completely and utterly disorganized, though I anticipate he will fix that in the future. I would avoid.

analysis.name: Aaron Aponick

Don't listen to the previous comments. Aponick is a great teacher and a very reasonable guy. For someone who never went to TZ or any other tutoring, I found that reading the book, doing the examples, doing all the recommended hw, and OWL was all you needed to do well. It's orgo so its hard, but its really not that bad if you invest time. Take him!!

Orgo I is notoriously tough and requires a huge amount of commitment to studying. However, Aponick is very fair, which is what you want in a teacher for the course because you need to be prepared you for the second semester. Tests are difficult but fair, and the final is very manageable. Curves tests so top 12-15% get A's and top 70% pass with a C.

Dr. Aponick is not a terrible professor, but he certainly isn't the best.  He is new so he uses someone else's practice tests... they are NOT like his AT ALL, so don't rely on them.  His lecture notes suck and don't bother using the study guides because they don't help either!!  Basically, he givess you no way of knowing what will be on the tests.

I took him in the fall of 2012. He was pretty much great. Funny, likable guy. Gives 3% to your final grade if you do I believe 90% of the online homework, which is very generous. The exams are not difficult, though it's easy to lose points if you don't understand something. DO his recommended problems, and REDO problems he goes over in class.

analysis.name: April Tovani

Great Teacher!  Not that hard of a class

analysis.name: Aqsa Bashir

This professor is always unclear about what she wants on assignments, but then takes points off for things she didn't previously state she wanted. Her assignments are vague, and her grading feedback is rude. I usually enjoy advertising classes, but her class is the exception.

She was super helpful throughout the entire semester with any questions that I had and provided meaningful feedback on work. The assignments were easy to understand, and the lectures were informative. Very fair grading as well. I also had her for ADV3500 and had a similarly positive experience.

Instructions for assignments can be very unclear or short and then points are taken off for things she wanted you to mention but failed to make it known that this was a requirement. Can be quite rude in her grading which could be justified if she gave better instructions but this is not the case. Made me dread every single assignment.

On days where he was teaching I would watch the other professor's videos during class and would just do the iClicker for the extra credit.

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super chill professor and exams are very similar to his practice problems. You don't need previous experience using R, he teaches you in class and it's easy to pick up. Overall similar to undergrad stats.

We were able to practice supply chain skills with increased repetition in creative ways. So it wasn't monotonous, but it also wasn't completely overwhelming. And even though the multiple simulations kept me up at night (nothing like watching a day go by and making $1mil!), I enjoyed them. Definitely participate to add clarity, he's very responsive.

Took as an MSM requirement. Prof. Vakharia is easy going and very responsive. Had pre-assigned groups for a written report, class presentation, and a simulation project. No textbook required. His PowerPoints are super straightforward and he connects content to real-world examples. Exams are open everything, literally. Highly recommend!

I like Dr. Vakharia as a person. He's pretty laid back, and class isn't too bad. However, the content in the class is tough, and he's a really hard grader. He's accessible outside of class, so definitely use that time to talk to him. He's not willing to give any extra credit, so make sure to do well on the tests.
Very easy grader. Clear grading criteria, would love to take his class again.

analysis.name: Asli Baysal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I studied Turkish with Dr. Baysal and she really pushed us to improve our speaking abilities. By the end of the course, it was really easy for me to express myself on a huge variety of cultural and political topics, to the point where speaking Turkish became second nature. Cannot recommend her enough

The only assignments were a few written-responses and one class presentation. As long as you are present and participating, you will finish with an A. Very caring professor and very passionate about what she was teaching.

Dr. Baysal is clearly very knowledgeable of the course content, which came across in her lectures. The class was not very organized, but it honestly was nice because she often ended up giving extra time for a lot of things. Overall, the class was not stressful or hard to manage workload wise and I would take another class again from Dr. Baysal.

Dr. Baysal is very knowledgeable, but EXTREMELY disorganized. Did not follow the syllabus at all, grades are due tmrw, & I still have a "N/A" for my grade. Our final paper is due the day before grades are due, but theres no way she'll read/grade thru all of them (8-10 paged papers) in that time, which is insulting to the student's time and effort

She seemed to care about material, but not about teaching. Did not follow syllabus remotely, did not give any feedback on assignments. By the end of the semester, she had not released a single grade (still showed as a N/A). It was insulting and stressful to deal with the inconsistency and lack of effort.

analysis.name: Autumn Rose
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Not the teacher's fault, but class is structured to be a ridiculous amount of work for a 2000 level class. Plagiarism course, followed by course on correct way to cite sources, then about 25 book quizzes. Then a huge midterm project, followed by 3000-word final paper. Lots of work in between. Too much to do. Not fun. Autum is cool, course bad.
Easiest introduction anthropology course ever. She doesn't interact with you much, it is mostly through her TA's. Nothing is proctored.

This class was wayyy more work than it needed to be. Assignments took forever to complete and they were graded pretty tough too. There were also so many Perusalls and 2 exams, but at least you get to work on the final project over the semester.
Fun professor and requirements are clearly communicated. Any issues were resolved quickly by the professor. Heavy writing but needed for 6000 words.

analysis.name: Austin Moss
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Moss was a first time professor when I took his class and he was still one of the best engineering professors that I have had up to this point. He makes content very easy to understand and he is very open to answering questions. There is a lot of homework; however, if you stay on top of it, you will do well in the class.

Dr. Moss is a good lecturer if you can stay focused, he is pretty monotone and I had him in FLG 270 so it was all on a chalk board, which if you did not sit in the front you could not see. he assigns 2 hw sets a week and they are not that bad, exams are fair and in class quizzes are well announced.

Some of the exam questions were pretty tricky, and there are lots of homework assignments, but the TAs go over all the homework assignments in office hours. It wasn't an easy class, but Dr. Moss is a great lecturer and a great guy overall, I would highly recommend taking him.

Extremely clear on the grading criteria, never felt any of my grades were unfair. Amazing lecturer, clearly has lots of passion for the material he teaches. There is a lot of homework in this class, but it is 100% doable with a good schedule and study groups. One of, if not, my best experiences with a class so far as an MAE student.
Extremely chill and respectful guy. Very clearly passionate and super knowledgeable about the material he teaches. Couldn't recommend him enough. 2018 Lebron of MoM.

analysis.name: Autumn McClellan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor McClellan is one of the best professors at the University of Florida! Take SYA4300, you will not regret at it! She is the perfect choice for this course, trust me!

Attendance and in-class quizzes on book material/documentaries make up the bulk of your grade, and the quizzes are pretty chill. There are a lotttt of group projects but the teacher/TA will give you feedback if u ask for it before the deadline. All in all, it was an interesting class and a doable A.

Dr. McClellan was one of the most fun professors I have ever had. Not only does she incorporate humor and passion during her lectures, they also encompass everything you need for tests. There was a textbook, but I never needed it with how her lectures are structured. As long as you come to class, pay attention, and ask questions you'll be fine.

For SYA4930: "Sociological Data Analysis" (in-person)
Professor McClellan is a wonderful professor who really wants to see her students succeed in the course. She teaches very clearly and has a nice sense of humor. FYI attendance is mandatory but other than that I would highly recommend!

The class, while not in my interest, was quite easy. There are daily individual and group quizzes but they are short and if you read the PowerPoint, you'll do fine. The teacher is straight forward and keeps an excellent schedule. No surprises and not too much extra work. The assignments are fun and not overwhelming. Great first class, recommended.

analysis.name: Karim Asghari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 215 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The material is overall simple but his tests are brutal. His lectures seem okay to comprehend and his study guide is helpful. The test questions are tricky despite it being multiple choice because each choice is not straight forward and has a multitude of options such as all of the above , none of the above, A and B or A,B and C or B and E.

Worst professor ever. He knows his stuff but is not a great teacher. Lectures are hard to understand. UF really needs to make this course and in-seat class. The test are very difficult to study for because his questions are very specific. He ends class 2 weeks early? Why not distribute that time throughout the course. Step it up UF!

The material itself wasn't too bad but his tests were ridiculously difficult. They're multiple choice but the options go like A, A &B, B &C, all of the above, two of the above, none of the above! You have to know the material in detail. Smokin notes help as long as you're ready to remember each and every word of it. You have to work really hard!!

This class was honestly awful. I dont understand how people thought this class was good. The exams have so many grammar mistakes and are very tricky. Buy smokin notes and literally know every little detail. do the extra credit As well. Didnt feel like the lectures were good for exams and hes not a good communicator or very nice but JMO.

This class was harder than I expected. You don't go to class, you just watch his lectures (about 3 a week, 1 hour ish each). There are 4 exams that make up your grade, but he offers some extra credit. I put this class on a pedestal and did everything in my power to do well, and I still got Cs on his exams, even when I felt confident.

analysis.name: Anthony Auletta
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The professor's passion is contagious and it makes studying less tedious than other course when the information is fascinating. Would 100% take again. Never a boring day. The course is set up very scheduled, one review assignment each week, the TA grades difficult and kinda slow so be mindful of that.

This is one of the most interesting courses I've taken at UF! I've learned a ton and it completely changed how I think about biology. Class is discussion-based and very interactive. Dr. A is amazing and does a great job of encouraging questions He also seems to truly care about students. Exams are long but the questions are fair. Highly recommend!

Professor is a great guy and the content itself isn't hard, but the way exams are graded is insane and It took over a month for them to grade. Very slow graders on everything. Lectures are not very helpful, more of a flipped class with lectures being "discussions" where people just ask questions. Do not take this if looking for an easy elective.

I wanted to do research and genetics coding. I did not. Felt like a waste of time. The first 3 months we did nothing but discussions, basic biology is, etc. Soo many reflections with harsh grading. Could be 3 assignments 1 week then 0 the next. The last 2 weeks we did ALL of the data analysis and posters. Slow feedback (day before due date)

This professor is passionate about entomology and the lectures are well structured.  The weekly quizzes and the exams are awful. The quizzes are misleading on purpose. The exams are graded extremely hard; your written responses are deducted heavily even when you get it right for not including some words. Spelling is law. Overall class is alright.

analysis.name: Sharon Austin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The greatest professor I have taken at UF. She is very kind and understanding. The class is made up of 3-4 papers overall in the entire semester and that is it. The papers are really easy as long as you answer all the questions she asks you to. The class can get a bit boring at times but she incorporates videos at times. Overall, very easy class.

I feel weird giving this professor a rating when essentially everything was handled by TAs. The prof gave 1-2 sentence feedback which was often "what [TA] said." Expect lots of papers and group discussions. This class isn't very difficult, I think the hardest part is knowing how to format papers since the grading rubric is practically nonexistent.

Dr. Austin is a very understanding and in my experience she responds to emails within 24 hours. She grades things fairly and you can make corrections on assignments before they are graded. Her lectures are also very concise. Just be ready to write, all the assignments are discussion posts and essays. I highly recommend this class.

Dr. Austin is amazing. I had her for my entire four years at UF; her classes are very straight forward and it is easy to get an A. She's very understanding and flexible, and her classes are never stressful. Grading is clear, and so are her expectations for papers. Very chill, responsive, and helpful thesis advisor too.

Kind professor who is super caring and understanding! The four 8-page papers were based on the readings, which are reviewed and summarized during lecture through powerpoint presentations, and were straightforward and did not take super long to complete. Format is important, so be sure to utilize office hours and you'll walk away with an A

analysis.name: Autumn Mclellan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A great professor who is extremely engaging and approachable when it comes to sociology. Lots of group assignments that are graded strictly. If you are unsure of something, go up to her and ask so you can get as many points as possible. Overall very straightforward class with chapter quizzes and readings. You'll do well as long as you go to class.

LOTS of group work - a very picky grader but does offer in class help. tests can be tricky so be prepared to study. she will NOT round up grades even by a point. i would take her again but be prepared to be on your A game

I took Dr. McClellan for SYG2000 in Summer B of 2023 and had no issue doing well in the class. Although this won't apply to everyone, I was able to get by with little effort & still perform extremely well on exams and quizzes as Dr. McClellan is able to structure a class very efficiently. Very collaborative class. Lots of group work.

I love Dr. McClellan. She really cares about her students' learning and is always available to chat (about both school and personal things). I've had her for 3 classes and she is one of my favorite professors at the university.

She uses a free online textbook to teach from. As long as you do the chapter readings you're set. She is very eager to help students, even if it's not related to the class. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will drop if you don't attend.

analysis.name: Meric Augat

review_highlights.comment: He's a nice guy and clearly passionate about math, but his lectures are often proof heavy and hard to understand. Go during office hours we will make it much easier. Book is useless, Do the HW and practice exams and you'll be fine, watch out for the final its way harder than the other 3 exams

He served as a visiting professor and taught Multivariable Calculus last semester at Bucknell University. He teaches really well on this course as he have taught it multiple times. If there is a seat in his Calc 3, don't hesitate to get in. It is really easy to get a A in his class.

Great professor, and very good at teaching. He explains the material very well. Be ready to take lots of notes during the lectures. His tests are a bit hard, but he always explains everything in the lectures. He also curved the final exam, because it was for many students. He also gave me an extension for the homework once. I took him for fall 22.

Meric's lectures aren't well structured. He spends lots of time proving concepts at the beginning of lecture, which is great until we run out of time for examples at the end. We are consistently .5-1 lecture behind Huang's sections, and his explanations could be clearer. However, he is a funny guy and clearly is passionate about math, which helps.

Meric is very smart. He definitely knows his stuff. In fact, he really isn't bad at teaching, I did understand a lot of the concepts he taught. However, the tests are IMPOSSIBLE. They are ten times harder than anything we learn, or any of the homework. The tests are also (mostly) multiple choice, so no partial credit. I don't recommend.

analysis.name: Avrajit Bandyopadhyay

review_highlights.comment: lots of problems accessing/submitting assignments. 2 tests that were alright, although some information was not clearly explained in the already tough to follow lectures. he wanted class participation, but shared his disappointment when people couldnt answer a question. attendance is taken through in-class assignments that are graded on accuracy.
Lectures clearly explained all concepts but some questions on the exams were not clearly discussed in the lectures. Lots of homework but the assignments do not take very long to complete.

What helped me was not taking notes, but rather sitting there and absorbing the info. Didn't really use textbook

Very caring on reopening assignments, seems like a nice guy but... lectures are a slumber fest attendance is recording randomly based pop quizzes. Accent can be difficult to understand. Tests are the worst does not give back scantron from tests its impossible to know what you got wrong. I surprisingly difficult class to get an A in.

analysis.name: Brian Avery

Brian is as intense as it gets, but he could not be more helpful with career prep. He is entirely devoted to helping any student who shows him that they really care. You can choose to not put in much effort and you'll still get an A, but what's valuable about this course is the wisdom you'll walk away with. Only knock is he's super hard to contact.

The Best professor I've had in 4 years of college. Brian knows everything about the industry. You will walk away from his class feeling like you actually learned something. His exams are difficult and he tells you this at the beginning of the semester but if you ask the right questions on the review day you will be good. add on snap for test ?

Brian is one of the best professors I've had at UF. Assignments are short and simple but are meant to help improve yourself professionally. His weekly yellowdig discussions are pretty interesting and help the class engage with each other. Takes time to meet with students and help fix resumes, cover letters, or network for internships.

Easily the best professors I have ever had. He is dedicated to his students and is more than willing to help with the course work or career aspirations. I would suggest him for any of his offered courses.

Always helpful and willing to break anything down on a one-on-one basis. Tests are challenging, but do the HW and study the review. This will make things go much easier on exams. Labs are mandatory to attend and are well explained. Help is always there when needed.

Luis is like the best teacher ever. I had no interest in the class, actually I took the class for fun. He is super chill and his exams are fair. Homework on the other hand can be tough but you're in college after all. :D
Luis is the most helpful and easy going TA I've had. The material is difficult, but thats hardly his problem. Go to class and always ask questions. He's always happy to help!
