I loved this class and would recommend it to anyone interested in literature.

He is absolutely adorable. I couldn't agree more (previous comment) ..that he cares more that you understand the reading rather than grades. The reading can be overwhelming but you you over it thoroughly in class so even if you don't understand it he will explain it! Hebrew Lit is very interesting! Highly recommended.

Stories all short, interesting, and well-chosen. Balaban knows his stuff but is very approachable and not condescending. Great respect and concern for students, VERY understanding. Inspired interest in subject. Wish more teachers were more like him. Highly recommend for a fairly simple yet interesting course.

This guy is adorable, and extremely understanding. He can read a bit too far into things when he really gets going, but it will open your eyes to literature you probably would have never read otherwise. Highly recommended.

Probably the nicest prof. ever.  Grades very easily and is more concerned with making sure you understand the material than grades.  Always helpful and gets to know students well.  I really recommend you take his class.

There isn't any in-class time devoted to group project, so coordinating is challenging.  Subject matter is very interesting and she is REALLY helpful and understanding.

She was a horrible lecturer and very scatter-brained.  She would go off on tangents and never return to her original thought.  The class material was interesting but she was so unorginized that it made the class a nightmare!
I've had some bad anthro courses but this is the worst by far. She doesnt seem to know much anthropology and I do not think she could even handle an intro class and this is an upper level class.

please don't take this course from him, take it from Kohler at all costs. he taught this class as if we had all worked for MSFT for 10 years and is not one to try and adjust the class schedule when 85% of the class can't keep up. he does try to help thoug

Dr. Billups is AMAZING! He is my favorite history professor I have had at UF and would 100% take his class again. review_highlights.comment: I found this class pretty boring because of the 3 hour lecture but none of that was Bridis's fault. He's a great professor and knows a lot about reporting. I would miss class from time-to-time, and it was no big deal. Lectures were online and the weekly quizzes or homeworks were simple to complete.

Prof. Bridis knows his stuff and his class is extremely useful. He's a funny guy and the class went the full three hours maybe once or twice. Tests aren't a cake walk, but he will go out of his way to let you retake them to help you at the end of the semester. Would highly recommend.

I loved this class! Definitely super useful and I was a big fan of his lectures and sense of humor, you could tell he's lived! He's always there to help so don't hesitate to reach out. For summer A we only had 6 quizzes and 4 assignments, so not many grades. The quizzes are really specific so have the lectures out and read the questions carefully.

Incredible professor!! He is incredibly knowledgeable about the journalism world and left every class wanting more. Every week consisted of a Packback assignment, and a quiz based on the lecture plus a couple of other assignments throughout the semester and some extra credit. Very easy to get an A. 100% recommend and can't wait to take him again

I absolutely loved Professor Bridis for JOU3110. He is one of the most down-to-earth professors I have ever had. He is always open to help you, and you can tell he truly loves what he teaches. The course content isn't that bad, some of it can get a little tricky. He makes sure to post the PowerPoints, which can be a great resource.

analysis.name: James Bonczek
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 160 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Simply one of the easiest classes ever. I just needed a science course and this class was a great filler for the summer semester.    Just dont get lazy and wait to study the day of. Its not fun to listen to multiple lectures per day. Spread the lectures out, study, fill out the review sheet and you should be fine come test day.

I took this class for fun and always found his lectures passionate and interesting. The lecture quizzes are in-class only written assignments are extremely easy, and exams are taken outside of class and open-note. He drops a few of your lowest scores too, very easy A and I learned a lot about Florida's hydrology

This is an amazing professor who understands that most students are only taking the class to fulfill a science credit. He is very passionate about what he teaches and outside of the lecture quiz taken in class and an open note quiz every 2 weeks or so, there really is no work required. The exams are open note and can be taken wherever.

Could literally say nothing bad about Mr. Bonczek. He's clearly into what he teaches, and his lectures are always interesting. There are lecture quizzes almost every lecture, but if you are paying attention, they are very easy. Tests are open-note and online, and they aren't taken in class. Such a nice and funny teacher, I highly recommend him!

Professor Bonczek is an incredible professor who is very passionate about what he teaches. You can miss up to 7 lecture quizzes but I never wanted to miss a lecture as I always learned something fascinating about water. Exams are open note, I highly recommend this course!

analysis.name: Erika Brooke
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Tough exams (3) even with a study guide. Had an assignment about every 2 weeks so it was manageable. The class is very organized and easy to follow which also helped. Second class with Dr. Brooke. She was very responsive and so was her TA. Even offered extra credit. Wish she taught more classes.

Dr. Brooke is very knowledgeable and impressive. She has a great setup for her online classes and integrates different assignments to keep it interesting. TA grades most things but there are only 3 exams that were very manageable. You probably should buy the textbook to ensure you get all of the material, but I did not use mine all the time.

This was my second class with Dr. Brooke and this one seemed significantly harder. There are three exams each of which is far more challenging than needed, beyond that, the workload is very manageable.

Dr Brooke was amazing. There was a lot of reading. If you only watch the videos, there is a good chance you will pass the quizzes. However, the assignment involve the textbook, so I recommend getting the online version and search up key words. There is a three page paper at the end, but it's fairly easy. 

Most importantly, THERE IS NO FINAL!!!!

Dr. Brooke was excellent! She was extremely accommodating of my disabilities and always accessible via email to answer any questions I had. Her quizzes were challenging, but as long as I kept up with the readings and lectures, they were manageable. Some classmates complained a lot, but this is UF—put in the effort. It's not high school. Take her!

analysis.name: Leon Brown
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is challenging without a textbook and in such timeframe (8wks), but he gave us soo much material to review even without a textbook. He also makes himself available to help students through regular office hours or you can just schedule a teams meeting with him. I would say it's a lot for a 2credit class but he's a good professor.

This course has way too many assignments. There are quizzes, labs, discussions, and two exams. He covers way too much material in 6 weeks. For the quizzes and exams, I felt very overwhelmed with the amount of material I had to know. I would have to constantly study to keep up. If there is another professor, take the class with them.

I've had Dr.Brown for both ISM3254 and ISM3255 now and I think he is incredible. I've had many coding professors in the past who can't seem to grasp the fact that coding is a new subject for many students. Dr. Brown walks you through Java so clearly and the assignments all have purpose. He is a gem of a professor.

Poor course structure across all his classes. With such a bad rate my professor at his previous school it's a mystery why UF hired him. He seems almost panicked teaching and gets himself always behind which puts us at risk consistently. Doesn't look out for student success at all.
He assigns convoluted assignments and never grades them so you do not know how well youre doing in the class. It is a 2 credit class that takes like 6 hours each weeek

analysis.name: Bryon Moraski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Moraski is a great guy, very knowledgable. Theres a lot of readings, and the class is only really graded by attendance and the exams, which aren't too bad, but he likes to throw a couple curveball questions in there about niche things, and that can really mess your grade up because of the lack of any other assignments.

He's passionate about teaching and means well, but his exams are highly specific to lectures & readings. I had to study at least two hours a day to keep an A, and he doesn't share his slides. Paper was tough, and he's really strict about attendance and participation. He can seem timid when you ask for help. There are easier classes.

Please do not take this professor for your own mental health. He is very specific with his exams and participation. His paper was not hard to write but he is a tough grader. There are far easier classes to take as a poli sci major. Attendance is mandatory and he does not share notes or his power point at all.

Very interesting class but is difficult if you have no previous knowledge of Russia. Very informative but his slides are bare, so you have to pay attention and take notes. He wants students to succeed and be engaged. The class can attract strange people but he handles them. It's important to read and study. The tests are specific but managable.

Dr. Moraski was the best professor I had at UF.  He is insanely approachable, and his lectures were always interesting.  His classes require a good bit of reading and work, but it ultimately made me a much better student as a result.

analysis.name: Kevin Butler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easy enough class, but not a super nice guy. He mistakenly tried to tell me I could not add his class during the drop/add period. Responds fast to emails, but not nicely. I get the feeling that he is interested in his research and teaching takes a backseat. Then again, students regularly showed up late to his lectures, so can't blame him.

Overall Dr/ Butler is a great professor and taught a great class. The course covered a wide range of materials but he was always ready to answer questions. I'll say the grading was a bit slow but, as I understand, no TAs were found for the course so it was understandable.Overall it was an engaging and interesting course with an expert in the field.

Extremely slow when it comes to grading. I submitted assignments back in late March that are still not graded, which has now caused me to receive an I* on my transcripts and not receive credit for the course. Communication with him is 50/50, sometimes he will respond within the hour and sometimes you'll never hear him. Class was manageable though.

analysis.name: Cameron Buckner
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was very interesting and he gave a bunch of fun examples to better explain harder concepts. There were 2 exams (a midterm and final) that were both FRQs. Class was simple and can't see how anyone get less than an A.
Clearly very smart and passionate, would be better in a smaller class environment but generally goated
Intelligent professor that clearly communicates expectations and presents information well. No reason you should be failing this class.
Easy class, professor has interesting lectures

analysis.name: Rebecca Butcher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Butcher has been top 3 professors I have had at UF. The lab was awesome in the fact that there was lots of continuity where we took a DNA sample and conducted multiple experiments to create a transformed plasmid that was used to express the protein and measure function. Super accessible outside of class, willing to give honest feedback

Would not recommend. Extremely uncaring and not receptive to life issues outside of the classroom. Grading is extremely confusing and messy. TA's grade so how much partial credit you get depends on the student who is grading your exam. Very slow, boring lectures. Often doesn't get through all material. Ignores emails. Not helpful.

Professor Butcher structures biochem in a very fair way. I would say that she doesn't lecture very well, however for a class as content heavy as biochem, most of the learning in this class is done through studying anyway. Adapting to this class was hard, but once you have a group to study with, it is very clear what you need to do to pass.

Dr. Butcher teaches well and is easy. Her tests revolve around whatever she writes on the board; there are no surprises. She is helpful in office hours. Her only downfall is that she is extremely slow during lecture and does not finish what is proposed on the syllabus, which is unfortunate if you need the information for MCAT or another exam.

Just go to class. I studied her tests a day or two beforehand, and always got a B or higher on the tests. Tests directly on lecture. If you passed the orgos (assuming you did), you can pass this class unless you're thumbing your phone during every lecture. It is not a walk in the park or anything, but it could be worse.

analysis.name: Michael Bumbach
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bumbach was a great teacher. Really friendly, knowledgeable, and always available for help. Seemed to really care that we understood the material and explained things well. Lectures were online and somewhat dry. Tests were a little difficult due to the material and NCLEX style questioning. Would definitely love to take a class from him again.
online lectures are kind of useless but the class was great. He was an amazing instructor. Kind of sad to see him go. Be ready to fill out like an entire workbook though lol

While others are harsh for Dr. Bumbach, I don't think this is a fair or accurate description. He teaches in a graduate program, so I anticipate his courses to be more difficult. There is a lot of reading and exams are pretty tough. He is accessible and always willing to work with any issues. I would take his classes again.

This is a tough class although he is very upfront about this. He is a tough grader, but this is graduate school and should be. There is a lot of information, get ready to read. Also, this is an online course, I did love that I can read/learn when I wanted.

Took two of his grad courses. Clearly recycled material. He was responsive via email but his responses were usually not helpful. I understand he prob has a huge workload but I'm not even sure he understood his own rubrics and guidelines. Poor instructions and guidance when it came to assignments. Really inconsistent grading. Exams straight textbook

analysis.name: Christine Bucan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Such an amazing professor. She has so much PR experience under her belt and her lectures reflect it. Textbook is useful for studying but not mandatory. Her review sessions are amazing! As long as you attend lectures and contribute with the group project, it's an easy A. She also has tons of guest speakers and networking experiences in her lectures!

to pass the class, you def need to attend the lectures bc she'll tell you what's on the exam and what isn't. the exams are all situation based, so her wording can be more difficult at times. it's not hard to get an A, but you have to attend lecture. i didn't read the textbook and just attended lecture and ended with an A. very test heavy though

I love her! She was so knowledgable and experienced. As long as you attend and put some effort in, you'll do well. It's a few easy assignments, 1 group project, 3 exams (read the textbook for it). She lets you drop the lowest exam and assignment grade if you complete everything. Couldn't recommend this enough if you're slightly interested in PR.

So informative and clearly passionate about what she is teaching. The class isn't super difficult, but spend time memorizing key terms for the exams. She offers lots of extra credit and connections to people she knows in the industry. However, my TA gave me great grades on all individual assignments and a pretty bad grade on the group project.

Christine is great! There are only a few assignments and 4 exams for the course. However, if you sit for the first three exams and do well, you do not need to take the final (she drops your lowest exam grade). Exams are not too hard as long as you read the textbook and review lecture slides. Assignments are not too hard nor time-consuming.

analysis.name: Derek Burdette
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed going to this class every week. Homework once a week. Lectures were very good. Take lots of notes and follow the rubric given to a T and make sure to answer the question in the discussion as a whole and mimic the language in the readings. Not that many readings for this class.

Passionate about subject, but extremely knowledgable. Any BA or BFA major looking for an art history credit take this. Focuses on both the ART and the HISTORY which I feel many other professors in art history classes focus too heavily on the art without explaining the history or context. Burdette goes above and beyond explaining both's importance.

I never interacted with Dr. Burdette, but his lectures were AMAZING. If you are even a little interested in art, I highly recommend taking ARH2000. Because of this class, I want to take more art classes in the future. This is also an easy A (one short assignment and quiz per week) and an easy project instead of a final.
Dr. Burdette is the best professor I've had at UF. He is smart, funny, and down to earth. He knows his subject really well.

This class was a piece of cake. I took it for the diversity credit. There was one assignment a week plus a discussion board as well. I did read the chapters and honestly, I thought they were interesting. There is an essay where you have to go to a museum but it wasn't too bad. There is also a recorded final presentation that you can just read off.

analysis.name: Brian Ray
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this class thinking it would be a relatively easy elective, seen as it is taught by two guidance counselors.  Awful tests and lots of lengthy assignments. They try and justify the difficulty of the class to other 3000 level business classes, but there is just too little substance for how hard and specific the tests are.  Really time consuming

The only positive reviews on this page are probably Ray himself. The class is not only useless, but requires a surprisingly high level of rote memorization. Avoid if you're looking for a course to further your education. Take this if you enjoy memorizing useless facts and spitting them out on exams.

Loved Professor Ray! I had a back injury midway through the semester, and he accommodated me instantly! 9 Assignments, 2 exams, and 3 papers for the ENTIRE class! He gives you plenty of time to complete all the assignments, just make sure not to procrastinate! Work gets graded by PAs, you'll be making your resume, LinkedIn, and autobiography.

Dr. Ray is one of the most inspirational and easygoing professors I've had at UF. He truly cares about his students and looks to make an impact on them in the long run. Class is very straightforward and clear on what is expected, would definitely take again.

This is a good class for someone who has never had a job before and still lives at home...However, for the rest of us who have been working since High School, the "useful" info is stuff we've already heard before. Tests are mere memoriziation of random facts, and not really about concepts discussed. If I didn't have to take this class, I wouldn't.

analysis.name: James Bunch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bunch is so fun and extremely caring for his Ag Ed students! I took AEC4324 which is a discussion based class where participation is crucial to getting anything out of the class. He is has a wealth of knowledge in this field, so ask questions and put forth an effort to get to know him. This class has a low workload but is an intro to Ag Ed.
By far my favorite professor since I got to UF. Lectures are actually really interesting and he makes them fun. Tests are also really easy.
Great professor, the class isnt easy but offers valuable information.

analysis.name: Jason Butler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is really really hard but good. I def remember everything from his class but be ready for super challenging exams that make up 100% of your grade and a fast moving pace. He is helpful though, but just be warned when he says something will be simple that is a lie.

Butler seems like a mean guy and that's because he is(he says it) but deep down he cares for the students. His lectures aren't the best, I never understood what was going on at all and I was below the average on all the exams. But I killed on the final and ended well. My advice, youtube every topic and don't be afraid to ask butler for help!

Dr. Butler knows what he's talking about, but sometimes had trouble conveying it to the class. Tests and HW were usually pretty tough (averages were in the 40%-60% range) but grading was completely scaled so it worked out.

Clear lecture style, a lot of algebra workouts left to the student. You must know and understand the homework to the point of being able to teach it to others in order to pass exams/quizzes.  Very difficult grader, not a lot of partial credit. Do extra homework problems and go to his office hours. Final exam is difficult.

Jason is tough but extremely helpful. He's quite knowledgeable and a great resource. Always answers emails. Swallow your pride and he will help you. Tests and quizzes are HARD but doing the homework will partially prepare you. He has optional texts, reading relevant sections of those helps too. Try to understand, not figure out what's on the test.

analysis.name: Taryn Buckley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is a great, easy elective. There are weekly quizzes that are not honor locked, and a midterm + a final that are honor locked and you have a week to take. There are also extra credit opportunities. The class was interesting and assignments are easy with most answers being found in the textbook.

Super easy class if you just work on the flashcards, the assignments are easy and interesting, and the tests are the quizzes but longer. The professor was kind and nice, and overall present for an online professor! Would recommend!

Great class. Super helpful if you're prehealth and very low maintenance. Midterm and final were super chill and if you do extra worksheets you can get extra points put towards ur midterm and final. Never had to worry about my grade in this class. I strongly recommend it!!!

Super easy class. You can finish the course (other than the midterm and final) in probably less than a week. Easy A and helpful for pre-health! The prof was very clear in her grading, though did not always respond to emails.

Very easy class that provided me with a lot of practical knowledge. Memorization based, so tests were very straightforward and easy to ace. A lot of extra credit provided, 12 points per each exam. Only two exams, a midterm and final. Professor seemed very nice and caring. She wanted the students to understand the content.

analysis.name: Charles Bwenge
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take this class! Dr. Bwenge is maybe the most caring professor that I've had at UF. His style is "untraditional," but in a good way. He mixes readings and films for an interactive conversation rather than a lecture. I was always excited to come to class and I surprised myself with how much I learned as the class was essentially a completion grade

He is very unorganized. He speaks very quickly and rambles often. Additionally, the work that he tends to give seems like busy work rather than valuable knowledge. This class is not very flexible and needs and online option as well. Everything he gives out is printed and in person which is difficult for when unexpected emergencies come across.

Professor is really passionate about the class and loves to hear what students have to say about the different topics that are explored. There are only 3 short papers you have to write, 4 reading quizzes (the readings are short), and a group project at the end. He gives very clear instructions for all assignments and answers all questions.

the best humanities class ever. He is the most entertaining and lively teacher. He has a strong accent, but hes SO flexible. NO exams. easy quizzes on like 3 pages every now n then. gives out A's like no tomorrow. 2 papers and 1 group project. LOTS of movies. BUY THE BOOK, you need it for the quizzes.

One of the best/most interesting professors I have had at UF. Bwenge is amazing. He has a true passion for the subject, and he cares about his students. Assignments are easy, and the projects help you learn a lot about Africa. Take this class for a requirement or just for fun.

analysis.name: Richard Burt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's perhaps the most notorious professor in the English Department, and that is a wildly good thing. Burt has something of a cult following and that's because of the way he has students engage the films and writings. You will never watch a movie the same way again. Also, the class is pretty easy, just expect a lot of watching/reading.

There is A LOT of reading.  It can get pretty confusing and philosophical, but is mostly enjoyable.  Every now and then we watched films.  Course is discussion based, with Burt acting more like a moderator than a lecturer.  So you need to speak up.  He values all opinions and makes jokes every once in a while.  Burt is great!

I took three classes with Burt because I respected him and his teaching style so immensely. He challenged his students with difficult texts, and guided us through discussion like a lighthouse. Burt makes his classes accessible  to everyone, while leaving room open for people to excel. He receives criticism well, as he is humble and hilarious.

But is an eccentric and interesting prof. He is genius and you'll learn a lot. But his classes are not easy, you will have to think critically, read a lot, and write a lot. He is a good Prof. Show up to class, do the work, pay attention, and try and you should be okay. But you will be busy! Short notice on deadlines as well.

Assignments were unclear, expectations were less clear, discussions were mediocre, and the professor was breathtakingly unconcerned about his students. His classes are on fascinating topics, but he makes them suck. Which is quite a talent, in its own warped way. Avoid.

analysis.name: Kathy Byrne
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a little quirky but I loved her class. It was interesting and funny. What she goes over in the lectures is on the tests so attend them. If you can't, make sure to attend the review sessions because those are hands down the most important days (next to the tests themselves). Have fun with her and get to know her. You'll love the class too.

easy easy class. really boring and strange but almost no work. u do have to go see 3 plays though. test review with all the answers right b4 the test so go to that. the teacher is not the best but just bring something to do during lecture since they take attendence. ta's not hard graders. group project at the end. good way to get a diversity credit

I took the online section of this class.  It was the most time consuming class that I had the whole semester.  While the assignments were easy and I got an A in the class, each assignment is only worth 10 points out of about 400 points possible.  You end up doing a ton of busy work.  If you want an easy A, go for it, but be prepared for busy work.

I took her for TPP2100. At first glance the semester seemed like it might be horrible. However, she taught us to get out of our shells, especially for those who had no prior acting experience. The class we had became one of the most close group of friends I've seen in a classroom setting. It was truly an honor. Take this class. You never know. :)

This is such and easy class, dont even buy the book. Its an extremely easy A. The problem is that I really like theatre, but there is not passion in this class. Take acting for nonmajors if you like drama and actually want to learn about it-its not a hard alternative. I didnt learn anything from the actual teacher, but the ta's showed passion. :)

analysis.name: Judith-Kelly Byram
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst teachers I've had at UF, and it is not because the class material is challenging.  Her attitude is the worst, she thinks that because she has a PhD in neurology she is better than everybody else.  Directions were never clear until papers were graded.  Also, she bases particpation grades pretty much on whether or not she likes you.

Unclear on assignments, refused to answer some reasonable questions unrealistic expectations, made 25% of the midterm on a question the class was confused about and told us she didn't have time to go teach it to us easily upset & often perceived as rude not helpful with any solutions when I reached out for help Worst scholastic experience to date

Believe me when I say this woman is insane. I am certain she has anger management issues because she screams at people for no good reason. NEVER have anything out unless its related to her class because if she sees even a planner she will embarrass you. Do the readings and take detailed notes because she asks for very specific answers on quizzes.

This class was HORRIBLE!! She is very unclear about what she expects from the assignments until after they're graded. Her grading is very inconsistent among different students. She never gives clear answers to questions either. Good luck in this class! I don't know how, but I somehow managed an A, so it is possible.

analysis.name: Fred Byrd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Summary: Take the class. And Go to his office hours, people.   The Backstory: I've always sucked at math. But The Byrdman was really helpful.  I was intimidated by his beard at first, but he's actually super nice. Knows a ton about math and worked hard to help me understand. I feel totally less mediocore now.

I loved this class a lot. He was very helpful and understanding. Just study your notes and complete the H.W. assignments and you'll be good. He was the best math professor that I experienced at UF. I finished off with an A.

I was pretty nervous about Calc 2 coming into this class since I was never really great at math, but Professor Byrd made it easier with his discussions and notes. I also used study edge and that helped a lot!
Mr. Byrd was very helpful. It's clear that he likes what he's teaching and wants you to do good. I took Trig and Precalc separate and recommend it. I would take his class again.
His helpfulness in office hours helped me pass. Personally I think Fred is a really cool guy.

analysis.name: Byung Ho Kang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst professors at UF. Should have been a simple science elective, turned out to be my worst class of the semester. The material itself isnt that bad, but the teacher thinks hes teaching at Harvard.The questions are so convoluted, you dont even understand what it is asking. Must teach yourself everything, forget understanding him speak.

If you have taken BCH 4024 then this will be extremely easy for you. If you have no prior knowledge of biochemistry then you are going to be utterly lost  but the textbook is written in very simple language so just read it and you'll be fine. He gives extra credit for coming to class. Study the practice questions and you will do well on the exams.

This class turned out to be way more difficult than I expected. Dr. Kang's dialect of what I assume resembles the English language to him is pretty much unintelligible. I feel like most professors are more concerned about the big picture when it comes to a class that covers a lot of material, however this guy wants you to know every little detail.

I thought this class would be just like any other Biology class where you put in the time to read the book, go to class, take notes, and do the practice tests and you would be fine. Wrong. I study so much for this class and still get low grades on the exams. Questions are extremely tricky. You should probably read the book twice to do OK on them.

His accent isn't a big deal and he's actually kind of funny.  As others have said, his tests are based off the practice problems he gives,a few might be verbatim but most he gives a different twist to the question and it can be really tricky.  Reading the book is really helpful need to make sure you UNDERSTAND the CONCEPTS not just memorizing.

analysis.name: Jason Byrd
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't take his classes ladies! It was evident that some students received preferential treatment, while others were often dismissed or criticized harshly. It's crucial for educators to foster respect and professionalism in their interactions with students. I observed him harass a student employee. UF did the right thing in firing him. Toxic!

This was the best class I have taken. Dr. Byrd is the best professor. He has so much experience which makes his lectures so much more interesting.  He's incredibly intelligent and hilarious. Definitely go to class! It's necessary to be able to pass, plus it's just great to listen to lectures. He's not bad to look at and crush on either.

He is a horrible professor, one of the worst at UF. He constantly makes really big assignments all due on the same day and then more big assignments due right after that without any kind of break. He can also be really mean and patronizing, especially if you are trying to advance yourself in the field. If you do not have to take him, then do not.

I took both of Dr. Byrd's classes and they were by far the best classes I've ever taken at UF. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful & honestly cares about his students. Class is easy and interesting. You don't really need the textbook. I highly recommend his classes!

Very interesting class. Easy A as long as you go to lecture. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful and sweet, and definitely not bad to look at. ;) Highly recommended. He's the only prof I've ever had a slight crush on!

analysis.name: Carlos Suarez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Extremely good lecturer and always ready to listen to any point any student brings up. Even with potentially controversial topics manages to navigate them with respect and level-headedness. Requires lots of writing but none of it particularly difficult for the average college student. Highly recommend taking any of his classes.

Classes have a reaction paper due every Monday and Friday that must be 500 words, be prepared to read. However, the readings are discussed in class and feel like they have a purpose in the class overall, rather than just being busy work. He genuinely cares about the class and encourages discussion. Very nice teacher and would definitely recommend.

Suarez is the best lecturer at UF. His passion for the class & for fostering discussion shines daily. He's difficult, with multiple papers/exams making up the bulk of grading, but the discussion makes up for it. As long as you're able to write, it's fine. Exams will only cover what he said in class, so notetaking makes them easy to prep for.

soooooooo many reaction papers. i had him for a caribbean class and every week there were 2 500 word reaction papers due. one due monday one friday. and he randomly grades  5 out of the 20 due. lectures would turn into tangents so he wouldnt even answer a question if u asked. a great guy but holy cow would not take him again if i could choose.

Suarez is the best lecturer I've ever had. You can tell he cares deeply about the art of teaching and engaging a classroom. He is an easy grader if you know what he is looking for, but he is very particular. Exams are all written, and 2 major papers are written with novels to be read outside class. He is flexible, but takes a while to grade things.

analysis.name: Megan Cantrell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is super nice and accessible outside of class for help with any assignments. She spaced out all of our writing assignments and quizzes so well that the workload never felt overwhelming. I recommend reading the modules and making good study guides before the quizzes. Overall, it's a very laid-back and manageable course for the summer.

Professor Cantrell was pregnant for my class, so we had the lab period with Cassandra Goff (who was great). I'll say the course itself is super easy and I 100% recommend it. We had 3 written assignments, 3 quizzes, and 1 final paper- all of which were spread out nicely. Professor Cantrell, though not in our classroom, was still very interactive.

Very organized lectures throughout the week and is a very fair grader. The entire class is mostly working on a group project with people you choose, so make sure to choose a good group. Not a lot of assignments, and theyre not hard, so theyre manageable. Also, multiple extra credit opportunities! As long as you do the work youll be pretty fine!

Truly one of my favorite teachers I've had. She makes class super interesting by teaching in different ways (doesn't just lecture the whole time). Tons of nongraded group activities and has great communication in and out of class. If you get the chance to take her in person, definitely do it. I took her for AEC3413

She is amazing as a person and teacher! The class was so fun and I actually enjoyed learning the material. Going to class was no problem and the homework was easy. Test were open note. The only kinda difficult project was the personal growth project, but even that was fine. Love her!

analysis.name: Luca Di Cerbo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
This was one of the only classes where attending lecture actually mattered and made sense in real time. I didn't feel like I had to reteach myself the material afterward.

That alone puts him among the best professors in the department, in my opinion. I highly recommend taking this class if you have the opportunity.

I'm not gonna lie, Dr. Di Cerbo was behind the main professor in lectures for the whole semester and he didn't explain the material quite as well, but if you happen to make your way to his office hours, he his very good at helping you understand the material. Only 75% attendance required for a 100% in the grade book. Beware of the tough final.
Quizzes are attendance-based and exams are straightforward with no tricks or surprises. He's also really funny and lighthearted. Take for a chill math elective
He was great would 100% recommend over pretty much any of the other math professors

I enjoyed this class. It was the first time he taught calc 3 and he explained the material very well. He answered everyone's questions thoroughly and is a very caring professor. The final is very difficult. I got high As on the first 3 exams and failed the final, the material got exponentially harder. But I am a freshman, and I am glad I had him!

analysis.name: James Cauraugh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite APK class and professor easily. I was nervous at first cant lie, but engage! He has an awesome personality and makes class fun as you go. Do not be afraid to answer when he cold calls. he makes a true effort to know you. Grading is VERY fair. Go to class, take good notes, and watch review videos since exams come straight from them.

Overall professor Cauraugh is an odd professor. He will learn everyone's name in the class week 1 and cold calls on students which is pretty entertaining to watch. He's very passionate about research, but somehow a lot of his lectures end up being pretty substance-less. Definitely watch the exam review videos and read the textbook and you'll be ok.

I really enjoyed Dr. Cauraugh. He is very particular, but is entertaining as it was my one class I never got tired in. I think everyone should experience a class with him because I feel that I am a better person after taking his class. The expectations for the class can be vague and hard to follow but just go to class and read the textbook

My main problem is that he forces students to buy his book, which is $48. If he was well established in his field, that would be reasonable. Literally no one besides his students buy the book, forcing us to read lower quality material for a higher price.

he is such an awesome guy. be ready to be cold called in class, but just pay attention to what he is talking about. its really not too tricky at all. read textbook for exams, but as long as youre able to just talk about the subjects and u can write a lot ur so fine. one of the best professors u will ever have

analysis.name: Alin Ceobanu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely difficult to work with regarding medical accommodations. Communication is passive-aggressive, inflexible, and stressful. Questions legitimate telehealth notes and repeatedly emphasized missed exams, making students feel unsupported. Not ideal if you need flexibility.
This guy didn't input too much time in class preparation, which is very obvious. You should not expect to learn too much in his class. The course is boring and useless.
do youself a favor, take this class online.

Lectures are pretty boring, there is little room for class discussions, and Ceobanu will not hesitate to talk down to you as if you are stupid. The "study guides" he provides are literally just a list of every bullet point from his PowerPoints, and the tests are probably 20% of what's on the study guide. The tests are also worded like riddles.

Literally the hardest class I've ever taken with the worst professor possible. He's nice but truly terrible. He had the students teach every class and sat in the back grading the presentations meticulously. The exams were hard and impossible and there was nothing to cushion the grade. Didnt give much resources so you teach yourself. Don't take him.

analysis.name: Celeste Martinez
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She was not made to be a teacher. Unorganized, unclear with directions and grades on what is not included in rubric. The rubric will show you did A+ work but she will give you a full letter grade off for kicks.

I have tons of respect for Professor Martinez because I can tell she is genuinely passionate about social media management. However, her class is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken! I am a straight A student taking five classes, and thought that social media would be a light course load. WRONG! She is unclear, unhelpful, and intimidating.

This is my 2nd time around with this professor and I can assure you I didn't select this class based on the instructor. As is often the case, UF will work with some lackluster professor based in another country who could not care less. The curriculum is full of technical issues that should have been fixed long ago- highly unprofessional.

This professor is a very tough grader and extremely strict, with little room for flexibility or accommodations. She doesn't even hold lectures at all and grading was harsh and didn't always reflect the effort put into assignments. I didn't feel supported, and it was difficult to get clear answers when issues came up.

AWFUL!! She is the most nit picky professor i've ever had at UF which is ridiculous for a class about social media. Grades so unfairly no matter how much time you put into an assignment. She takes a week to answer an email, I had to follow up twice before getting a response. Avoid her.

analysis.name: Recep Celebi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Recep's lectures were engaging, but make sure to write fast because he doesn't stop going once class starts. He was pretty funny and kind, and wants his students to succeed. Make sure to go to office hours if you are struggling because he does randomly call on students during class for answers, which keeps the class engaged.

Mr. Celebi cares about his students and is happy to answer questions in class or office hours. However, he is exceptionally particular about the take-home quizzes, to the point where he would critique my handwriting and formatting of my work. This was my first math class at UF and I hated it, but it also prepared me for my future classes.

I took Calculus 3 with Professor Recep Celebi in summer 2024. His enthusiasm for mathematics and willingness to provide additional support outside of class significantly enhanced my learning experience. I highly recommend his course to anyone looking to deepen their understanding of calculus.

I honestly did not struggle to get an A in this class but I know that was not true for most of our class. His tests were really hard but he awards a majority of the points for the work and the tests have bonus points, so I found it easy as a non-math inclined student to get A's on them. He gives EC + weekly at home tests. He's also really funny lol

I'm not going to lie, Recep was a tough TA. However, I wouldn't have any other instructor for Calc 2. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures were so clear and easy to follow. However, he did single out students sometimes, which is the only thing preventing me from giving him a 5/5.

analysis.name: Erta Cenko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Cenko! She is one of my favorite professors here at UF simply because of how kind she is to her students and her passion for public health is clear. The class is simple (I took it in-person) and the requirements to get an A are clear. She is also always open to feedback, which I love in a professor.

Cenko is the best professor I've had at UF! I took two classes with her in Fall and she was amazing in both. She cares for the students and wants us to learn. I messed up an assignment and instead of giving me 0 points she offered to meet and review the module together to make sure I understood. She was also very helpful with a rec letter. 10/10

Great professor. Things felt a bit disorganized but it's obvious she cares about her students and the subject matter. Basically everything involves a group-project, which wasn't my favorite. It is such an easy class, only 2 quizzes are graded and there are no exams. Grading was a bit slow at times, but that was mainly the TA, not Dr. Cenko.

If I could take another class with Dr. Cenko, I absolutely would. She is hands down one of the nicest and best professors I've had not just in PHHP but in my entire time at UF! Probably one of the best decisions I made was taking HSC3502 with her over Hanson. Everything about this class from tests to projects was handled so great. 1000+/10 for sure

Dr. Cenko is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about public health and teaching it understandably to her students. We had a hybrid class that met once a week and made our semester-long groups at the beginning of the semester. If you're looking for a light workload class that you'll enjoy, this is the one. Would definitely take her again!

analysis.name: Celeste Wagner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I am so sad that she left UF. She is honestly one of the nicest and caring people I've met. Her class was full of discussion where people could freely say and think without judgement. You can tell that she put a lot of effort into her lectures and the assignments were simple enough to teach the material without overwhelming you.

Prof. Wagner was such a joy. I think the class would have been better if more people responded to her questions, but it was pretty easy and she made her assignment expectations clear. She did always take a point or two off on the group projects but she left feedback on ways to improve that I think was valid. Definitely the best option for MMC2604!

She's one of the sweetest people ever! She's incredibly accommodating, understanding and flexible. She gives really good and interesting lectures and tries to engage class discussion. There's a lot of readings, supplemental materials but if you find your way to more easily go through it you should be fine. I'd definitely take her again!

The difficulty of this class honestly depends on the TAs. I got stuck with very harsh graders, so understand what their expectations are. Dr. Wagner is great and tries to keep students engaged. She listens to the needs of the class and adjusts her lectures based on that. I'd recommend going to the office hours before exams and the short essays.

analysis.name: Cecilia Schulz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cece is a great teacher who tries to make every topic fun and interesting. She really knows so much about the retail industry so you know you are getting correct information. There are only a few assignments and pop quizzes but overall not too difficult!

I never know what to expect! Every day in class is something completely different. You can tell she puts in a lot of thought and effort in making her lectures interesting and FUNNY! Youll definitely learn a TON about he retail industry in this section. I know I feel more prepared now to head out into the field. Worked hard but definitely worth it.

Just read the chapters 1 day before and make sure you know the vocabulary. There are 4 exams (50 questions each) composing 200 out of the 300 possible points. There is a presentation about a current event article(10pts), a group project(30pts) , 3 pop quizzes (5 points each) and 40 points ( 10 each) of online HW and attending retail bash (5pts)

Great one credit class and great if you're interested in retailing.  There are guest speakers every class and it's easy to get an A.  All you have to do is attend a luncheon (great food), write a paper on one of the speaker's presentation (3-5 pgs) and attend a focus group.

Lectures are enjoyable and workload is minimal. 4 exams that primarily cover the content from the online textbook on Connect. Do not skip the short "lecture extensions" as it is common to be asked about them on an exam. Do the extra credit and you should get an easy A

analysis.name: Hadder Ceballos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was probably the first time I actually enjoyed a Spanish class and it was all because of Hadder! He was hilarious, and always made it a point to get to know everyone in the class. He was also a super fair grader. The only reason I got an A- instead of an A is because I didn't really study for anything in the class, so I'd recommend practicing!

My favorite professor at UF by far. He is very laid back, loves teaching, and is very in tune with his students' lives and interests. He is very understanding if you miss class and will do everything he can to help you learn tough topics. He makes learning Spanish so easy and fun. I looked forward to going to his class every day!

This professor is the best I've had so far. He's so helpful and caring. Spanish can be difficult but he makes it fun and I actually looked forward to going to class. 100% recommend. Thinking about continuing further with Spanish. This prof makes getting an A very doable.

Prof Ceballos is one of the best teachers I've ever had at UF. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He goes out of his way to make class fun! I honestly can't say enough good things about him.
While this class has a major online component with quizzes that werent very enjoyable, its fairly easy overall. Professor Ceballos was great! I loved going to his class.

analysis.name: Douglas Cenzer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cenzer makes this class very easy!  Don't read the book, it will just confuse you.  Cenzer's lectures are very clear and show you exactly how to do the test questions.  At times he loses himself and stands muttering to himself, but this minor flaw is greatly overshadowed by his greatness as a professor.  Take Cenzer for Differential Equations!

He seems to be a nice guy, but he is definitely not a good teacher. His lectures are unorganized and sometimes incomprehensible. Since he is not much of a help, the course becomes unnecessarily more difficult, especially if you are new to the concept of mathematical proofs. Be prepared to grind the textbook. Please avoid him if you can.

He offers little to no explanations; one time he literally said no when I asked him to go over a problem. His lectures are all over the place and impossible to comprehend. I have to rely heavily on the textbook, yet it's not enough and he doesn't offer supplementary learning besides that, classwork, and homework. Avoid him if you can.

if you are going to take this class, you better make sure you have this teacher, he has been one of my favorite teachers so far. VERY VERY clear with his lectures, made this class really easy, 4 exams (final optional), exams questions come exactly from suggested HW problems, knew every student's name, very kind and encouraging!

Seems like a normal guy compared to many in the math department. Nice and helpful person, but one of the worst lecturers. He isn't prepared, mutters to the board, you can't understand him, searches notes frantically, forgets how to do proofs, just stands drumming his fingers on the desk. Each lecture is improvised with him.

analysis.name: Nathalie Ciesco
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would strongly discourage anyone who is not genuinely interested in learning French from taking this course. To those who are, however, I would highly recommend it: Professor Ciesco designed a really efficient online system that covers a lot of material for just one semester. The assignments can get pretty tedious but there's plenty of groupwork

I was scared by the reviews here but this class was great. Yes there is a lot of homework but it certainly did not take up 5 hours of my week. I have a very intense class schedule and this one is the least of my worries. VERY accommodating whenever I emailed her for an extension.  In my opinion, if you have to take a language this is the way to go.

Definitely a lot of HW but it was all very relevant and useful. I feel like I've significantly improved my french language skills. Quizzes are pretty easy if you study and she gives many opportunities for extra credit. Gives half points back on all writing exams.

Definitely my favorite french teacher so far!! Nathalie is lots of fun and very entertaining. She's also VERY willing to help outside of the classroom, and will work with you to help you succeed. She does expect a lot from her students though, so come prepared to class- and be ready to participate! :)

This is a very intensive class, but the professor is very accommodating. You have to do 5 talk abroads and I think 5 group assignments a semester. The homework is very intensive and the tests are difficult, but they always address what was taught in class. You will pretty much be doing homework everyday for the semester, but it's a 5 credit class.

analysis.name: Cindy Dosch
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I've had at UF. If you have the opportunity to take her at a decent time slot, do a favor for your GPA and take FAR 2 with Dosch. Very tough exams, but extremely fair and she prepares you well. Everything you need to know is in her lecture slides and in the assigned homework problems.

Great public speaker. Nice. Funny. Goes above and beyond. Very caring, if you're going through anything personal she will help A LOT. Amazing at explaining content. Very fair. Takes one week to grade. Send you an email if shes concerned about you not passing. Simply deserves every award and raise out there FR

Professor Dosch is the best! I am an accounting major who took the ACG2391 elective for fun, and it was extremely worthwhile. I am actually looking forward to FAR 1 in the future, since she is the professor. If you have a chance, definitely take Exploring Careers in Accounting and get to know Professor Dosch.
A simple Pass/Fail class, definitely not difficult at all, just show up. Dosch is lovely and very charismatic, clearly cares a lot about working with students.

If Cindy Dosch has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has ten fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has only one fan then that is me. If Cindy Dosch has no fans, then that means I am no longer on earth. If the world is against Cindy Dosch, then I am against the world.

analysis.name: Cindy Spence
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was very tough in the beginning and had a harsh learning curve, but Spence made me such a better writer in the end. She will be very tough on you, but listen to everything she says, and you will become such a better writer because of it. I started the class with a 58 and ended with a B, and three papers were published! Go to her for help

This was by far the hardest class I have taken. Spence gives out 2x more assignments than other JOU3101 professors. I recommend Ross. Spence was difficult to communicate with; more than half my class dropped out.

Prof. Spence is the best. I am so happy I had her as my lab instructor. She is so encouraging and really cares about the success of her students. She is also super accessible and willing to help outside of class. She gives great feedback and honestly just wants to see her students do well. Don't let this course intimidate you!
Really tough but you will learn a lot from her. I went from a 44 in the beginning of the class to a B. Do Not Give Up.

analysis.name: Daniel Cicenia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Likes participation. takes random attendance. tests are multiple choice, gives good review though. really listens to students and is open to debates and concerns. really easy class and cool professor. Attend class to get participation points.

If you are a poly sci major or you are going for the Political Campaigning Certificate, TAKE THIS CLASS! There is no easier class at UF. All the lectures are on powerpoints that he emails you. He takes random attendance. All his tests, including the midterm, he reviews the class before. In his reviews he practically gives you the answers! Take it!

Boring teacher but easy class and very helpful.  Gives random attendance so you should go to class.  Before every test he gives a review and basically tells you every question that will be on the test as well as the essay question, so it is very easy to do well if you just study for 15 minutes.  Definitely recommend taking this teacher!!!!

He's a really nice guy, but a bit of a pushover so his class is REALLY easy. Go to reviews before the tests - he'll pretty much give you the answers. If you participate in class and go to his office hours, he'll go easy on you when grading your papers.
Take him! you learn a lot and if you put in a little effort you can get an A. He does go over everything before the exam. Takes random attendance so go.

analysis.name: Cindy Prins

review_highlights.comment: Course was hybrid, with lectures recorded online and discussions in class once a week. It's an interesting course and I've come to like it. The book is a must because the lectures are based on the book. It's very helpful in clarifying concepts because the lectures do not cover everything.

Good class, first half was great but second half was not my favorite. Tests are ambiguous and difficult. Study hard; be ready for anything and give as much detail on free response questions (70-90% of questions are free response on exams).
Dr. Prins is an incredible teacher! Epidemiology is awesome to begin with, but she mak
Great teacher! She is very nice and her lecture notes are mostly from the textbook.
Good epidemiology professor. Helpful, and cute too.  Overall satisfactory.

analysis.name: Cindi Figueroa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Keeps my interest and brings clinical life experiences to her teachings. Highly recommended if interested in becoming an Adult Nurse Practitioner at UF in the College of Nursing. She is a faculty who truly listens & understands her students! Glad to have Dr Figueroa-Haas as my advisor & looking forward to continuing in this program. BSN-DNP student

It was a difficult & disruptive class for Dr Haas to teach, but she did the best she could with what she had to deal with..a new unprepared,cooker,lab professor in 3067L,who did not cover the required objectives for her course and the multitude of rude, immature students that kept talking while Haas lectured. Hands up to Dr Haas for getting us out!

Dr Haas is an exciting, enthusiasic,awesome professor that keeps your attention at ALL times during lectures. I've learned so much from her...love the stories! It's obvious that she loves her students, faculty & job. I hope to be just like her one day! Thank you for being such a great role model for me. I will never forget you. YOU ROCK MY WORLD!

I learned so very much from Dr Haas, my experence on the Unit was unbelievable & life long rewarding. I hope Dr Haas nevers leaves UF/CON...she is such an asset to the college. She is so smart, caring & fair to all her students. You can tell she loves teaching & working with us. Thank you Dr Haas for working so hard with us, We ALL love you!
Dr. Haas is super helpful and enthusiastic about everything! She makes the class super fun and interesting. Awesome professor! =]

analysis.name: Christopher Dutton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The best of all the gen biology professors I have had! His lectures kept me very attentive, I learned a lot each class, and he provides so many different resources for studying and remembering the material. I'm really glad I got to have him as my last gen bio professor. I actually laughed during lecture more than a few times :) 100% recommend!

Dr. Dutton is one of the greatest lecturers at the UF. He explains things concise and clearly. He teaches the ecology unit and made it interesting to learn. He usually finishes up lectures earlier and gives the slides out with speaker notes. He was the best out of the three bio professors for this semester. Also gives a little extra credit.

Dr. Sutton is truly amazing. He is so well-spoken and has like the most zen voice ever. He is very understanding in his lectures, offers lots of opportunities for extra credit, and made coming to class enjoyable. He is a super nice guy and his content is not too hard for comprehension.

I LOVE DR DUTTON!!! He genuinely cares about his students and their success in his section of BSC2011. His lectures are genuinely interesting and easy to understand and he provides an great amount of materials to prepare for the exam.

THE BEST BIO 2 PROF. Very kind and warm to students, its apparent he is rooting for all of our success. Highest exam average of the three. Lectures are very direct (he emphasizes which content to lock in) and not confusing. Attendance not mandatory because clicker Qs are included in slide PDFs, but he guides the class to the correct answer in class

analysis.name: Chamila Gamage
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: explains concepts very clearly. her lectures are very engaging, and they were never boring in my opinion. Was a very sweet prof and she was a great teacher. If you had any questions she would always answer them. Was in the honors section and when we did practice problems she would circle around the room to see our work and if we were doing it right or if we had questions and she would guide us accordingly. Pay attention to her reviews for exams.

I took the honors section of calc 1 and had a great experience. She provides so many resources and had efficient, effective, and well structured lectures. the exams were all very fair and easy to prepare for. strongly recommend, she definitely has a very deep understanding of mathematics and is an excellent educator.

Took her for Calc 1, and she's a good instructor. Answers questions in class, and would circle around whenever we'd do practice questions. Gives lots of resources to study for exams, which I found so helpful. She really shines during office hours, though, so definitely go to those even if you're retaking the credit!

She was really nice and cared about all the students. I would watch Dr Stresses lectures for more help. Definitely get StudyEdge because it teaches you in a different way so can understand the material better and extra practice is always good. Do all old practice exams before tests because test is almost exactly like practice exams!

analysis.name: Lynne Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
